item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox can't catch a break as Mickey Gasper pulled vs. Cubs amid injury fears
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli

item.content:encoded:
Mickey Gasper stepped up to the plate in the fifth inning on a windy day in Boston and worked the count full. He gave an aggressive swing on the sixth pitch he saw for a strikeout with two runners on base, but that isn't the worst of it.
Gasper winced after his big swing. On his walk back to the Boston Red Sox's dugout, he flexed his arm and bent his elbow. He pressed his bicep, looking for an issue. A trainer examined him in the dugout before he went down the tunnel and left the game. Connor Wong replaced Gasper behind the dish.
Gasper left the game with biceps discomfort, according to multiple sources including Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. That's a vague diagnosis, but any further injuries are an ugly sign for the Sox. Willson Contreras has been sidelined since he was hit in the hand by a pitch on September 17, just four games after he returned from the injured list with a hamstring injury. The first baseman isn't confident he'll be available for the Wild Card round, and Boston needs all the offensive help it can get without him.
Gasper has cooled down lately, but he's recently off an incredible stint at the plate in the second half of August. He slashed .400/.571/1.100 with three doubles, six home runs and 10 RBI over 12 games last month.
Mickey Gasper pulled from first game of Cubs-Red Sox doubleheader with apparent arm injury following big swing
Even if Gasper has slowed down offensively, he's still proven a home run threat since his red-hot month. He's hit four homers in September, one as recently as September 22, while slashing .196/.328/.451.
If Gasper can't return to play this season, Boston has a few replacement options with the "stay ready" squad in Fort Myers. Romy Gonzalez was scorching with the WooSox in September to the tune of a .371/.410/.571 slash line. Braiden Ward and Tsung-Che Cheng are also there, but Gonzalez is the best pick given his MLB experience and recent heater. He also crushes lefties and the New York Yankees are sure to throw at least two the Red Sox's way during the Wild Card round.
Top prospect Franklin Arias is also part of the Fort Myers squad and he was in Boston on the night of September 24. The shortstop posted a breakout season between Double-A and Triple-A with a .323/.400/.557 28 doubles and 25 home runs over 117 games. The Red Sox have avoided calling Arias up this year when infield injuries cropped up, and they could be reluctant to do so now, in the biggest moment they've had all season.
A healthy Gasper would be a valuable bench option in the postseason, especially now that he's found his home run swing. Instead, the Red Sox have possibly been dealt another injury to work around at the worst possible time.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the final few games of the regular season, with the postseason starting up next week.
Boston has clinched a playoff spot, and they will be a wild-card team this season. The Red Sox battled back from a very slow start to the season, putting together a massive rally in the middle of the year.
The goal is to win a World Series title, and they seem to have a decent shot at getting it done. But while the players are focused on the play on the field, the front office also has its sights set on the upcoming offseason.
Even with the impending lockout likely coming to baseball, teams all over the league could try to maneuver rosters before it happens. For the Red Sox, they do have a key free agent hitting the market in ace Sonny Gray.
The veteran right-hander has been excellent for the Red Sox this year, firing a 2.79 ERA over 29 innings. Gray has helped establish the Red Sox rotation as one of the best in baseball, and he has been a major reason why the team has made the playoffs.
The right-hander has a mutual option for next season, but there has also been some retirement talk. However, given how strong of a year he has seen, the right-hander may postpone that idea, looking to land one last big contract.
Boston would surely want him back, but that all remains to be seen. But his free agency will be something to watch for the Red Sox and other potentially interested teams out there.
Sonny Gray Gets Major Free Agency Prediction
MLB analyst
“It sounds like everything is on the table for the 36-year-old. Per Mass Live’s Chris Cotillo, Gray could fetch a similar deal to the three-year, $75 million deal Nathan Eovaldi inked with the Texas Rangers two years back. But Cotillo also noted that Gray relayed in a recent interview with The Boston Globe he would retire “in a heartbeat” if his family indicated any desire for him to do so.
“Only Gray knows what he’s thinking, and since he doesn’t need to make a decision right now, it’s very possible even if he isn’t sure. If he wants to keep playing, though, he has clearly set himself up to strike it rich in free agency,” Buckley wrote.
Should Red Sox Resign Sonny Gray?
Given how dominant Gray has been, the Red Sox should try to sign him to a new deal. Even if this would be just for another year or two, having Gray around would help Boston heading into next season.
Gray has seen a lot of success with the Red Sox, and the team is a contender, so the two sides may come together. But for now, the focus will be on trying to win the World Series, with free agency in the back of everyone’s mind.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have already clinched a spot in the MLB playoffs and will wrap up the 2026 regular season across Friday and Saturday against the Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park.
For Boston, they’re coming off a 1-0 loss to the Cleveland Guardians on Thursday night, a game in which they decided to give star outfielder Roman Anthony the night off. He didn’t make any pinch-hit appearances during the contest.
Red Sox Announce Anthony Decision
Now, as they gear up for an afternoon game against the Cubs, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy has elected to put Anthony back into the lineup in his normal role.
He’ll bat leadoff and get the start in left field, while Mickey Gasper bats second and gets the start behind the plate for southpaw Alec Gamboa, who will start Game 1 of the doubleheader.
Here’s the full Red Sox lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Red Sox Game 1 9/25 R. Anthony LF M. Gasper C A. Rutschman DH W. Abreu RF C. Durbin 3B N. Sogard 2B J. Duran CF A. Monasterio 1B I. Kiner-Falefa SS A. Gamboa SP.”
Red Sox Game 1 9/25
R. Anthony LF
M. Gasper C
A. Rutschman DH
W. Abreu RF
C. Durbin 3B
N. Sogard 2B
J. Duran CF
A. Monasterio 1B
I. Kiner-Falefa SS
A. Gamboa SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 25, 2026
Anthony’s 2026 Season
It’s been a frustrating year two for Anthony, who is the current centerpiece of the Red Sox franchise.
He’s battled a wrist injury for the majority of the season, and while he’s moving back into form over the month of September, he’s appeared in just 52 games in 2026. He’s hitting .235 across 204 at-bats with 48 hits, five home runs, and 15 RBIs.
Looking at the Red Sox
Boston enters Friday’s doubleheader holding an 85-74 overall record. They remain just one win or a Chicago White Sox loss away from clinching the second Wild Card spot, which would match them up against the New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series.
The worst the Red Sox could fall is the third Wild Card seed. In that case, they’d play the No. 3 overall division winner in the AL.

item.content:encoded:
When the Chicago Cubs' lineup dropped on Friday morning, fans were greeted with quite the surprise.
Alex Bregman is back in his normal spot against a left-handed hitter, batting third in the order. While both Bregman and Craig Counsell implied that he could be back before the Wild Card round, no one would have blamed either party if that didn't come to fruition.
Bregman is only five days removed from a scary hospital visit. He was hit in the face with a foul ball during the Cubs' matchup with the Cincinnati Reds. Immediately grabbing at his face in pain and bleeding, Chicago's staff rushed him off the field and sent him for further testing. Bregman would later share images that revealed a black eye and swollen face. Testing revealed that he suffered multiple facial fractures.
Nevertheless, upon his return to Wrigley Field for the team's matchup with the Marlins, Bregman shared that he planned to get back in the batter's box sooner rather than later. And Counsell has now granted him that opportunity.
The Cubs will play Bregman at DH, meaning Matt Shaw will hold down the fort at third base. We've also seen Pedro Ramirez in that spot during Bregman's absence. All things considered, it will be interesting to see how the Cubs continue to handle the position. Keeping the still-healing Bregman off the field may be in his best interest, but there is also no ignoring the stakes.
Cubs Offense Needs a Bregman Boost
The Chicago Cubs offense was reminded of how much they need Alex Bregman's bat this week.
The Cubs' series with the Marlins left a lot to be desired. They scored a mere 2 runs in each of the three games, which included their playoff clincher on Thursday afternoon. As exciting as the moment was for the organization, it was hard to feel great about where the group was trending.
Obviously, you don't want to put too much pressure on Bregman in his return. It's already miraculous enough that he's back in the lineup. However, he has undoubtedly been the Cubs' second-best hitter in the second half of the season. The player the organization thought they were signing to a five-year deal has shown up in full force, providing a thrilling one-two punch with NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong.
Bregman is slashing .289/.374/.640 in his last month. This includes hitting double-digit home runs with a whopping 28 RBIs. He's also struck out only 13 times to 12 walks. To be sure, he has cooled off a bit over his last seven games, but the overall production still speaks for itself.
The Cubs may have a Wild Card slot locked in, but they still have a ton to play for over these next two days. The San Diego Padres hold a one-game lead for home-field advantage after picking up another win over the Dodgers on Thursday night. With how scorching hot they have been, Chicago would adore a sweep of the Red Sox.
The Phillies are also only one game behind tying the Cubbies, which remains something to monitor. Nevertheless, the good news remains that Chicago has the tiebreaker over each of their Wild Card competitors. In other words, even if they even the tally with San Diego, they will get another series at Wrigley Field.
A Bregman return will now give the Cubs their full group for one last push. Not to mention, regardless of what happens, it should help him get into a rhyhtm before the Wild Card battle starts up.
Sign up for our free newsletter to stay up-to-date with all things Chicago Cubs.
Elias Schuster is a sports journalist and content creator from the northern suburbs of Chicago. A graduate from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, he has covered the Bulls since 2019-20, previously serving as the editor of BN Bulls at Bleacher Nation, where he also covered the Cubs. He has been the Publisher for Bulls On SI since December of 2025-26 and has managed both the Cubs and White Sox in 2026. When he isn't typing away, Elias loves strolling the streets of Chicago for the best cozy bar or restaurant with his wife and far-too-energetic Jack Russell Terrier.

item.content:encoded:
The Cubs got a lift ahead of their doubleheader against the Red Sox at Fenway on Friday. Third baseman Alex Bregman was in the starting lineup and hitting third for Chicago in Game 1.
Bregman was struck on the left side of the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch on Sunday and was examined at a local hospital in Cincinnati. He has seen multiple specialists and received as good of news as could be expected under the circumstances. No surgery was required and Bregman does not have any vision or concussion issues.
Following a slow start to the season, Bregman has been one of baseball’s top hitters since the All-Star break (.978 OPS in 59 games), while playing Gold Glove-caliber defense at third.

item.content:encoded:
Let’s play two!
With a nor’easter rolling into the area, the Cubs and Red Sox are looking to get ahead of the weather by playing a doubleheader Friday. The first game, with a 1:05 p.m. start, was originally Sunday’s contest. The teams will suit up again for a 5:35 p.m. first pitch in the nightcap — moved up slightly from its original 7:10 p.m. start, then again Thursday morning from a 6:05 start.
The Red Sox’ offense is still trying to find its form heading into October. Boston has lost four of five and has not scored more than two runs in any game during that stretch.
The Red Sox managed just two singles in Thursday’s 1-0 loss to the Guardians. In Wednesday’s 1-0 win, Andruw Monasterio snapped an 0-for-21 skid with an RBI single.
“Over these next three games, if you see some [offense] bust out, that would be great,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said. “We did have some quality plate appearances from certain guys, which was good to see.”
Willson Contreras sat out his sixth consecutive game. Contreras was hit in the right hand by a pitch a week ago, and said he couldn’t swing a bat the past two days. Tracy hopes to have Contreras back for postseason play when it begins Tuesday, but the first baseman gave a disappointing update about his condition.
“It’s really frustrating when you’re doing the best you can do, you’re expecting to heal faster and it doesn’t happen,” he said.
Alec Gamboa gets the nod for the Red Sox in the opener, followed by Brayan Bello in the second game. Gamboa, who has never faced the Cubs, owns a 0.50 ERA in his past 13 outings.
The Cubs are expected to start Clay Holmes and David Peterson — both midseason acquisitions from the Mets — in the Friday games.
Here’s a preview for this afternoon’s contest.
Lineups
This file will be updated with Game 2 lineups
CUBS (88-71): Crow-Armstrong CF, Suzuki RF, Bregman DH, Taylor LF, Hoerner 2B, Shaw 3B, Busch 1B, Swanson SS, Amaya C
Game 1 Pitching: RHP Clay Holmes (6-8, 3.25 ERA)
Game 2 Pitching: LHP David Peterson (9-8, 4.96 ERA)
RED SOX (85-74): Anthony LF, Gasper C, Rutschman DH, Abreu RF, Durbin 3B, Sogard 2B, Duran CF, Monasterio 1B, Kiner-Falefa SS
Game 1 Pitching: LHP Alec Gamboa (1-0, 1.16 ERA)
Game 2 Pitching: RHP Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.49 ERA)
Game 1 time: 1:05 p.m.
Game 2 time: 5:35 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Cubs vs. Gamboa: Has not faced any Cubs batters
Red Sox vs. Holmes: Wilyer Abreu 2-5, Willson Contreras 5-11, Jarren Duran 0-6, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 3-7, Ceddanne Rafaela 0-3, Adley Rutschman 2-4, Nick Sogard 0-2, Trevor Story 1-8, Connor Wong 1-3
Stat of the day: The Red Sox own a 39-39 record at home this season.
Notes: The Cubs downed the Marlins, 2-1, Thursday afternoon to secure their second straight postseason berth. ... Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh 40-homer, 40-steal player in major league history after stealing second base in the first inning. Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite, has 45 homers and 40 steals. ... The Cubs occupy the second NL wild-card spot. Chicago is a game behind the Padres and one game up on the Phillies. The top wild-card team hosts through the opening round of the playoffs.
Cam Kerry can be reached at cam.kerry@globe.com.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox begin the postseason on Tuesday and have scored just 5 runs over the last 5 games. In other words, now would be a great time for the team's best offensive contributor to return to a lineup that desperately needs a spark. But unless a miracle happens over the weekend, things aren't looking good. Willson Contreras took batting practice on Tuesday, only for his hand injury to worsen in the subsequent days. He's still struggling to grip a bat and admitted to tearing up out of frustration. "I'm doing everything that I can to come back and play with the boys and be there with the boys," he said. "But sometimes you have to listen to your body." (Tim Healey, Boston Globe)
At least Ceddanne Rafaela has returned. He should be able to give a little lift for the lineup, though he does present a conundrum for Chad Tracy, as the Sox now have too many outfielders and DHs to fit into the lineup at once. With Roman Anthony, Rafalea, and Wilyer Abreu essentially locked into starting spots, Tracy has to decide whether to prioritize Duran's glove and legs over the platoon DH production of Mickey Gasper and Jahmai Jones. (Sean McAdam, MassLive)
And all of this is occuring against the backdrop of this weekend's storm. And if you think we're done dealing with that now that MLB has moved Sunday's game to today, we're not. There is still a possibility that one or more of this weekend's games is moved to Tropicana Field in St. Pete. (Conor Ryan, Boston.com)
With the depressing news about Contreras, the team could probably use a pep talk. If so, Pedro Martinez — as someone who still believed in this team in the darkness of May — is available. "I just feel good about approaching the Yankees this time around. And [the Red Sox] are young, yes. We don't have the highest expectations about them, but man, for some reason, I just feel so positive," said the right arm of God. "I just feel so excited that this young group of guys that we have out there are able to do something special. I don't see anything wrong with these kids, and I don't see why they shouldn't give everybody knuckles. Not just the Yankees, but everybody." (Ian Browne, MLB.com)
If the Sox are going to give everybody knuckles, then Ranger Suarez is probably going to be a part of it. The offseason signing has an outstanding postseason resume, and his final 2026 stats are more or less in line with the numbers he'd been putting up in Philadelphia, even if he sounds slightly disappointed in his performance. "Obviously I think I could have done better," he said of his season. "But I was happy I was able to finish the season strong." (Peter Abraham, Boston Globe)

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead at the trade deadline, but he fractured his wrist in his first game with the team.
Mead avoided surgery, but he is in a race against the clock if he wants to return this season. Mead has been progressing toward a return and is planning to take a major step on Friday.
"Curtis Mead (left wrist fracture) plans to take another step forward Friday by taking batting practice off of a machine," reported The Boston Globe's Tim Healey. "He will head to Fort Myers with Crochet and potentially hit against him on Saturday, he said. He is not ruled out for the first round of the playoffs beginning Tuesday, but that deadline might be too soon."
Mead was having a career year before his injury, and getting that version of him in the lineup could be huge for the Red Sox's offense. However, if he's not at 100%, it may not be the best idea for the Red Sox to stick him in the lineup at second base in the most important series of the year.
Mead was slashing .253/.353/.498 with 17 home runs before he went down. The Red Sox's options at second base in the postseason include Andruw Monasterio, Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Nick Sogard. However, if Willson Contreras is unable to play due to his hand injury, Sogard will likely draw the starts at first base.
If Contreras can't play, Mead's presence in the lineup may become more important. The Red Sox's offense has been scuffling lately, and Mead could provide a boost in October.

item.title: [Over the Monster] Chad Tracy made history with the Red Sox… and followed in his father’s footsteps
item.dc:creator: Tim Crowley

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox are officially playoff bound thanks to a historic turnaround from a slow start to the season and a redirection under interim and now full-time manager Chad Tracy. The fact that Tracy made history – and even more impressively family history – is still pretty mind-boggling, even though I wrote about it on May 1.
The blueprint and context was there as Chad’s father, Jim Tracy, took over as the manager of the Rockies in May 2009 after Colorado fired Clint Hurdle. The Rockies took off immediately with a 21-7 record in June on the way to a franchise-record 92 wins and a playoff berth. Tracy won National League Manager of the Year in a magical season at Coors Field.
Several outlets discussed this history when Tracy took over from the 10-17 start to the season that cost Alex Cora his job. It didn’t change right away for Boston with a 13-14 record in June before that stunning 32-5 run that vaulted the Red Sox back into playoff contention. And now here we are. Father and son each taking over as interim skippers and guiding their respective teams to the postseason after sub-.500 starts. Here’s an excerpt from the story we published the time:
Jim Tracy showed the impact of the right in-season switch. Can his son get another team to the playoffs 17 years later?
The stories would write themselves in one of the more fascinating intertwingings in recent baseball history.
Ultimately, these situations aren’t totally the same and the Red Sox roster has arguably more to overcome than Colorado did.
“I think you can’t paint every situation with the same brush,” (Dan) O’Dowd commented while discussing the differences, including the initial decisions with Hurdle in Colorado and Cora in Boston.
For Chad Tracy in the meantime, however, the ex-Colorado executive believes in the Red Sox interim given the baseball path his family set for him to follow one way or another.
The paths and personnel to make both postseasons happen are noticeably different. The Red Sox have now clinched back-to-back playoff berths, but the expectations of how far they’d go in October were different. Colorado struggled early, but that team had also been to the World Series just two years prior and still had a star-studded roster. Not to say the Red Sox didn’t have big names, but Roman Anthony and Garrett Crochet did spend most of 2026 on the shelf with injuries.
Regardless, the Red Sox got the best possible scenario out of their managerial change that will forever link Jim and Chad Tracy even deeper than the already deep father-son relationship.
In October 2009, the Rockies fell to the eventual National League champion Philadelphia Phillies in the National League Division Series. With Chad Tracy at the helm, how far will the Red Sox go this postseason?

Wilyer Abreu and his Boston Red Sox will take on the Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park, on Friday, Sept. 25 at 1:05 p.m. ET. Abreu has +520 odds to hit a home run as of Friday morning.
What It Means
Abreu is hitting for a .251 BA, .330 OBP and .451 SLG with a 20.6% strikeout rate and a 10.5% walk rate. His OPS is .781 and he has scored 81 runs. In 669 plate appearances, he has hit 24 home runs and driven in 74 runs. Abreu has recorded eight steals on 12 attempts. In his previous game he had a hitless showing (0 for 4) against the Guardians.
The Cubs are sending Clay Holmes (6-8) to make his 18th start of the season. He is 6-8 with a 3.25 ERA and 75 strikeouts through 97 2/3 innings pitched.
NOTE: Odds are subject to change. Please check FanDuel Sportsbook for the most up-to-date betting markets.

item.title: [Audacy] Why Willson Contreras' hand means so much to the Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Rob Bradford
item.description: There was the 1-0 loss to the Guardians. There were the weather updates that might very well have the Red Sox and Cubs playing somewhere other than Fenway Park this weekend. And there was Ceddanne Rafaela's return from his hamstring scare. But when it came to news that mattered for the Red Sox, it was hard to top what Willson Contreras said after this latest defeat. The first baseman's bruised right hand evidently does not seem to be cooperating when it comes to postseason readiness. "I mean, it
item.content:encoded:
There was the 1-0 loss to the Guardians. There were the weather updates that might very well have the Red Sox and Cubs playing somewhere other than Fenway Park this weekend. And there was Ceddanne Rafaela's return from his hamstring scare.
But when it came to news that mattered for the Red Sox, it was hard to top what Willson Contreras said after this latest defeat.
The first baseman's bruised right hand evidently does not seem to be cooperating when it comes to postseason readiness.
"I mean, it's really concerning,” Contreras said. “But at the same time, I'm putting all my effort -- and everything I can do, I'm doing it. I don't know what else to say. I’m working hard with the trainers; the hand is slowly getting better. But I haven’t been able to swing the last two days. I’ll be honest with the team. I know Tuesday is a really important game. It's a really important series, and I'll be completely honest with the team.”
Contreras added, "It's frustrating, if I’m being honest. I was hoping to swing today, and I couldn't swing. I came into my locker just tearing up because that's what we play for. We play to play in October, and it's really frustrating when we're doing the best you can do and you're expecting to heal faster and that doesn't happen."
It appeared as though Contreras was headed in the right direction, taking an exorbitant amount of swings prior to Tuesday's game, both on the Fenway field and underneath with the Trajekt pitching machine. But the results from the exercise were not positive, with the righty hitter unable to replicate any sort of batting practice over the last couple of days.
There is still time for Contreras, with the Red Sox's first wild-card game on Tuesday. But his original plan to use the weekend games against the Cubs as a tune-up for the playoffs seems extremely unlikely.
Why is this such a big deal? It's because of the skill-set Contreras carries, one that the Red Sox seem starved for heading into the postseason.
All good postseason runs are usually built on the back of top-of-the-order power, with opponents needing to navigate their way through a team's alpha batters. Hitting home runs, in particular, is usually a top priority. The Blue Jays and Dodgers lived that life a year ago, as did the Yankees and Los Angeles the year before. You know who didn't? The 2025 Red Sox during their three wild-card games at Yankee Stadium.
Trevor Story's solo homer in Game 2 of last season's playoff showdown with the Yankees marked the only time a Red Sox player cleared the fences. It was a deficiency that was difficult to ignore.
It was why Craig Breslow proclaimed early in the offseason that his team needed more power. It was the reason acquiring Curtis Mead became a priority heading into the trade deadline. And it is why Contreras, who leads the Red Sox with 27 homers, has been so important. (The Red Sox are 18-8 when Contreras hits at least one homer.)
While this Red Sox team has taught us that things can turn in a hurry, the way the Sox's offense has been trending isn't good. In the last five games, the Sox have hit only two home runs. And in September, Chad Tracy's team has the second-lowest batting average and OPS in baseball, while scoring the fewest runs (13 fewer than the next-worst).
There are potential solutions to the Red Sox's postseason power problem, including Roman Anthony (who is tied with Mickey Gasper for the team lead in homers for September with four), Adley Rutschman, Story, Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu, who has two home runs since Aug. 16.
But Contreras has always been the constant ... until now.
“When it hurts, it hurts. Especially when it's the top hand,” Contreras said. “If it was the bottom hand, I could swing with the right hand, but when it's the right hand, my right hand just feels weaker until I just let the bat go. It's not a good sign. ... Again, I'm doing everything that I can to come back and play with the boys and be there with the boys. But sometimes you have to listen to your body, and I'm listening to the trainers and doing everything that they ask me to do, and [it's] just one of those things that I can't control."

item.title: [heavy.com] Boston Red Sox Get Curtis Mead News Ahead of Wild Card Series
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals on July 26. He arrived riding one of the best stretches of his career, slashing .367/.465/.650 with three home runs over 16 games in July. The right-handed bat Boston needed for a playoff push had landed. Three days later, a left wrist fracture put him on the injured list. Mead has not played since. The Red Sox gave up left-hander Connelly Early to get him, and two months later, they are still waiting to see what their midseas
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals on July 26. He arrived riding one of the best stretches of his career, slashing .367/.465/.650 with three home runs over 16 games in July. The right-handed bat Boston needed for a playoff push had landed.
Three days later, a left wrist fracture put him on the injured list.
Mead has not played since. The Red Sox gave up left-hander Connelly Early to get him, and two months later, they are still waiting to see what their midseason investment looks like when it matters most. That wait may be close to ending.
Mead Takes Next Step Toward Return
Mead plans to hit off a pitching machine on Friday, per Tim Healey of the Boston Globe.
From there, Mead heads to Fort Myers alongside Garrett Crochet, who is working his way back from a left shoulder injury. Saturday could bring a live BP session against Crochet, which would represent a significant jump from machine work in the span of 24 hours.
Mead has not officially been ruled out for the Wild Card Series. But the timeline remains tight. Going from no game action since late July to postseason at-bats would be an aggressive return, even for a player eager to contribute. Healey noted the deadline might be too soon.
What Mead Brought This Season
The Red Sox targeted Mead for a reason. His .253 average across the full season tells only part of the story. The Australian slugged .500 and posted an .851 OPS through 87 games with Washington, ranking 10th among qualified right-handed hitters in slugging and 12th in OPS at the time of the deal.
He provided positional flexibility at second base, third base, and first base. Boston slotted him at second upon arrival, keeping Caleb Durbin at third. The plan was to add a middle-of-the-order presence with pop for the stretch run.
The wrist fracture erased all of it. Mead went from a deadline acquisition to a recovery project overnight.
What it Means for the Red Sox
The Fort Myers trip is the checkpoint that matters. If Mead handles machine BP on Friday and responds well against live pitching on Saturday, the conversation about his Wild Card roster spot becomes real. If the wrist is not ready, the Red Sox head into October without a bat they specifically traded for this moment.
Mead’s 17 home runs and 48 RBI represent production that does not sit on the bench easily. Getting him back would add a right-handed power threat the lineup currently lacks.
The deadline might be too soon. But Mead is pushing toward it.
Final Word for the Red Sox
Curtis Mead has spent almost all of his time in Boston on the injured list.
The wrist fracture stole the stretch run. Now the postseason is days away, and he is heading south to find out whether his body will cooperate.
The fact that he has not been ruled out says something about where this is trending. Saturday’s live BP will tell the rest.

item.title: [si.com] Willson Contreras Update Puts Red Sox’s Playoff Run in Peril
item.dc:creator: Jackson Roberts; Unknown
item.description: The Boston Red Sox’s game on Thursday didn’t mean much. But after a 1-0 loss to the Cleveland Guardians, the fan base got a much worse gut punch. All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras, who has been Boston’s best hitter all season, has been working to return from a hand injury sustained on a wild pitch last Thursday. He was seen taking batting practice on the field earlier this week at Fenway Park, but evidently, he’s not feeling close to 100%. Contreras told the media on Thursday night that h
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox’s game on Thursday didn’t mean much. But after a 1-0 loss to the Cleveland Guardians, the fan base got a much worse gut punch.
All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras, who has been Boston’s best hitter all season, has been working to return from a hand injury sustained on a wild pitch last Thursday. He was seen taking batting practice on the field earlier this week at Fenway Park, but evidently, he’s not feeling close to 100%.
Contreras told the media on Thursday night that he was unable to swing on Wednesday or Thursday due to the slow recovery he had after Tuesday’s batting practice session. With only five days until the playoffs begin, that leaves the Red Sox working against the clock.
Contreras doesn’t sound optimistic about playoffs
Worst of all, Contreras’ language postgame made it seem as if he was already anticipating that he wouldn’t be able to take the field on Tuesday, likely in the Bronx against the arch-rival New York Yankees.
"I mean it's frustrating, being honest. I was hoping to swing today. Couldn't swing, I came into my locker, I was tearing up. I'm being honest," Contreras said, via Michael Hurley of NBC Sports Boston. "Because that's what we play for. We play to play in October … and it's really frustrating when you're doing the best you can do and you're expecting to heal faster and that doesn't happen."
Anything can happen in a three-game series, but the Red Sox would be at a serious disadvantage without Contreras, their team leader in most offensive categories. It makes the situation all the more painful that Contreras had just worked his way back from a stint on the injured list for a hamstring issue, which he’d played through for most of the season.
If Contreras isn’t able to go, the Red Sox have their pick between Nick Sogard and Mickey Gasper at first base on the current roster, and there might be a spot for Romy Gonzalez to return from Triple-A to fill a void against left-handed pitching at the position. All of those guys are capable of helping out, but none have the consistency or power potential of Contreras.
It’s a developing story, but Thursday was a tough pill to swallow for the Red Sox and their fans. All Contreras can do is keep working, and as long as he’s out, the Red Sox have to do all in their power to stave off elimination and earn him more games to play.
Jackson Roberts is a former Division III All-Region DH who now writes and talks about sports for a living. A Bay Area native and a graduate of Swarthmore College and the Newhouse School at Syracuse University, Jackson makes his home in North Jersey. He grew up rooting for the Red Sox, Patriots, and Warriors, and he recently added the Devils to his sports fandom mosaic. item.title: [heraldglobe.com] MLB roundup: White Sox, Guardians, Cubs, Padres wrap up playoff berths
item.description:
Field Level Media
25 Sep 2026, 12:10 GMT+10
(Photo credit: William Purnell) Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth. Chicago is back in the postseason for the first time since 2021 after enduring three straight 100-loss seasons. Fueled by an early barrage against Royals right-hand
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

25 Sep 2026, 12:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: William Purnell)
Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth.
Chicago is back in the postseason for the first time since 2021 after enduring three straight 100-loss seasons.
Fueled by an early barrage against Royals right-hander Randy Dobnak, the White Sox remained a game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland. Whichever one of those two teams fails to win the division will wind up as the third AL wild-card team.
Sandlin (3-2) yielded one run and five hits. Dobnak (3-5) allowed six runs (four earned) and six hits in 1 1/3 innings.
Guardians 1, Red Sox 0
Angel Martinez's second-inning home run was all visiting Cleveland needed for a win over Boston to clinch its third consecutive playoff berth.
Joey Cantillo (11-9) dominated for five shutout innings as the Guardians' bulk reliever, yielding one hit. Hunter Gaddis, Erik Sabrowski and Cade Smith allowed a combined one hit over the final three innings to help Cleveland win its seventh game in the last eight.
The playoff-bound Red Sox fell for the fourth time in five games despite getting five innings of one-run ball from Ranger Suarez (8-5).
Cubs 2, Marlins 1
Nico Hoerner ripped a go-ahead RBI single in the sixth and Matthew Boyd tossed seven strong innings, helping host Chicago clinch a playoff berth with a victory over Miami.
Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong walked to lead off the first inning and promptly stole second base to become the seventh player in major league history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in a single season.
Seiya Suzuki belted a solo homer in the fifth inning to highlight his two-hit performance for the Cubs, who salvaged the finale of their three-game series with Miami. Chicago sits in the second NL wild-card spot, one game behind San Diego.
Padres 4, Dodgers 2
Dustin Harris drove in the go-ahead run in the sixth inning as visiting San Diego beat Los Angeles to clinch a playoff spot for a franchise-record third consecutive season.
Yuki Matsui (4-1) earned the win with a scoreless inning, and Mason Miller gave up a run with two outs in the ninth before securing his 38th save. Ethan Salas and Fernando Tatis Jr. each had two hits and an RBI for the Padres.
Tyler Glasnow (5-2) fanned a season-high 11 but allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings for the Dodgers, who secured a first-round playoff bye thanks to the Atlanta Braves' loss on Thursday. Shohei Ohtani went 2-for-5 with an RBI double.
Brewers 5, Phillies 1
Jake Bauers' RBI single in the eighth inning plated the go-ahead run for Milwaukee, which reached the 100-win mark for the first time in franchise history with a win at Philadelphia. When the Dodgers fell to the Padres later, the Brewers clinched the top record in the major leagues.
Bauers, who went 2-for-5, singled up the middle, allowing Jackson Chourio to score from second, giving the Brewers (100-59) a 2-1 lead and starting a three-run frame.
Philadelphia remains in an NL wild-card spot, but the Phillies could not drop their magic number to clinch from two. Phillies starter Andrew Painter threw six innings of one-run ball, fanning eight. Bryce Harper went 2-for-4 with an RBI.
Diamondbacks 12, Rockies 8
Gabriel Moreno and Nolan Arenado homered in a six-run first inning and surging Arizona beat Colorado in Denver to continue its drive for a wild-card berth.
James McCann also went deep for Arizona, which moved within two games of Philadelphia for the third and final NL playoff berth. Arizona finishes the regular season in San Diego while the Phillies host Tampa Bay this weekend.
Cole Carrigg homered among his four hits, Kyle Karros and Zac Veen also went deep and had two hits for Colorado, which finished with 17 hits.
Rangers 3, Mets 1
Kumar Rocker pitched five solid innings for Texas, which salvaged the finale of a three-game series against New York in Arlington, Texas.
Josh Jung (3-for-3) hit a two-run homer in the first and Corey Seager went deep in the sixth for the Rangers, who remain tied with Houston for first place in the American League West. Rocker (6-11) allowed one run on three hits. Jordan Montgomery recorded his first save of the season.
Mets starter Zac Thornton (5-6) yielded two runs on four hits over five innings. Brett Baty extended his on-base streak to 17 games.
Astros 7, Athletics 5
Rookie Lucas Spence hit his first three career homers and drove in five runs as Houston smacked five homers while defeating the Athletics in West Sacramento, Calif.
Isaac Paredes and Christian Walker added solo blasts for the Astros who remained tied for first in the AL West with the Rangers. Houston holds the tiebreaker, having gone 9-4 vs. Texas this year.
Houston reliever Miguel Ullola (2-0) fired three scoreless innings and Brayan Abreu worked 1 1/3 shutout innings for his ninth save. Zack Gelof hit two homers and Jeff McNeil drilled a three-run shot for the Athletics, who lost for the seventh time in nine games.
Yankees 6, Rays 4
Rookie George Lombard Jr. hit a tiebreaking two-run homer with two outs in the eighth inning as New York overcame a four-run deficit and earned a victory over visiting Tampa Bay.
New York ace Cam Schlittler allowed two runs (one earned) in three innings in a playoff tuneup, ending the season with a 1.95 ERA. Bradley Hanner (1-0) threw two scoreless innings for his first career victory.
Junior Caminero had a pair of RBI singles for the Rays. Ian Seymour allowed one hit in five scoreless innings. Steven Matz (5-6) served up Lombard's decisive homer.
Pirates 2, Cardinals 1
Spencer Horwitz's sacrifice fly in the eighth drove in the go-ahead run, and Paul Skenes concluded his season with a quality start as Pittsburgh wrapped up its home schedule with a victory over St. Louis.
Skenes tossed 6 1/3 innings, struck out eight, walked two and allowed one run on three hits. His final pitch completed a strikeout of Leo Bernal, giving him 200-plus for the second straight season. Luke Weaver (4-1) escaped an inherited eighth-inning jam before Mason Montgomery recorded his 17th save.
Alec Burleson homered for the Cardinals. St. Louis (77-82) is guaranteed to finish with back-to-back losing seasons for the first time since 1994-95.
Reds 7, Braves 6
A two-run homer by Hector Rodriguez, one of three long balls by Cincinnati, helped the visiting Reds beat Atlanta in the rubber game of a three-game series.
Rodriguez clubbed a 423-foot homer to right field against AJ Smith-Shawver (0-3) in the sixth inning to give the Reds the lead for good. Elly De La Cruz added his 30th homer and Carlos Jorge hit his first career homer. Cincinnati reliever Connor Phillips (2-0) pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings.
Atlanta right-hander Tyler Mahle threw five innings and gave up five runs on six hits in his worst outing since being acquired from San Francisco at the trade deadline.
Angels 6, Mariners 4
Christian Moore doubled, singled and drove in three runs as Los Angeles won at Seattle.
Josh Lowe also had a single and a double and scored three times for the Angels. Los Angeles starter Grayson Rodriguez (5-8) gave up four runs on five hits over five innings. Ryan Watson pitched the ninth for his fourth save.
Julio Rodriguez homered for the Mariners, whose postseason hopes were dashed when the Rangers defeated the Mets earlier in the day. Bryan Woo (12-10) allowed five runs, four earned, on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox Get Excellent Rehab Update on Garrett Crochet originally appeared on NESN. Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Boston Red Sox are hopeful that over the next couple of days, they'll get a definitive answer on what left-hander Garrett Crochet is going to look like in the playoffs. As of now, he's certainly out for the next four games, which will conclude the Red Sox's regular season.
As for when he could return, it seems possible he could be available for the Red Sox's expected series against the New York Yankees in the Wild Card round.
It's tough to know exactly what Crochet might look like at this stage, but if the Red Sox put him on the mound, they'll have a lot of confidence that he's healthy. Even if his stuff isn't what it usually is, the bigger focus needs to be keeping Crochet healthy.
Speaking to reporters about how he looks, Chad Tracy provided an update about the left-hander, adding that the weather made it difficult to arrange live batting practice against hitters.
"Garrett felt pretty good today, which is encouraging," said the Red Sox manager, per MassLive. "He felt pretty good (today), all things considered. That was his first real intense live (batting practice)."
"With the weather, where are we doing (a live BP)?" wondered Tracy. "But the next step would be another live this weekend. (We're just) figuring out what that's going to be and where it's going to be."
The weather was something to consider this weekend, though there were other ways for the Red Sox to get a good feel for what Crochet can do on the mound. Facing hitters will be a step in the right direction and build Boston's confidence.
Reports have indicated he will head down to Fort Myers to get some work in against hitters.
"The left-hander originally was set to throw the live BP at Fenway Park, but with a Nor'easter expected to hit this weekend, the Red Sox decided to move it to their spring training complex," Mass Live reported.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Red Sox hoping investment in Ranger Suarez pays off again in the postseason - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Peter Abraham

Eight months later, it’s fair to say Suarez did what was expected. He was 8-5 with a 3.22 earned run average over 28 starts and 148 innings. item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox made their biggest investment of the offseason in January when they signed free agent lefthander Ranger Suarez for five years and $130 million.
Eight months later, it’s fair to say Suarez did what was expected.
He was 8-5 with a 3.22 earned run average over 28 starts and 148 innings. Suarez was an All-Star, and the Sox were 17-11 in the games he started. Outside of missing three starts with a groin strain and a sore lower back, Suarez was a reliable rotation pillar.
He allowed one earned run or none in 16 starts. That’s right in line with how he pitched for the Phillies in 2024 and ’25.
Suarez allowed one run on three hits over five innings in a 1-0 loss against the Guardians on Thursday night. The one run came on a 319-foot Pesky Pole home run by Angel Martinez in the second inning.
Otherwise, Suarez stayed in control despite throwing 39 pitches over the first two innings.
“When you look at the body of work, especially coupled with the other guys in the rotation, he was fantastic,” manager Chad Tracy said. “He had a great year.”
Suarez wasn’t quite so complimentary of himself.
“In general, good,” he said via a translator. “Obviously I think I could have done better. But I was happy I was able to finish the season strong.”
Now comes the true test.
Suarez was 4-1 with a 1.48 ERA in 11 postseason games for the Phillies, eight of them as a starter. Philadelphia won eight of those games.
That includes Game 3 of the Division Series against the Dodgers last season when Suarez pitched five innings out of the bullpen and held the mighty Dodgers to one run at Dodger Stadium. That’s what he’s capable of in a big game.
Suarez is likely to start Game 3 in the Wild Card Series next week, which means he could have a huge say in whether this memorable season will continue.
“Being able to finish this month strong, I think, is going to be the key for the playoffs,” Suarez said.
Suarez was referring to the 1.09 ERA and 0.93 WHIP he posted over his final four starts.
His results against the Yankees this season were less encouraging. Suarez faced them three times and allowed 11 earned runs over 16 innings.
But he did have a strong start at Yankee Stadium on June 7, allowing one run over 6 innings against Cam Schlittler. It was 1-1 when Suarez left the game; then the bullpen allowed five runs.
Tracy has not revealed his rotation for the series. But if he stays in order, it would be Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Suarez.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone has held back that information, too.
Schlittler, who is a heavy favorite to win the Cy Young Award, would make sense to start Game 1. He dominated the Sox in four starts this season, allowing two earned runs over 24 innings and striking out 27.
A Tolle-Schlittler matchup would be must-viewing for even a casual baseball fan.
But there is speculation that the Yankees would save Schlittler for Game 2 and give Game 1 to lefthander Max Fried, who also has pitched well against the Sox this season.
That might be overthinking it, but it’s an option.
Based on the last few games, the Red Sox will need their pitchers to be close to perfect. Tracy has used the last 10 days to give his regulars rest while giving extra time off to players who have been dealing with injuries.
The Sox have scored only five runs over their last five games and hit .222. Willson Contreras, who was thought to be progressing well from a bruised right hand, said after the game he was concerned about being ready for the Yankees series.
“I’m doing everything that I can to come back and play with the boys and be with them,” Suarez said. “But sometimes you have to listen to your body.”
If Contreras can’t play, or is compromised, that would put even more pressure on the pitchers.
“This team can pitch,” Suarez said. “We’ll be ready for next week.”
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [NBC Boston] Red Sox legend Pedro Martinez launches coding program for kids in Lawrence
item.dc:creator: Malcolm Johnson

More than 20 years later, as schoolchildren cheered and swarmed around him for autographs Thursday in Lawrence, Massachusetts, it was clear that has not changed. The baseball Hall of Famer's childhood struggles continue to inspire his commitment to giving back. Martinez and his wife, Carolina, are launching a new afterschool coding program serving seven elementary schools in Lawrence. "I had to struggle for every
item.content:encoded:
When Pedro Martinez was on the mound for the Boston Red Sox, he was a fan favorite.
More than 20 years later, as schoolchildren cheered and swarmed around him for autographs Thursday in Lawrence, Massachusetts, it was clear that has not changed.
The baseball Hall of Famer's childhood struggles continue to inspire his commitment to giving back. Martinez and his wife, Carolina, are launching a new afterschool coding program serving seven elementary schools in Lawrence.
"I had to struggle for everything I achieved in life, and I just want to make it easier for others to get to where I got," Martinez said.
The program will give hundreds of third- and fourth-grade students access to modern technology and opportunities to develop coding and problem-solving skills.
"Maybe because it's something I was denied when I was younger," Martinez said when asked why the program is so important to him.
Martinez spoke with students at Lawrence schools as part of a back-to-school celebration, where children also received school supplies and gift bags.
The program is focused on reaching students early, Carolina Martinez said.
"Their age mattered to us in terms of the decision, because the earlier you get them, the more motivated they're going to be, but also, the more resourceful they're going to be later on," she said.
South Lawrence East Elementary School Principal Lori Butterfield said students are already immersed in technology, and the program will help them move from simply using technology to creating with it.
"They love playing games. They love using apps. They're using AI all the time. I want them to learn how to create those things, and I think this program will allow them to do that," Butterfield said.
For Martinez, the connection to Lawrence is personal.
"Why? Because in Lawrence, I quickly identified the need, I found my culture, I found my people here. I found my roots," he said.
Martinez also reflected on what can happen when young people are given even one opportunity.
"Remember, what you're seeing right now is the product of an opportunity. Only one, and that's all it took," he said.
Martinez seized his own opportunities on the mound, becoming one of baseball's most accomplished pitchers.
With the Red Sox preparing to face the Yankees in the postseason, Martinez was asked how he would feel about taking the mound today.
"I'll be ready from here, to give them all the knowledge and everything, all the experience I've done before — I'm ready to do that any day," he said. "But physically, to go pitch? I have Payton Tolle and I have Sonny Gray to go do it for me."
Martinez said he plans to continue coming back to Lawrence and contributing to the community — a place he now considers home.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Willson Contreras' lingering injury worries Red Sox ahead of potential Wild Card series vs. Yankees
item.dc:creator: Ben Pawlak
item.description: With the Yankees set to host a best-of-three AL Wild Card series next Tuesday, it's time to take a detailed look at their most likely opponent - who also happens to be their most hated rivals, the Boston Red Sox. With this in mind, the most recent news coming out of Boston certainly shakes up the outlook for their potential playoff series in New York. All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras, who was hit on the right hand against the Texas Rangers on Sep. 17, is still unable to swing a bat due t
item.content:encoded:
With the Yankees set to host a best-of-three AL Wild Card series next Tuesday, it's time to take a detailed look at their most likely opponent - who also happens to be their most hated rivals, the Boston Red Sox.
With this in mind, the most recent news coming out of Boston certainly shakes up the outlook for their potential playoff series in New York.
All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras, who was hit on the right hand against the Texas Rangers on Sep. 17, is still unable to swing a bat due to the pain.
"I tried to swing the bat yesterday, and couldn't swing, I tried to swing the bat today, and couldn't swing," Contreras lamented. "It's really concerning... I couldn't hit because my hand hurts, my right hand just feels weaker. It's not a good sign."
"I know Tuesday's [Wild Card opener] is going to be a really important game, the start of a really important series," the slugger continued. "I'm an honest guy, so if [on Tuesday], the game comes around and I don't feel confident in my hand to play, if I'm not feeling good, I'm not taking [a teammate's] spot."
Red Sox manager Chad Tracy commented that the team is "still working through" Contreras' injury, but has "the goal of getting him to the postseason."
Following the team's 1-0 loss to the Guardians on Thursday, Contreras leads all qualified Red Sox batters in home runs (27), RBI (81), on-base percentage (.387), and OPS (.905).
The Red Sox will conclude their season with a three-game home stand against the Chicago Cubs, with Friday being a doubleheader due to Sunday's game being postponed due to inclement weather.
Unless the Boston Red Sox (85-74), Cleveland Guardians (83-76), and Chicago White Sox (82-77) all finish the regular season with identical 85-77 records, the Yankees will face the Red Sox in that playoff series.
For anyone interested in that extremely unlikely scenario where all three teams finish 85-77, here's the breakdown: the White Sox would win the AL Central on a head-to-head tiebreaker with the Guardians, and the Guardians would earn the higher AL Wild Card seed due to their superior interdivisional record compared to that of the Red Sox.
In that (and only that) scenario, the Yankees would host the Guardians rather than the Red Sox in that series.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Frustrated by lingering pain, Red Sox slugger casts doubt on availability
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo

When he came back to Fenway Park on Thursday to try again, he once again discovered he couldn’t do it. At the very least, Contreras doesn’t expect to play in Friday’s doubleheader. “I tried to swing yesterday, could
item.content:encoded:
When Willson Contreras picked up a bat and tried to swing on Wednesday, he was disappointed to find he couldn’t do it pain free.
When he came back to Fenway Park on Thursday to try again, he once again discovered he couldn’t do it.
Now as his teammates look to wrap up the regular season and gear up for the playoffs, the Red Sox slugger is unsure if he’ll be ready in time to join them.
At the very least, Contreras doesn’t expect to play in Friday’s doubleheader.
“I tried to swing yesterday, couldn’t swing, I tried to swing today and couldn’t swing, so we’re taking it day by day, putting in all my efforts with the trainers on my hand to make it feel better,” Contreras said postgame Thursday. “As of now I don’t think I’m playing tomorrow.”
Contreras was hit in the right hand by a pitch during the eighth inning of last Thursday’s 4-3 win over the Texas Rangers, and while subsequent imaging — including a fresh CT scan this Thursday — has ruled out a fracture, the All-Star first baseman is still dealing with inflammation and a bone bruise.
Contreras acknowledged that he’s frustrated and about how slowly his hand has recovered, saying he teared up at his locker when he couldn’t swing Thursday, and he’s concerned about whether he’ll be ready in time for the postseason.
“I’m putting in all my effort, everything I can do I’m doing it, I don’t know what else to say,” Contreras said. “I’m working hard with the trainers, the hand is slowly getting better, I haven’t been able to swing and I’ll be honest with the team, I know Tuesday is a really important game, it’s a really important series, and I’ll be completely honest with the team.”
When asked about his confidence level for Game 1 on Tuesday, Contreras replied: “Did you hear what I said?”
Contreras said the fact that his right hand was hit is especially problematic and if it had been his left hand he might still be able to generate the power necessary to complete his swing. He emphasized again that he’s doing everything he can to get back, but ultimately he’s going to listen to his body and do what he feels is best for the team.
“If I don’t feel confident in my hand to be able to play Sunday or Tuesday I’ll be completely honest with the team, I don’t want to hurt the team in any way,” Contreras said. “I know the guys here have been playing every single day, and I respect that, if I don’t feel good I don’t want to take anyone’s spot.”
If Contreras can’t make it back by the start of the playoffs, the Red Sox will go into the AL Wild Card Series without perhaps their best all-around hitter. In his first season in Boston Contreras leads the Red Sox with 27 home runs and is batting .276 with 81 RBI and a .905 OPS.

item.title: [unanimodeportes.com] ¡Aroldis Chapman, el cubano que sigue haciendo historia en MLB! - UNANIMO Deportes
item.dc:creator: Jocelyn Blasco
item.description: Aroldis Chapman volvió al montículo y recordó por qué se ha convertido en uno de los relevistas latinos más importantes de la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El cubano regresó este miércoles con los Boston Red Sox después de 10 días fuera y cerró la victoria 1-0 sobre los Cleveland Guardians con tres ponches consecutivos. - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Shohei Ohtani está de vuelta! Los Dodgers recuperan a su estrella - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Braves regresan a la cima! Atlanta asegura el Este de la Nacional Sus
item.content:encoded:
Aroldis Chapman volvió al montículo y recordó por qué se ha convertido en uno de los relevistas latinos más importantes de la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El cubano regresó este miércoles con los Boston Red Sox después de 10 días fuera y cerró la victoria 1-0 sobre los Cleveland Guardians con tres ponches consecutivos.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Shohei Ohtani está de vuelta! Los Dodgers recuperan a su estrella
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Braves regresan a la cima! Atlanta asegura el Este de la Nacional
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
El zurdo necesitó apenas 12 lanzamientos para retirar la novena entrada, 10 de ellos strikes. Chapman comenzó el episodio ponchando a los tres bateadores que enfrentó y aseguró su salvamento número 35 de la temporada, demostrando que mantiene su capacidad para dominar en los momentos de mayor presión.
A sus 38 años, el nacido en Holguín, Cuba, atraviesa su decimoséptima temporada en las Grandes Ligas. En 2026 registra una efectividad de 1.92, 71 ponches en 51.2 entradas y 35 salvamentos en 37 oportunidades. Su WHIP se mantiene en 1.12.
Pero la temporada de Chapman también tiene un significado histórico para el beisbol latinoamericano. A principios de septiembre, el cubano llegó a los 400 salvamentos en su carrera, convirtiéndose en apenas el noveno relevista en la historia de MLB en alcanzar esa cifra. Con ello, se unió a un grupo encabezado por el panameño Mariano Rivera y en el que también aparecen figuras como Francisco Rodríguez, de Venezuela, y Kenley Jansen, de Curazao.
El otro gran capítulo de su legado llegó en julio. Chapman consiguió su ponche número 1,364 y superó a Hoyt Wilhelm para convertirse en el relevista con más ponches en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. La marca había pertenecido al miembro del Salón de la Fama durante más de cinco décadas.
Ese récord adquiere todavía mayor dimensión cuando se considera el camino recorrido por el cubano desde su debut. Chapman llegó a las Grandes Ligas en 2010 con los Cincinnati Reds y posteriormente lanzó para los New York Yankees, Chicago Cubs, Kansas City Royals, Texas Rangers y Pittsburgh Pirates antes de consolidarse con Boston.
Además de sus récords, el cubano dejó una huella particular por la potencia de su recta. Chapman llegó a registrar una velocidad de 105.8 millas por hora en 2010, una marca que contribuyó a construir el perfil de uno de los lanzadores más reconocibles de su generación.
Ahora, Chapman encara el cierre de la temporada con los Red Sox y apunta a octubre después de superar una molestia en el costado que lo mantuvo fuera durante 10 días. Su regreso no necesitó grandes discursos: tres bateadores enfrentados, tres ponches y un salvamento más para una carrera que ya ocupa un lugar especial entre los relevistas latinos de las Grandes Ligas.
Más allá de los números, Chapman representa una de las carreras más longevas y exitosas de un lanzador cubano en las Grandes Ligas. A casi dos décadas de su llegada a MLB, el zurdo continúa sumando capítulos a un legado que ya lo coloca entre los relevistas latinos más destacados de la historia.

item.title: [USA Today] Alex Bregman's wild MLB playoff streak has star in rare air – injured face willing

item.content:encoded:
Alex Bregman's wild MLB playoff streak has star in rare air – injured face willing
Major League Baseball’s playoffs are coming soon and Alex Bregman will be a part of it.
Of course he is.
Bregman made baseball history Thursday, Sept. 24 when the Chicago Cubs clinched a National League wild-card berth with a victory over the Miami Marlins. And for the 10th consecutive year, injured eye willing, Bregman will take part in the postseason, this time with a twist.
Bregman, the Cubs’ 32-year-old third baseman, will become the first position player to play postseason baseball 10 consecutive seasons with multiple teams. In fact, he’s done it with three ballclubs – eight straight years with the Houston Astros and then the past two with the Boston Red Sox and Cubs, as he settled for good in Chicago by signing a five-year, $175 million contract in January.
And it seems like wherever Bregman goes, October baseball follows.
Texas loves him anyway
Bregman was a two-time All-Star and two-time champion in Houston, the brash young slugger in his first full season when they won the 2017 World Series, the MVP runner-up when they lost the 2019 Series in seven games.
After bearing much of the scorn for the club’s 2017 sign-stealing scandal, he was the chastened veteran on the 2022 squad that won a second World Series, this time without a cloud of controversy to follow.
Yet Bregman’s chops as a club cornerstone gained greater veracity a year ago, when he left the Astros and, combining his production with his baseball smarts and clubhouse gravitas, lifted the Red Sox to the postseason for the first time in three years as the Astros missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016.
Those vibes were as attractive to the Cubs as Bregman’s career .846 OPS when they pursued him after he opted out of his contract with Boston. And it’s all come together in Wrigleyville: Thanks to a second-half surge, Bregman has hit 26 home runs, posted an .804 OPS and produced 5.4 WAR, second only to presumed MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong on the Cubs.
“Anytime Alex Bregman is playing an Alex Bregman brand of baseball, it’s just good for the program,” Crow-Armstrong told USA TODAY Sports last month.
And if he manages to play just days after suffering a gruesome eye injury, the legend will only grow.
Heroes of the fall
Bregman’s postseason constancy has put himself among some legendary and curious October stalwarts.
Unsurprisingly, the consecutive postseasons list is littered with alumni from the three dominant playoff groups of the wild-card era: The 1990s Atlanta Braves, the late-century New York Yankees and the current batch of Los Angeles Dodgers.
Yankees closer Mariano Rivera tops the list, appearing in 13 consecutive postseasons from 1995-2007, followed by Derek Jeter, whose 12-year streak began a year after Rivera’s playoff debut.
Catcher Jorge Posada and Braves Hall of Famers Chipper Jones and Tom Glavine all played in 11 consecutive postseasons. As did lefty reliever Mike Stanton, who did it with four teams – the Braves, Red Sox, Yankees and Texas Rangers – between 1991-2002.
Who let him in?
Bregman, longtime Dodgers closer Kenley Jansen and Hall of Famer Greg Maddux all reached 10 consecutive postseasons. Current Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman and longtime third baseman Justin Turner are at the nine-year mark, Freddie winning a World Series championship with Atlanta in 2021 and two more in L.A. the past two seasons.
Retired Dodgers lefty Clayton Kershaw leads the “but for” category: He pitched in eight consecutive postseasons from 2013-2020, and would have made it 13 in a row if not for injuries in 2021 and 2024. Same with Braves Hall of Famer John Smoltz – he was present for all of Atlanta’s 14 consecutive division titles yet underwent Tommy John surgery in 2000.
And several likely 2026 participants had streaks broken thanks to one unlucky season – such as slugger Kyle Schwarber, who’d be working on a 12-year streak with the Cubs, Red Sox and Phillies if not for the 2019 Cubs missing the playoffs. Same with Mookie Betts, ticketed for his 10th postseason in 11 years with the Dodgers and Boston, missing only in ’19 with the Red Sox.
The wild-card format – which began in 1995 and expanded in 2012 and 2022 – makes this list unavoidably modern due to the expanded access it affords. Still, some players from past eras were near-constants in the playoffs.
Mr. October himself, Reggie Jackson, reached the postseason 10 times in 12 years from 1971 to 1982, winning four World Series with the Oakland Athletics and New York Yankees, and then, just for kicks, reaching the 1982 ALCS with the California Angels.
The great Yogi Berra was a 10-time World Series champion, but his longest consecutive streak of playoff runs was five years. Yet reaching the World Series 14 times in 17 years, when only two teams reached the playoffs, remains a stunning feat.
So perhaps Bregman - even with 102 career postseason games, 19 homers, 91 hits and a .791 OPS - has a little more work to do to match some of the legends of October. Yet from Houston to Boston to Chicago, he’s leaving little doubt that wherever he goes, winning follows.

item.title: [bignewsnetwork.com] Guardians eke out 1-0 win over Red Sox, clinch playoff berth
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: Guardians eke out 1-0 win over Red Sox, clinch playoff berth (Photo credit: Paul Rutherford) Angel Martinez's second-inning home run was all the visiting Guardians needed for a 1-0 win over the Boston Red Sox on Thursday night, allowing Cleveland to clinch its third consecutive American League playoff berth. While Martinez provided the only offense, Joey Cantillo (11-9) dominated for five shutout innings behind opener Daniel Espino. Cantillo allowed just one hit and two walks and striking out fo
item.content:encoded:
Guardians eke out 1-0 win over Red Sox, clinch playoff berth
(Photo credit: Paul Rutherford)
Angel Martinez's second-inning home run was all the visiting Guardians needed for a 1-0 win over the Boston Red Sox on Thursday night, allowing Cleveland to clinch its third consecutive American League playoff berth.
While Martinez provided the only offense, Joey Cantillo (11-9) dominated for five shutout innings behind opener Daniel Espino. Cantillo allowed just one hit and two walks and striking out four. He has not allowed a run across his last three outings (15 innings) as a bulk reliever.
The Guardians (83-76) totaled four hits but allowed only two to the Red Sox (85-74) en route to winning the decisive game of the three-game series. Boston earned a 1-0 victory on Wednesday.
Cleveland logged its seventh win in eight games to remain one game ahead of the Chicago White Sox (82-77) atop the AL Central. Both teams have three regular-season games remaining.
The playoff-bound Red Sox fell for the fourth time in five games despite getting five innings of one-run ball from Ranger Suarez (8-5). He struck out five and allowed three hits and one walk.
Espino bookended his 1-2-3 first inning with strikeouts.
The lone run came in the second, as Martinez broke up Suarez's four-up, four-down start with a 319-foot solo homer inside Pesky's Pole in right field.
Suarez escaped a two-on jam in the third with back-to-back outs and retired the final eight Guardians he faced.
Both bullpens were very strong. Hunter Gaddis allowed the sole hit in relief of Cantillo, a Jarren Duran single in the seventh, but they came after a leadoff walk in the frame was erased in a 6-4-3 double play.
Cleveland's Erik Sabrowski struck out two in the eighth, and Cade Smith fanned the side in a 1-2-3 ninth for his 41st save of the season.
Boston's Patrick Sandoval, Erik Miller and Raymond Burgos allowed just one combined hit across four shutout innings after Suarez departed. Burgos pitched hitless ball over the final two frames.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Red Sox try Patrick Sandoval out of bullpen but bats go quiet as Guardians clinch playoff spot - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Tim Healey
item.description: In these waning days of the regular season, the Red Sox are trying something new: Patrick Sandoval, reliever. Sandoval tossed a scoreless sixth inning in a 1-0 loss to the Guardians on Thursday, his first appearance out of the bullpen since 2021. It was a successfully uneventful frame at Fenway Park: After José Ramírez grounded a single through the left side of the infield and stole second, Sandoval retired Chase DeLauter (strikeout looking), Jo Adell (ground out), and Angel Martínez (ground out
item.content:encoded:
In these waning days of the regular season, the Red Sox are trying something new: Patrick Sandoval, reliever.
Sandoval tossed a scoreless sixth inning in a 1-0 loss to the Guardians on Thursday, his first appearance out of the bullpen since 2021.
It was a successfully uneventful frame at Fenway Park: After José Ramírez grounded a single through the left side of the infield and stole second, Sandoval retired Chase DeLauter (strikeout looking), Jo Adell (ground out), and Angel Martínez (ground out). His velocity was down a tad in the small sample size of 12 pitches (10 strikes), but he was pitching just three days after his most recent start.
Ahead of the playoffs opening Tuesday, the Sandoval twist is of particular note because of his recent struggles as a starter and the Red Sox’ recent struggles looking for a reliable lefthanded reliever.
As a member of the rotation, Sandoval had a 5.15 ERA in 13 outings this year. That included a 7.32 mark in four starts this month. He has appeared unlikely to fit into the postseason plans in that role.
Also of late, Erik Miller, the team’s top lefty reliever, has had a bad time, entering the day with a 8.53 ERA in seven appearances this month. Of the 36 hitters he had faced, 17 had reached base: six hits, a whopping nine walks, and two batters hit by pitches.
Immediately after Sandoval departed, though, Miller entered — and maybe figured it out. He turned in a perfect seventh on just eight pitches, getting a strikeout of David Fry, a routine fly out from Travis Bazzana, and a 108-miles-per-hour line out from Patrick Bailey.
The loss dropped the Red Sox to 85-74 and — with three games to go — ensured that they will not match their 89 wins from last year.
They totaled two hits. Nick Sogard and Jarren Duran each had a single. It was the fourth game this month in which the Sox recorded four hits or fewer.
Lefthander Ranger Suarez finished a strong September — and strong regular season — with five innings of one-run ball. He held the Guardians to three hits and a walk and struck out five.
Cleveland’s lone run against him came on Martínez’s home run, tucked inside the Pesky Pole, an estimated 319 feet down the right-field line. It came off his bat at only 94 m.p.h. The batted ball had an expected batting average of .160.
At the end of the first season of a five-year, $130 million contract, Suarez owns a 3.22 ERA, third best in the Red Sox’ rotation behind righthander Sonny Gray (2.72) and lefthander Payton Tolle (3.03).
Suarez suffered from a midseason dip — a groin injury followed by mediocrity — but rebounded late, posting a 1.09 ERA over his final four starts.
The Sox mustered minimal offense against opener Daniel Espino (perfect first inning with two strikeouts) and lefthander Joey Cantillo (one hit and no runs in five innings).
For Cantillo, who entered the night with the most walks in the American League (79) but issued just two free passes against the Red Sox, it was his third consecutive scoreless appearance. In all three, he entered behind an opener.
Tim Healey can be reached at timothy.healey@globe.com. Follow him @timbhealey.

item.title: [Cubbies Crib] Cubs, Red Sox continue to face never-ending weather drama while Alex Bregman return looms
item.dc:creator: Jordan Campbell

While it was announced on Wednesday night that the Cubs and Red Sox would play a doubleheader at Fenway Park on Friday, it sounds like the final plans have yet to be determined. Word from Wrigley Field on Thursday was that scenario could see the te
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Cubs will be playing the Boston Red Sox this weekend, but there's still the question of Alex Bregman potentially making his return to the Cubs before the playoffs, and, more importantly, whether the series can actually be played in Boston.
While it was announced on Wednesday night that the Cubs and Red Sox would play a doubleheader at Fenway Park on Friday, it sounds like the final plans have yet to be determined. Word from Wrigley Field on Thursday was that scenario could see the teams play at Fenway Park on Friday, and then move the series to Tampa Bay for the final two games. The Rays are finishing the season on the road against the Philadelphia Phillies this weekend.
If the final two games were to be moved to Tampa Bay, they would go back to Saturday and Sunday as originally scheduled.
It would seem that Major League Baseball is trying to find an outcome that works for each time. The Cubs very much would be put in a tough spot with their pitching staff if they were forced to get through a doubleheader on Friday, and then pitch Shota Imanaga on short rest on Sunday. Meanwhile, the Red Sox are looking at a potential loss of revenue, which does need to be factored into these conversations.
Note that if the Cubs and Red Sox do move forward with a doubleheader, roster rules in September prevent an additional player being added to the roster, considering rosters have already been expanded.
Alex Bregman injury update sets up Red Sox revenge before Cubs begin playoff run
Beyond the weather, for the Cubs, there's the matter of Bregman potentially returning before the playoffs. Despite Bregman dealing with multiple facial fractures, he's avoided surgery and has resumed baseball activities. With each day, the impression is that Bregman has taken steps forward in his recovery.
Speaking with reporters on Thursday, Craig Counsell confirmed that Bregman has resumed hitting and would get some additional running in before the Cubs made any further decisions. Barring a setback, it would seem that Bregman is positioned to return over the weekend as the Cubs' designated hitter.
That does set the stage for an awkward revenge opportunity against the Red Sox. The whole reason Bregman was available to the Cubs last offseason is because the Red Sox low-balled their final offer to him, and called Scott Boras' bluff. Safe to say Red Sox fans have had this series circled since Bregman signed with the Cubs, but it certainly would be a strange sight if it takes place in Tampa instead of Fenway Park.
