item.content:encoded:
Willson Contreras remained absent from the Red Sox’ lineup Thursday night at Fenway Park, seven days after he got hit by a pitch and bruised his right hand.
Is it fair to say he will be ready for the start of the playoffs?
“I hope so,” manager Chad Tracy said before the team’s finale with the Guardians. “I hope so. But [the Red Sox] want to see how he gets through all this stuff and where he’s at. And my hope is — at least for now — that he swings and feels even better than he did the other day, and then we’ll go from there.”
The first baseman took batting practice in the indoor cage, as he did earlier in the week.
It would be “huge,” Tracy said, if he was ready in time to play at any point during the Cubs series. Otherwise, he may well roll into the AL Wild Card Series without having faced live pitching in nearly two weeks.
“But I also think you’re talking about a guy [who has] a pretty good idea of his swing,” Tracy said. “[With] Willson not being down that long, the most important thing is that he’s healthy. So if he’s healthy and feeling good about it, where we’re able to get him some at-bats, that’d be great. But we’re still going to be reactive to how he’s feeling.”
Weather watch
The Cubs-Red Sox series remains in flux.
They will attempt to play a doubleheader at Fenway Park on Friday, with 1 p.m. and 6 p.m. first pitches, before a potential nor’easter arrives.
Yet to be decided: where and when the teams play their regular-season finale. Although it is scheduled for 7:15 p.m. Saturday in Boston, it could be moved to another venue, such as Tampa Bay, if the weekend forecast remains horrendous.
If the game is moved, the clubs would leave Friday night and likely play at 3 p.m. Sunday, same as all of the other finales.
MLB and the teams intend to make a call by midday Friday about what to do about Game 162.
“In a nutshell, it doesn’t look good. That’s basically what I’ve heard,” Tracy said of the weather. “Seems like we should be able to get that [doubleheader] in even [if during] the second game there might be a little bit of drizzle or whatever. It doesn’t look bad, at least what I’m seeing, and then figure out what happens next.”
Crochet on the move
A wrinkle from the weather: Garrett Crochet (left shoulder injury) will head to Fort Myers, Fla., on Friday so that he can throw an inning of live batting practice on Saturday.
The Sox have a stash of Triple-A hitters, including infielders Romy Gonzalez and Franklin Arias, working out at Fenway South.
Rafaela OK
Ceddanne Rafaela turned out to be just fine after a scare Wednesday.
The Thursday MRI on his right hamstring came back “clean,” Tracy said, affirming Rafaela’s stance from the night prior that his exit after two innings was no big deal.
“The feel is that it was a cramp, probably actually precipitated by the diving catch an inning prior],” Tracy said. “He tends to dive, and he does have low back/hip stuff that throws him out of the line for a second, that’ll manifest itself in feeling [the hamstring].”
Rafaela was back in the lineup against the Guardians, batting sixth and playing center field. It was his second game back from a right quad strain.
Major honors from minors
The Red Sox announced their annual minor league award winners, a group headed by Arias, the offensive player of the year. He slashed .323/.400/.557 with 25 homers and 91 RBIs in 117 games with Double-A Portland and Triple-A Worcester, emerging as one of the top prospects in all of the minors.
Lefthander Dylan Brown was named pitcher of the year. A 22-year-old starter, he had a 3.46 ERA and 143 strikeouts in 106⅔ innings with Low-A Salem and High-A Greenville.
Other honored were catcher Gerardo Rodriguez (defensive player of the year), outfielder Andrews Opata (baserunner of the year), outfielder Joskairo Ramirez (Latin program position player of the year), and righthander Emanuel Jimenez (Latin program pitcher of the year).
Mead update
Infielder Curtis Mead (left wrist fracture) plans to take another step forward Friday by taking batting practice off of a machine. He will head to Fort Myers with Crochet and potentially hit against him on Saturday, he said. He is not ruled out for the first round of the playoffs beginning Tuesday, but that deadline might be too soon … Tracy left Roman Anthony out of the lineup to give him a day off. The outfielder had started 22 consecutive games since returning from the IL, batting .242 with a .726 OPS … Eli White was back at Fenway for the first time since season-ending right foot surgery Tuesday. He said he is due for a three-month recovery. That timeline would allow the outfielder to get almost all the way back to full health before the expected lockout on Dec. 1, at which point teams will not be allowed to communicate with players … Infielder Anthony Seigler said he was diagnosed with a carpal boss, a bony lump on the back of his right hand/wrist — the same injury that plagued catcher Connor Wong last year. Wong wound up having surgery to get it removed. Seigler said he has not discussed that possibility with the Red Sox … DH/outfielder Masataka Yoshida (left hamstring strain) appeared on the field at Fenway, playing catch and doing light agility drills … Dustin Pedroia and his family, in town this week, were on the field about five hours before first pitch against Cleveland, chatting with Red Sox personnel. His three sons made sure to poke their head into the Green Monster.
Tim Healey can be reached at timothy.healey@globe.com. Follow him @timbhealey.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Alex Bregman may return from horrifying injury in time to play Cubs' final series against Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: All season, a reunion with short-term former third baseman Alex Bregman has hung over the Boston Red Sox's heads. The Chicago Cubs are scheduled to play the final series of the year against the Sox in Boston but Bregman isn't expected to be part of the action The third baseman looks the worse for wear after he was hit in the face by a foul ball near the on-deck circle, blackening his eye, cutting and fracturing his face. The accident occurred on September 20 but Chicago hasn't been able to keep
item.content:encoded:
All season, a reunion with short-term former third baseman Alex Bregman has hung over the Boston Red Sox's heads. The Chicago Cubs are scheduled to play the final series of the year against the Sox in Boston but Bregman isn't expected to be part of the action
The third baseman looks the worse for wear after he was hit in the face by a foul ball near the on-deck circle, blackening his eye, cutting and fracturing his face. The accident occurred on September 20 but Chicago hasn't been able to keep Bregman off his feet since then.
Bregman is determined to play sooner than he probably should with multiple facial fractures. He told reporters on September 23 that he would try to get an at-bat in the Cubs' game that evening, which didn't end up happening. Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters there was no chance he'd play, but Bregman is seemingly choosing optimism.
Chicago still hasn't placed Bregman on the injured list, and as long as he's willing to play through his injuries, it probably won't. Bregman's excitement to get back into a game is a good sign as long as he isn't being overly reckless. According to Counsell via Jordan Bastian of MLB.com, the veteran still hasn't tried running, which would be critical to his return if he were to make one.
Alex Bregman is determined to return to action before Cubs-Red Sox season finale despite fractured face
Red Sox and Cubs fans would be shocked to see Bregman play in the regular season finale. On the night he was hit, his eye was swollen completely shut — the eye that points in the direction of the pitcher while he stands in the righty batter's box. His willingness to put his face on the line to get back into games is admirable, if not a little crazy.
The Cubs' postseason situation is a more precarious one than the Sox's. Boston has already clinched a playoff spot, and only in one rare, three-way tie scenario would keep it from playing a Wild Card rematch in the Bronx. Chicago is in a tight race against the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres to determine which team will face the twice-reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the first round (or the Milwaukee Brewers if they drop their hold on first place in the National League).
Bregman has been one of the Cubs' top hitters in the second half after a lackluster first, which puts his determination into perspective. He's posted a .296/.378/.600 slash line with 17 home runs over 59 games since the All-Star break.
It would be wild for the Cubs to let Bregman play with a fractured face but he seems unwilling to rest. The Red Sox and Cubs' three game series has already been condensed into two days due to a nor'easter coming Boston's way, so Bregman has even less time to get better to prepare for an appearance. If Bregman gets his way, Sox fans could see him at Fenway in the regular season finale.

item.title: [bostonherald.com] Red Sox outfielder in lineup after leaving Wednesday with hamstring issue
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Ceddanne Rafaela is back in the Red Sox lineup a day after leaving Wednesday night’s game with a right hamstring tightness. The Red Sox outfielder will bat sixth and start in center field for Thursday night’s finale against the Cleveland Guardians. “He’s good,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said pregame Thursday. “All the scans last night were clean, we did an MRI as a precaution, all clean, subjectively he feels really good, so seems exactly what it was, the feel is it was a cramp.” Rafaela left W
item.content:encoded:
Ceddanne Rafaela is back in the Red Sox lineup a day after leaving Wednesday night’s game with a right hamstring tightness.
The Red Sox outfielder will bat sixth and start in center field for Thursday night’s finale against the Cleveland Guardians.
“He’s good,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said pregame Thursday. “All the scans last night were clean, we did an MRI as a precaution, all clean, subjectively he feels really good, so seems exactly what it was, the feel is it was a cramp.”
Rafaela left Wednesday’s game in the top of the third inning after initially feeling tightness during his first at bat in the bottom of the second. He had just been activated from the injured list earlier that day after missing 17 games with a right quad strain, though Rafaela expressed optimism postgame that the hamstring issue was far less serious.
Losing Rafaela again so soon before the playoffs would have been a huge blow to the Red Sox. The outfielder is a favorite to win his second Gold Glove in center field and has enjoyed a strong season at the plate, batting .284 with 16 home runs, 17 stolen bases and a .763 OPS.
Though Rafaela won’t miss any more time, Willson Contreras remains out of the lineup with a bruised hand after being hit by a pitch last Thursday in Texas. Contreras has now been sidelined for a week, and the plan was for him to run through a battery of hitting drills in the cages and on the field Thursday to see how his hand is progressing.
While the hope is he will be ready to return soon, Tracy acknowledged that isn’t a guarantee.
“I hope so, but I want to see how he gets through all this stuff and where he’s at, and my hope is at least for now that he feels even better than he did the other day and we’ll go from there.”
Tracy added that while it would be great for Contreras to get some at bats before the regular season ends, he hasn’t missed much time and has a good idea of his swing, so it wouldn’t be an issue if he didn’t play before the postseason.
“The most important thing is he’s healthy,” Tracy said. “So if he’s healthy and feeling good about it where we can get him some at bats, that’d be great, but we’re still going to be reactive to how he’s feeling.”
Minor League awards
Top prospect Franklin Arias highlighted the Red Sox minor league award winners, earning Offensive Player of the Year recognition. The 20-year-old shortstop enjoyed a dominant season in which he batted .323 with 25 home runs, 91 RBI and a .957 OPS over 117 games across Double-A and Triple-A, and he finishes the year ranked as MLB’s No. 2 prospect according to Baseball America.
The other recipients include left-hander Dylan Brown (Pitcher of the Year), catcher Gerardo Rodriguez (Defensive Player of the Year), outfielder Andrews Opata (Baserunner of the Year), outfielder Joskairo Ramirez (Latin Program Position Player of the Year) and right-hander Emanuel Jimenez (Latin Program Pitcher of the Year).
Right-hander Wyatt Olds is also being recognized as the 2026 recipient of the Lou Gorman Award, which annually honors a Red Sox minor leaguer who demonstrates perseverance to make his big league debut.
Extra innings
With heavy rain expected throughout the weekend the Red Sox plan to send left-hander Garrett Crochet to Fort Myers on Friday so he can throw his next live batting practice session on Saturday. The expectation is he will throw one inning but probably more pitches than the 16 he threw on Tuesday. Depending on how things go the club will decide whether or not to add him to the Wild Card roster. … Roman Anthony, who is also not in Thursday’s lineup, is being given a day off his feet to rest, Tracy said. … Back in the clubhouse wearing a walking boot following his foot surgery earlier this week, outfielder Eli White confirmed he’ll be non-weight bearing for several weeks and will miss the remainder of the season. … Infielder Anthony Seigler (right wrist inflammation) has resumed taking ground balls and ran through a series of drills Thursday. … The Red Sox have not determined who will start Game 1 and 2 of next week’s AL Wild Card Series.

He singled off the Green Monster in the second inning and came up lame at first b
item.content:encoded:
BOSTON — Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who came off the injured list on Wednesday, left the game against the Cleveland Guardians before the third inning after pulling up while running out a single in the second.
Rafaela, who started and made a diving catch on the game’s first batter, had been sidelined since Sept. 3 with a right quad strain.
The team announced that he left with right hamstring tightness.
He singled off the Green Monster in the second inning and came up lame at first base. He was visited by manager Chad Tracy and a trainer, jogged a bit down the right-field foul line and stayed in the game.
He then trotted out to his position for the top of the third, but came walking off. He was replaced by Jarren Duran.
“He had like a little tightness in the upper hamstring, more on the swing,” Tracy said after their 1-0 victory over the Guardians. “I still saw him kind of flexing it a little bit (when he was heading to center), so I said ‘Let’s get him out of there.’ Everything so far is OK, they are going to get an MRI (Thursday) just to rule out anything.”
Rafaela, who won his first Gold Glove last season, made a headlong dive to rob Steve Kwan in right center on the third pitch of the game. He handled all three putouts the first inning.
“I was excited since (Tuesday) to be back on the field with the boys, then with the swing I felt a little bit of a cramp,” he said. “I was not happy.”
He said he still felt it a bit when he went to center.
“The sensation was there, it was just a cramp,” he said. “After that, I got in (the clubhouse) and did what I needed to do, and right now I feel much better.”
He was batting .284 with 16 homers and 70 RBI coming into Wednesday’s game.
To make room for him, the club optioned INF/OF Nate Eaton to Triple-A Worcester.
THE RED SOX are adjusting the schedule of their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs because of a significant storm that’s expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to the Boston area.
The team said it was moving the Sunday afternoon game to Friday to create a split doubleheader. The first game is scheduled to begin at 1:05 p.m. The originally scheduled 7:05 p.m. night game was moved up to 6:05.
The Red Sox said in a press release Wednesday that the change was made in consultation with Major League Baseball.
The Cubs are currently in a tight race for one of the NL’s three wild-card spots.
There was no mention of a change to Saturday’s game, which is slated for a 7:15 p.m. first pitch.

item.content:encoded:
A THREE-TIME Cy Young winner gave a blunt quote about his MLB future after his team’s disappointing season.
Toronto Blue Jays starting pitcher Max Scherzer, 42, revealed that he will make an announcement about his future in the coming days.
Scherzer and the Blue Jays have had brutal seasons.
The future Hall of Famer has a 3-9 record with a 6.14 ERA, and Toronto was eliminated from the postseason after appearing in the World Series in 2025.
After pitching in Game 1 of a Blue Jays doubleheader against the Baltimore Orioles on Wednesday, the 19-year veteran Scherzer said he’ll address his future soon.
“I’ll probably say something here in the next couple days,” Scherzer said.
Read More on MLB
The two-time World Series champion gave up four runs on four hits and three walks along with seven strikeouts in five innings in a 4-2 loss.
Scherzer told reporters he wants to pitch on Sunday against the Cincinnati Reds in the season finale in front of the home crowd in Toronto, which means he’d have to pitch on short rest.
“I don’t know if I want to publicly say, yet. I’d rather keep the blinders up and address once the season’s over,” Scherzer continued regarding his future.
“I’m not limping to the finish line, I’m accelerating through the finish line.
“. … We want to keep the focus on just getting to the finish line.”
Scherzer has had a less-than-stellar two-year stint in Toronto, as he pitched to a 5.19 ERA in 17 starts last season.
He has struggled this year while also battling injury.
Scherzer has nothing to prove, as he’s currently ninth on the all-time strikeouts list with 3,5000, just four behind former Detroit Tigers and New York Mets teammate Justin Verlander, who will make his final start on Sunday.
In 19 seasons, the eight-time All-Star has a 3.29 ERA and a 224-126 record across 3,040 2/3 innings.
Scherzer helped the Nationals to their first-ever World Series title in 2019, and won a second ring with the Texas Rangers in 2023.
He could make his final career start on Sunday against the Cincinnati Reds.
MLB important dates
THE 2026 Major League Baseball season is here as teams look to stop the Los Angeles Dodgers from completing a three-peat. Here are the season's important dates to know:
March 25 – Opening Night Game on Netflix (Yankees vs. Giants at Oracle Park)
March 26 – Traditional Opening Day
April 25-26 – MLB World Tour in Mexico City (Diamondbacks vs. Padres at Estadio Alfredo Harp Helú in Mexico City)
May 15-17 – MLB Rivalry Weekend
June 8-14 – Athletics host two series in Las Vegas
July 13-14 – MLB Home Run Derby, All-Star Game in Philadelphia
August 13 – MLB At Field of Dreams (Twins vs. Phillies on Netflix)
August 23 – Little League Classic (Brewers vs. Braves) in Williamsport
September 27 – Final day of the regular season
September 29 – Postseason begins
October 23 – World Series begins

item.content:encoded:
Roman Anthony is out of the Boston Red Sox lineup, raising an immediate question about whether something is wrong with the young star.
Here’s why Anthony is out of the lineup and what his absence means for the Red Sox.
Anthony is out of the Boston Red Sox lineup Thursday against Cleveland, but the club has not attached any new injury news to the decision.
Thursday is Anthony’s first day off since he returned from the injured list. The Red Sox have just three regular-season games left to play after Thursday.

| SP: Ranger Suárez (LHP #55) • 8-4, 3.27 ERA, 135 K | | | | |

Roman Anthony’s Lineup Status for Guardians Series Finale
Manager Chad Tracy had not yet explained the absence when the club posted the lineup ahead of his pregame media session.
The rest of the card shows how the night is built. Jarren Duran starts in left field, Mickey Gasper takes the designated hitter spot and Ceddanne Rafaela returns to center. Gasper bats right-handed, and Cleveland counters with right-hander Daniel Espino, according to MLB.com‘s lineup page. Left-hander Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) starts for Boston.
Rafaela left Wednesday’s 1-0 win with right hamstring tightness and was set to undergo an MRI Thursday, according to the Boston Globe. Duran replaced Rafaela in the third inning and went 2-for-3, according to the Globe‘s recap. Willson Contreras sits again.
Gasper was among the players optioned to make room for Anthony’s return.
“It was bittersweet. Like, I really mean it,” Tracy said, as quoted by Yahoo Sports.
Boston has already clinched a playoff spot. Tuesday’s card benched Trevor Story, Duran and Contreras with no public explanation, according to NESN reporter Rodney Knuppel.

| Season stats shown (AVG / OPS). | | | | |
Boston Red Sox Playoff Plans for Roman Anthony
No report ties Thursday’s absence to the right ring finger that cost Anthony nearly four months. He left a May 4 game at Detroit with wrist and hand discomfort, later described as a partially torn ligament, according to NESN‘s injury timeline.
Rehab stalled. Anthony “hasn’t made any substantive progress,” Tracy said in a late-June update, as quoted by Boston.com.
The Red Sox shifted him to the 60-day list and sent him to Fort Myers. Even after 3 1/2 months, the club declined to circle a return date, according to the Boston Globe. He was finally activated on Aug. 30, according to NBC Sports.
He has hit .242/.294/.432 with four home runs in 22 games since activation. His return began 10-for-22 over five games, then cooled to .137/.214/.296 across 56 plate appearances through Sept. 18. That night at Tampa Bay he hit a 438-foot leadoff homer, according to CBS Sports. He went 0-for-5 Tuesday and 1-for-4 Wednesday, according to CBS Sports‘ game log.
Tracy has resisted singling out Anthony during cold stretches.
“It’s not a Roman thing,” he said in May, as quoted by The Boston Globe.
Anthony wants the October he missed in 2025 with an oblique injury, and he said he is “where I want to be,” as quoted by The Boston Globe. The AL wild-card series opens Tuesday.
Anthony remains active and available off the bench. Any appearance Thursday would likely come as a pinch hitter, a role for his left-handed bat late in the game.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 24, 2026, 3:16 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) is missing a sixth straight game in Thursday's series finale against the visiting Cleveland Guardians, per MLB.com. Nick Sogard is making another start at first base and will bat out of the leadoff spot against Guardians right-hander Daniel Espino. Contreras was hit by a pitch on his right hand in last Thursday's game against the Texas Rangers. X-rays came back negative, but Boston has elected to give him some extra rest with the postseason starting next week. We would expect Contreras to return during this weekend's series at home against the Chicago Cubs. The four-time All-Star has hit a career-high 27 home runs while driving in 81 runs in 129 games across 533 plate appearances, but he has only played in four games in September after hitting only .217 (18-for-83) with three homers, 11 walks, and 26 strikeouts in 23 games in August. The Red Sox will need Contreras, who has been one of their most consistent hitters for the majority of the 2026 season, in top form if they want to make a deep playoff run.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
More Recent News
Sep 24, 2026, 3:16 PM ET
Miami Marlins infield prospect Jacob Lombard's first taste of professional baseball was a mixed bag while playing for Single-A Jupiter. The Marlins' fourth-ranked prospect hit four home runs, stole 11 bases, and registered a 13.1 percent walk rate in 22 games for the Hammerheads. He also propelled the team to the Florida State League playoffs (which they went on to win) by hitting a go-ahead home run with the team down to its final strike of the season, then went 5-for-14 (.357) with a pair of home runs during the playoffs. The downside was that he hit just .220 during the regular season, due largely to an astronomical 39.4 percent strikeout rate. If the 2026 first-round draft pick can make progress in that area next season, he should see time at High-A and perhaps even Double-A by season's end. At just 18 years old, it will be a few years before he debuts in the majors, but there is plenty of upside here to make him a worthy stash in dynasty leagues.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Ceddanne Rafaela Back in Boston's Lineup


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 3:10 PM ET
Boston Red Sox outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela (hamstring) is starting in center field and batting sixth for Thursday's series finale against the visiting Cleveland Guardians and right-hander Daniel Espino, according to MLB.com. Rafaela returned from a stay on the injured list due to a quadriceps injury but was pulled on Wednesday night against the Guardians with tightness in his hamstring. An MRI exam on Thursday morning apparently ruled out anything concerning, and the power/speed threat and starting center fielder is back in action for the final game of the series at Fenway Park. It is great news for the Red Sox, who did not want to head into the start of the postseason next week without their starting center fielder. The 26-year-old will now have four games to try to set a new career-high mark in home runs, as he enters Thursday's action with 16 homers, 70 RBI, 17 stolen bases, 67 runs scored, and a .284/.319/.444 slash line in 536 at-bats this year. Rafaela was a first-time All-Star this year in his third full season in the big leagues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 3:06 PM ET
Miami Marlins outfield prospect Cam Cannarella tore through the Miami farm system this season on his way to Triple-A, logging just 19 games at High-A, then only 34 at Double-A before earning the promotion to the minors' highest level. Although his strikeout rate spiked from 12.9 percent at the lower levels to 23.8 percent while at Jacksonville, the Marlins' sixth-ranked prospect maintained a strong walk rate of 14.1 percent and still hit .282 with an .813 OPS to go along with three home runs and 11 steals in 45 games with the Jumbo Shrimp. In all, he hit 15 home runs across all three levels, not bad for someone who doesn't have a highly rated power tool, so it's something to keep an eye on in 2027. If the 23-year-old can continue to produce home runs to go with his penchant for contact and a keen eye, not to mention his plus speed, there could be a valuable fantasy asset here who would be on the verge of making his MLB debut next year.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 2:55 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles outfield prospect Ike Irish (knee) was enjoying his first full season of professional baseball earlier this year while playing for High-A Fredericksburg. The former first-round draft pick had really heated up before a torn left meniscus ended his season in late July. The Orioles' fifth-ranked prospect batted .361 with nine doubles, a triple, seven home runs, and nine steals over his final 26 games before the injury. The hot stretch pushed his season-long slash line to .286/.388/.528 with 16 home runs and 20 steals in just 76 games for the Keys. The left-handed hitter recently returned to the diamond and will head to the Arizona Fall League to make up for lost time. As such, he should be fully healthy come spring and looks ready to spend much of the 2027 season at Double-A. He likely won't make his major league debut until 2028, but the 22-year-old has shown good contact, plenty of power, and an ability to steal bases despite not having a ton of speed, so his dynasty arrow is pointing way up for the potential to impact multiple fantasy categories.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Liam Doyle Finishes 2026 on a High Note


Jarod Rupp




Sep 24, 2026, 2:37 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals pitching prospect Liam Doyle capped off his 2026 season with a strong start in the Double-A Texas League Championship on Wednesday, allowing just one run (zero earned) on four hits and two walks while striking out six batters in five innings of work. It followed his earlier playoff start in which the left-hander gave up just one earned run on no hits and five walks while striking out eight batters in only 3 2/3 innings pitched. The former fifth-overall draft pick spent the entirety of the 2026 regular season at Double-A Springfield, recording a 3.76 ERA, 1.31 WHIP, and a 17.6 percent K-BB% in 23 starts (130 K in 103 IP). His performance this year puts the Cards' top pitching prospect on track for Triple-A in 2027 and a possible MLB debut at some point next year. If there is one criticism, it is that his walk rate remained elevated throughout the season, coming in at 12.5 percent, but so long as the 6-foot-2 hurler can keep striking out batters at a high clip, then it shouldn't get in the way of moving up the ladder. The 22-year-old remains a strong dynasty stash.--Jarod Rupp

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Red Sox's Jarren Duran Hits Surprise 20-20 Milestone With Mookie Betts
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The 2026 Major League Baseball season has been anything but smooth for Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran, but he still has found a way to put himself into some elite company. item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Major League Baseball season has been anything but smooth for Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran, but he still has found a way to put himself into some elite company.
Duran has taken a lot of heat all season to this point. He's batting .207 this season and striking out a lot and not walking much. In fact, Duran's 39 walks this season are his fewest since 2023. That year, he only played 102 games. This season, he has 147 games under his belt. He hasn't gotten on base a lot, but the power numbers have still been there. Duran has 20 homers on the season, which is one off from his career high of 21, which he set in his All-Star season in 2024. He has driven in 69 runs this year. Plus, despite the fact that he hasn't been on base much, he has still been a terror on the basepaths. On Wednesday, he recorded his 20th stolen base of the season.
Now, Duran has two 20-20 seasons under his belt and is just the third member of the organization, along with Mookie Betts and Jackie Jensen, to record multiple, per former Red Sox director of baseball communications and media relations JP Long.
"Jarren Duran (2024, ’26) joins Mookie Betts (2016, ’17, ’18) and Jackie Jensen (1954, ’59) as the only Red Sox to record multiple 20-HR/20-SB seasons," Long wrote. "Jarren and Mookie are the only Red Sox ever to record 3 consecutive seasons of at least 15 HR and 20 steals."
Who Saw That Coming?
Talk about improbable, huh?
The last time Duran had a 20-20 season, he was a 9.0-WAR player and finished the season with 21 homers, 75 RBIs, 34 stolen bases, 48 doubles, 14 triples and a .285/.342/.492 slash line. He was incredible and led the league in both doubles and triples.
The 2026 season hasn't been kind to him, but quietly he has still had an impact. He's slashing .207/.265/.364. If you look around the league and see numbers like those, you're not going to typically see 20 homers and 20 stolen bases as well. That doesn't make the .207 batting average any better, but it is a bit of a silver lining in an otherwise difficult season. The talent is there. There's no denying that. Boston has to find a way to get him back to the 2024 version of himself. But for now, this is something to celebrate.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Aroldis Chapman makes MLB history, becomes only relief pitcher to ever accomplish feat
item.dc:creator: Matt Larter
item.description: MLB history was made Wednesday night when Boston Red Sox relief pitcher Aroldis Chapman reached a milestone that no other reliever has ever accomplished. Chapman became the first relief pitcher in MLB history to record 1,400 career strikeouts when he struck out Cleveland Guardians outfielder Joe Adell in the top of the ninth inning. The 38-year-old then recorded two more strikeouts in the inning, bringing his career total to 1,402, as Boston secured a 1-0 victory. Chapman continues to rewrite th
item.content:encoded:
MLB history was made Wednesday night when Boston Red Sox relief pitcher Aroldis Chapman reached a milestone that no other reliever has ever accomplished.
Chapman became the first relief pitcher in MLB history to record 1,400 career strikeouts when he struck out Cleveland Guardians outfielder Joe Adell in the top of the ninth inning. The 38-year-old then recorded two more strikeouts in the inning, bringing his career total to 1,402, as Boston secured a 1-0 victory.
Chapman continues to rewrite the record books
Chapman had already established himself as the all-time leader in strikeouts among relief pitchers earlier this season. On July 3, he surpassed Hall of Famer Hoyt Wilhelm, who finished his career with 1,363 strikeouts and now sits second on the list.
Wednesday’s appearance was Chapman’s first for Boston since Sept. 13, and he immediately delivered a dominant performance. He struck out all three batters he faced in the ninth inning on just 12 pitches, earning his 35th save of the season.
The save also marked the 10th season of Chapman’s 16-year career in which he has recorded at least 30 saves.
Chapman has been a major contributor to Boston’s bullpen throughout the season. He has recorded 71 strikeouts across 53 appearances, posting a 1.92 ERA and 1.12 WHIP. He has also reached at least 70 strikeouts in a season 13 times during his career.
Red Sox prepare for postseason
Chapman’s historic season comes as the Red Sox enter the final days of the regular season and look towards the postseason.
Boston sits at 85-73 and currently holds the second American League Wild Card position, four games ahead of the Chicago White Sox, who are 81-77.
The Red Sox have four games remaining. They will finish their three-game series against the Guardians on Thursday before closing out the regular season with three games against the Chicago Cubs over the weekend.
With Boston battling for a playoff spot, Chapman will likely remain an important part of the team’s late-inning plans. After adding another remarkable achievement to his résumé, the veteran reliever enters the final stretch of the season as MLB’s only pitcher to reach 1,400 strikeouts exclusively as a reliever.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have just four games left in the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season and the fanbase will not be seeing Garrett Crochet on the hill before it wraps up. While this is the case, there is still hope for a postseason return.
The two-time All-Star has been building up and throwing bullpens with the hope of returning in a bullpen role for Boston's playoff push. Crochet's most recent bullpen came on Tuesday — and was the most exciting one yet. Crochet topped out at 96 miles per hour with his fastball and faced live hitters for the first time since May. On Wednesday, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy confirmed that Crochet will not pitch in the regular season, but is likely to throw another bullpen over the weekend and wouldn't rule him out for the Wild Card round, which begins on Sep. 29, as transcribed by MassLive.com's Chris Cotillo.
Don't Count Out Garrett Crochet Yet
"Doesn’t necessarily void him for the Wild Card, but the conversations around that are deep in a lot of ways," Tracy said. "It could change a playoff roster. What is he able to give you? Can he give you two games? Can he give you multiple innings? Can he go back-to-back? All of those questions have to be answered, not only for his own health but for our team and what puts us in the best position."
If you're a Red Sox fan hoping to see Crochet again in 2026, don't give up hope. The fact that Crochet isn't going to pitch in a regular season isn't a negative update in the slightest. In early September, Tim Healey of The Boston Globe reported that Crochet was "tracking toward being ready for the first round" despite not being expected to pitch in a game beforehand. So, the fact that Crochet isn't expected to pitch in one of the club's final four regular season games isn't necessarily new information.
The important thing to think about here is the progression of the big lefty. He faced live hitters for the first time in months on Tuesday. He looked good and said afterward that he thought that he could get outs in a game right now for Boston if he threw like that again. If he feels like himself, that's more important than getting into Game 162. He's pitched enough in the big leagues and the coaches and front office have been tracking him enough to know where he's at. The Red Sox aren't going to put Crochet on the mound in a playoff game if they don't think he can be himself.
So far, there haven't been updates pointing in that direction. There are playoff roster questions to think about, who would come off the roster to put him on. But that's a good problem to have and is a sign of how good Boston's bullpen is. If Crochet is himself, he makes Boston better. The Wild Card round begins on Sep. 29. Crochet still has a shot to be there.

Chapman holds the record for the fastest pitch thrown in the Statcast era at 105.8 mph. He also holds the No. 2 spot with a 105.7 mph pitch. Chapman is ninth all-time in saves and has more strikeouts than any reliever in the history of baseball. Chapman has left his mark on the game, and the 38-year-old is still playing like an All-Star. Chapman has been around for a while, so there's not much he hasn
item.content:encoded:
Aroldis Chapman has made a name for himself by lighting up the radar gun throughout his career.
Chapman holds the record for the fastest pitch thrown in the Statcast era at 105.8 mph. He also holds the No. 2 spot with a 105.7 mph pitch. Chapman is ninth all-time in saves and has more strikeouts than any reliever in the history of baseball. Chapman has left his mark on the game, and the 38-year-old is still playing like an All-Star.
Chapman has been around for a while, so there's not much he hasn't seen. However, he, like everyone else, is in awe of Jacob Misiorowski. Chapman's fastball has been one of the best pitches in baseball for years, but to see that kind of velocity from a starter is special.
"He's unbelievable," said Chapman, per The Athletic's Jayson Stark. "I love to watch him."
The third fastest pitch thrown in the Statcast era belongs to Ben Joyce, at 105.5 mph. However, this year, Misiorowski tied him with a 105.5 mph fastball to Pete Crow-Armstrong. It is the fastest pitch ever recorded by a starting pitcher in the Statcast era.
Chapman has been amazing fans with his velocity for years, but now there's a player who's able to match him on the radar gun as a starter. What makes Misiorowski so impressive is the fact that he maintains his velocity late into games. While Chapman comes in for an inning and blows his fastball by hitters for one inning, Misiorowski is doing it for six innings every five days.

El relevista cubano Aroldis Chapman alcanzó un nuevo salvamento este miércoles en la temporada 2026 de Grandes Ligas (MLB) con los Red Sox de Boston. El holguinero enfrentó a los bateadores de los Cleveland Guardians y propinó tres ponches para superar los 1400 ponches en su carrera.
Chapman participó en el triunfo de Boston 1-0 sobre Cleveland en Fenway Park, con una asistencia de 36 mil 360 aficionados. Chapman subió al montículo en la parte alta del noveno episodio para asegurar el éxito de su conjunto.
Aroldis Chapman se apuntó el juego salvado 35 de la temporada
El experimentado relevista cubano enfrentó a tres bateadores tras sustituir a Garrett Whitlock en esa entrada. Chapman retiró por la vía de los strikes a sus rivales y se apuntó tres ponches para llegar a 71 en la actual temporada. De igual forma, sumó su 35.º juego salvado de la campaña en 37 oportunidades. Su efectividad descansa hasta el momento en 1.92 ERA.
Por otra parte, Chapman alcanzó en el juego una velocidad máxima de 99 mph y utilizó 12 lanzamientos, de los cuales 10 terminaron en strikes. Para Chapman no fue otro salvamento más, ni mucho menos un strikeout más a sus registros. El antillano alcanzó los 1400 ponches contra Jo Adell y se convirtió en el primer pitcher con 400 juegos salvados y 1400 ponches. Simplemente Chapman es un jugador digno de admirar. Su carrera es un ejemplo de disciplina, constancia y éxito.
El misil cubano va rumbo a otra postemporada. Será su décima aparición en playoffs, la segunda consecutiva con Boston. Chapman, que acumula dos anillos de Serie Mundial con los Cubs y Rangers, volverá a octubre para aportar al objetivo de los Medias Rojas en esta instancia de competición. En nueve playoffs acumula 11 salvamentos y 73 ponches en 51.2 innings de labor.

item.content:encoded:
Aroldis Chapman regresó este miércoles a un montículo de las Grandes Ligas (MLB, por sus siglas en inglés) y el momento no pudo ser más propicio. El cubano lanzó por primera vez en casi dos semanas, tras lidiar con una lesión en el dorsal ancho, y selló con tres ponches el triunfo de los Medias Rojas de Boston sobre los Guardianes de Cleveland con ajustada pizarra de 1-0.
El holguinero de 38 años se había presentado por última vez el pasado 13 de septiembre y, tras el recomendado descanso, disparó 12 veces al plato —con velocidad cercana a las 98 millas por hora—, 10 de ellas en la zona de strike, para liquidar por esa vía a los tres bateadores enfrentados.
El primer pulso lo sostuvo con Jo Adell, quien llegó registrado como la víctima del ponche 1400 de su exitosa trayectoria, lo que le convierte en el único relevista en alcanzar y superar luego esa barrera, con los recetados a Ángel Martínez y Ángel Genao.
“Me siento saludable”, dijo el zurdo en español. Explicó que la molestia ya desapareció y que su única preocupación era el control, un aspecto en el que salió satisfecho. En el mismo sentido se expresó el estratega Chad Tracy, acaba de terminar su paso interino al firmar el contrato que lo declara oficialmente como el mánager de la franquicia de Massachusetts.
Así, el Misil Cubano firmó otro hito en la brillante campaña de 2026. El pasado 3 de julio, en Anaheim, Chapman superó a Hoyt Wilhelm como líder histórico -por más de medio siglo- en ponches para un relevista, al llegar a 1364 frente a Denzer Guzman.
El 6 de septiembre llegó otro peldaño: se convirtió en el noveno lanzador de la historia con 400 salvamentos y cerró el juego con una recta de 101 mph ante Baltimore.
Además, fue seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas por novena vez, dato que habla de la solidez de una carrera a lo largo de 17 campañas, desde que debutó en 2010 con los Rojos de Cincinnati, y que incluye el paso por los Yankees de Nueva York, Cachorros de Chicago, Reales de Kansas City, Rangers de Texas y Piratas de Pittsburgh.
En ese periplo, su brazo cambió la forma de medir la velocidad en el béisbol. El 24 de septiembre de 2010, en su año de novato, lanzó una bola a 105.8 mph, la más rápida registrada desde que existe el rastreo de lanzamientos en 2008.
Sus números de por vida son contundentes: efectividad de 2.49 y 402 salvamentos en 916, a lo que se añade un balance de 63 victorias y 52 derrotas, de acuerdo con las estadísticas oficiales.
De Boston a Cooperstown
A la par de sus estadísticas históricas marchan las de la campaña en curso, en la que ha lanzado 51.2 entradas y rescatado 35 partidos, además de archivar tres éxitos y cuatro fracasos, junto a una efectividad de 1.92 carreras limpias por juego y 71 ponches.
Ese despliegue sostiene en buena medida las grandes posibilidades de que los Medias Rojas cuenten con sus servicios para 2027 —a cambio de 13 millones de dólares como establece la cláusula—, más allá de lo que suceda en la inminente postemporada.
Sobre su futuro, el veloz zurdo ha reiterado varias veces que seguirá mientras pueda hacer el trabajo. A pesar de su longevidad, ha demostrado que su recta se mantiene cerca de las 100 mph, algo poco común al máximo nivel.
Sea cual sea su destino, las opciones de convertirse en miembro del Salón de la Fama de Cooperstown son más fuertes que nunca. En su poder tendrá por buen tiempo el récord de ponches para relevistas, más de 400 salvamentos, nueve Juegos de Estrellas y dos anillos de campeón de la Serie Mundial.
El recinto ya abrió sus puertas a cerradores como Mariano Rivera y Trevor Hoffman, y este año incorporó a Billy Wagner, quien firmó 422 rescates, cifra que Chapman podría alcanzar si sigue activo un par de temporadas más.
Por ahora, su enfoque se centra en el calendario de octubre. Los Medias Rojas aseguraron su boleto como comodín y Chapman lanzará la próxima semana contra los Yankees, el equipo con que escaló a la cima en el béisbol más exigente del planeta.

item.title: [MLB.com] Durbin finally meets Pedroia and it's kind of a big deal
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne
item.description: BOSTON -- In a meet-and-greet a couple of years in the making, Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin at last had the thrill of meeting Dustin Pedroia before Wednesday’s game against the Guardians at Fenway Park. For Durbin, this was no small thing. And no pun intended. Yes, Durbin is drawn to Red Sox Hall of Famer Pedroia because of the way he overcame his lack of size to become an iconic player for Boston. But that is just one of the reasons. “Just the way he went about his business,” said Durbin.
item.content:encoded:
BOSTON -- In a meet-and-greet a couple of years in the making, Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin at last had the thrill of meeting Dustin Pedroia before Wednesday’s game against the Guardians at Fenway Park.
For Durbin, this was no small thing. And no pun intended.
Yes, Durbin is drawn to Red Sox Hall of Famer Pedroia because of the way he overcame his lack of size to become an iconic player for Boston. But that is just one of the reasons.
“Just the way he went about his business,” said Durbin. “From things as far as just how he played the game on the field to how he acted off the field, the way he battled through things is something I wanted to model my game around.”
For Pedroia, who lives in Arizona, it was his first trip to Fenway this season. And not a moment too soon for Durbin, who joined the Red Sox in a trade from the Brewers in February.
When Durbin was with the Brewers, his manager was Pat Murphy, who coached Pedroia at Arizona State.
Murphy long wanted to connect the two, but the timing never worked.
After Durbin finished infield work on Wednesday, he spotted Pedroia in street clothes a little bit in front of Boston’s dugout.
Durbin struck up the nerve to talk to Pedroia, and the two exchanged pleasantries for a few minutes. The mutual respect was obvious.
“He’s a great guy. He’s a legend around here,” Durbin said. “Any time you get to rub shoulders with a guy like that, it only makes you better. Just a cool moment for me.”
In Durbin, Pedroia sees a kindred spirit.
“Durb’s the man,” said Pedroia. “He plays hard. He’s a grinder. He had a slow start, but you know how it is. It’s a full season. I think he’s coming into his own and the fans are seeing who he truly is.”
A little while before Durbin sidled up to Pedroia for a conversation, Boston’s former star second baseman crashed the team hitters' meeting.
“He was joking around with us and being serious at times,” Durbin said. “It’s good to have a guy like that around the guys, around the clubhouse. Lightens the mood up a little bit at this time of the year and good to have him around.”
Considering that Durbin went to a Division 3 college (Washington University in St. Louis) and Pedroia was a standout player at a Division 1 powerhouse at Arizona State, Durbin was a far bigger underdog to get to the Major Leagues than the man he admires so much.
But both players know what it is like to be undersold by scouts and evaluators because of their lack of size.
While Durbin has established himself as an everyday player for contending teams the last two seasons, Pedroia set a high bar by winning the AL Rookie of the Year and MVP in his first two years in the Majors.
In the first two months of the '26 season, Durbin slumped mightily,
bringing back memories of Pedroia’s slow start in '07 before he rallied to win that Rookie of the Year Award, not to mention his first of three World Series championship titles he helped lead the Red Sox to.
Much like Pedroia 19 years ago, Durbin kept his head down and kept working when things were at their toughest. He said he didn’t get texts from Pedroia when he was struggling, nor did he expect to.
“I think he knows how tough this game is,” Durbin said of Pedroia. “Sometimes the best thing is to just let it be. I think he has a pretty good idea -- just from communication with Murph and other mutual coaches and friends -- the type of guy I am, and I don’t think he was too worried about me.”
When the Red Sox went on a 32-5 surge from June 25 to Aug. 7, Durbin had several of the team’s most memorable hits, including a go-ahead homer off Cam Schlittler and a walk-off single to cap a 12-11 thriller over the White Sox in 13 innings on Aug. 6.
To Durbin, Wednesday’s chance meeting with his baseball idol matched his on-field highlights from earlier in the summer.
“It’s super cool. I’ve had some communication with him. Obviously seeing him in person, it’s pretty surreal,” Durbin said.

item.title: [meridiano.net] MLB: ¡Rumbo a Cooperstown! Aroldis Chapman hace historia con 1.400 ponches
item.dc:creator: Humberto Mendoza
item.description: Aroldis Chapman volvió a ser protagonista con Boston Red Sox y escribió una nueva página en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El lanzador cubano apareció en el noveno inning del triunfo 1-0 sobre Cleveland Guardians y no solamente aseguró la victoria de los patirrojos, sino que alcanzó una cifra inédita entre los relevistas. Con tres ponches consecutivos, el veterano llegó a 1.400 abanicados de por vida en MLB, convirtiéndose en el primer relevista que alcanza dicha cantidad. Su increíble labor
item.content:encoded:
Aroldis Chapman volvió a ser protagonista con Boston Red Sox y escribió una nueva página en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El lanzador cubano apareció en el noveno inning del triunfo 1-0 sobre Cleveland Guardians y no solamente aseguró la victoria de los patirrojos, sino que alcanzó una cifra inédita entre los relevistas.
Con tres ponches consecutivos, el veterano llegó a 1.400 abanicados de por vida en MLB, convirtiéndose en el primer relevista que alcanza dicha cantidad. Su increíble labor frente a los Guardianes también le permitió lograr su salvamento 35 de la campaña, en la jornada de este miércoles 23 de septiembre desde el Fenway Park.
El momento histórico llegó en el enfrentamiento contra Jo Adell. Chapman utilizó un splitter de 91.6 millas por hora para conseguir el ponche número 1.400 de su carrera y ampliar todavía más su legado como uno de los grandes relevistas de la historia. Después de ese turno, el cubano continuó dominando a Cleveland y también retiró por la vía de los strikes a Angel Martínez y Angel Genao, completando una entrada perfecta en apenas 12 lanzamientos.
Aroldis Chapman se consolida como futuro inmortal a Cooperstown
La actuación también le permitió sumar su salvamento 35 de la temporada y el número 402 de su trayectoria, cifra que lo mantiene entre los principales cerradores de todos los tiempos. Además, el taponero de Holguín se encuentra empatado con David Bednar en el tercer lugar de la Liga Americana en rescates. A sus 38 años, el zurdo atraviesa una campaña en la que registra efectividad de 1.92, WHIP de 1.12 y 71 ponches en 51.2 innings de trabajo.
El histórico registro llega después de una temporada en la que Chapman ya había superado a Hoyt Wilhelm como el relevista con más ponches en la historia de MLB, al dejar atrás los 1.363 abanicados del legendario lanzador. Ahora, el cubano suma otra marca exclusiva a su carrera y se prepara para afrontar la Postemporada con Boston. Tras su presentación ante Cleveland, el propio Chapman aseguró que se encuentra físicamente bien y que espera realizar una salida más para llegar preparado al béisbol de octubre.

item.content:encoded:
With the coming nor’easter hitting town this weekend, the Red Sox and Guardians have played with an October chill in the air this week.
The Red Sox halted their three-game slide with a 1-0 win on Wednesday. Andrew Monasterio’s RBI single in the bottom of the sixth held as the eventual winner after Sonny Gray dealt six shutout innings.
That came after the Guardians won Tuesday’s contest, 3-2, setting up Thursday’s game as the series rubber match.
Given his postgame comments, the Red Sox hope to have avoided a scare regarding center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who left his first game back from the injured list with right hamstring tightness. A quad injury sent him to the IL on Sept. 3.
“Not even close,” Rafaela said of the severity comparison of the two injuries. “I think it was just a cramp.”
After the game, Tracy said Rafaela would have an MRI exam on Thursday.
Ranger Suarez will start for the Red Sox on Thursday. He’s 1-1 with a 4.00 ERA in four career appearances, including three starts, against Cleveland. On May 31, he struck out 10 and allowed four runs across five frames against Cleveland in Boston’s 9-4 win.
“He’s a very good competitor, a good pitcher that even when he gets traffic, you trust that he’s going to find his way through it,” Tracy said of Suarez, whose ERA in three September starts is 0.92.
Daniel Espino will open for Cleveland before giving way to Joey Cantillo.
Here’s a preview of Thursday’s action.
Lineups
GUARDIANS (82-76): TBA
Pitching: RHP Daniel Espino (0-0, 4.73 ERA)
RED SOX (85-73): TBA
Pitching: LHP Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA)
Time: 6:45 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Guardians vs. Suarez: Jo Adell 2-5, Travis Bazzana 0-3, Chase DeLauter 2-3, David Fry 4-5, Austin Hedges 1-4, Steven Kwan 1-6, Nathaniel Lowe 1-6, Angel Martínez 0-2, José Ramírez 5-8, Brayan Rocchio 1-2
Red Sox vs. Espino: Has not faced any Boston batters
Stat of the day: The Red Sox have notched an American League-leading 17 shutouts this season.
Notes: The Guardians are on the verge of sealing their postseason berth. Cleveland’s magic number is just one, the same as their AL Central rival, the White Sox. If both win on Thursday, they both will earn a postseason berth. ... Cleveland, which had a six-game winning streak snapped on Wednesday, has a one-game lead over Chicago in the race for the division title. The White Sox own the division tiebreaker. ... “We know we control our own destiny still,” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “So, I like where we are. We’ve got four games left, and we have a chance to get in. That’s all you can ask for.” ... Espino will serve as an opener for Cantillo, who will pitch in a bulk role. Cantillo is 10-9 with a 3.74 ERA this season. ... Cantillo is 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in eight career innings against the Red Sox, and Espino has never faced Boston.
Cam Kerry can be reached at cam.kerry@globe.com.

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON (AP) — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia's Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians' six-game winning streak.
It was just the fifth win in 13 games for the Red Sox, who clinched a playoff spot on Sunday.
The 36-year-old Gray (18-5) is in line to become the fourth Red Sox pitcher since 2000 to lead the AL in victories, joining Rick Porcello (2016), Josh Beckett ('07) and Curt Schilling ('04).
Gray allowed four singles, struck out three, walked one and lowered his ERA to 2.72.
Aroldis Chapman struck out the side in the ninth for his 35th save of the season.
Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) gave up a run on 10 hits with seven strikeouts.
The Guardians entered with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the AL Central after winning the series opener Tuesday, but needed a win Wednesday combined with a loss by either the Rangers or Astros to clinch a postseason berth.
The victory came with a price for the Red Sox when center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela left with right hamstring tightness after running out a single the same day he was activated from the injured list. He had been sidelined with a right a quad strain since Sept. 3 and made a diving headlong grab on Steven Kwan, the game's first batter.
