item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox lost 3-2 to the Guardians on Tuesday night at Fenway Park. The game was tied heading into the ninth inning. It did not stay that way for long.
Erik Miller entered to protect the tie and hit Chase DeLauter to start the inning. Two batters later, Nathaniel Lowe lifted a sacrifice fly that brought DeLauter home with the go-ahead run. Miller threw 22 pitches. Ten were strikes. The Guardians had their lead, and the Red Sox had another loss.
It was the fourth consecutive outing in which Miller has allowed at least one run. After the game, the left-hander did not sugarcoat where things stand.
Miller’s Patience Is Running Thin
Miller was asked about his recent stretch and whether his patience with himself was wearing down. He did not dodge the question.
“It’s definitely running thin at this point,” Miller said. “I’d be lying if I said otherwise…I would like to have been through this by now, be over it.”
In September, Miller has posted an 8.53 ERA and a 2.37 WHIP. He has recorded one clean inning in seven appearances. For a pitcher who spent the summer as one of the most reliable left-handed setup arms in the American League, the slide has been sudden.
Miller said after the game that he has been working through a mechanical issue that he has not been able to shake. The frustration is compounded by the reality that the only way to fix it is to keep pitching in live situations. There is no shortcut. The regular season has five games left, and the postseason starts a week from Tuesday.
Tracy Still Believes in the Stuff
Manager Chad Tracy acknowledged the struggles but offered a different read on Tuesday’s outing.
“I thought today was even another step in the right direction,” Tracy said.
Tracy plans to get Miller into a couple more games before the regular season ends Sunday. The idea is to give him every opportunity to find the command before the Wild Card Series begins on September 29. Tracy said after the game that the trust in Miller’s raw ability has not changed, even as the results have gone sideways. The stuff is not the problem. The location is.
Final Word for the Red Sox
Erik Miller is not hiding from this. He knows the numbers. He knows the stakes. He is frustrated with himself and not pretending otherwise.
The stuff is still there. The command is not. Five days remain to find it.
Miller’s patience may be running thin. The Red Sox’ belief in him has not wavered. Whether those two things can meet in the middle before October will go a long way toward determining how far this team can go.

item.dc:creator: Clark Dalton
item.description: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is recovering quickly after a scary injury. Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after a foul ball off the bat of first baseman Michael Busch hit him while he was standing in the on-deck circle during Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday. Luckily for the Cubs, the injury won't require surgery. Even better for Chicago, he could return to the lineup soon. Counsell spoke with the media Tuesday before the Cubs faced the Miami Marlins in t
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is recovering quickly after a scary injury.
Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after a foul ball off the bat of first baseman Michael Busch hit him while he was standing in the on-deck circle during Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday. Luckily for the Cubs, the injury won't require surgery. Even better for Chicago, he could return to the lineup soon.
Counsell spoke with the media Tuesday before the Cubs faced the Miami Marlins in the first of their three-game homestand. The skipper said Bregman is in a "good place" and they're not placing him on the injured list. Counsell added Bregman may return for the final week of the regular season. (Entering Tuesday, the National League Central squad had six games remaining.)
Cubs president Jed Hoyer, meanwhile, exercised more caution when discussing Bregman's status. The executive said he wants to see how the third baseman responds to increased activity before reinserting him into the lineup. Taking a close look at Bregman's face explains why Hoyer remains ultracareful.
Craig Counsell announced that Alex Bregman will not be placed on the injured list. pic.twitter.com/3aoA8f6RWs
— Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) September 22, 2026
Jed Hoyer Addresses the Alex Bregman Injury and Next Steps pic.twitter.com/nA3GDTeukj
— CHGO Cubs (@CHGO_Cubs) September 22, 2026
Bregman arrived at Wrigley Field before the Cubs played the Marlins. His left eye was still bruised and his face swollen, but he's in better shape than he was on Sunday. Shortly after suffering the injury, the infielder shared a selfie on his Instagram story. His eye was swollen shut and his face bloodied.
Expect Bregman to put plenty of ice packs on his face over the next few days as he aims to return promptly. When he does, the three-time All-Star could be an instant difference-maker for a Cubs team hoping to make noise in the postseason. Chicago (87-69) can no longer win the division after the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) clinched it, but it could secure one of three NL wild-card seeds. The team is in a chaotic race with the San Diego Padres (87-69), Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) and Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74). (All records were entering Tuesday.)
Assuming the Cubs grab one of those spots, Bregman, a proven postseason performer, should then deliver in October. The two-time World Series champion slashed .239/.349/.442 on 380 postseason at-bats in his first eight seasons with the Houston Astros and Boston Red Sox.
Bregman could produce more postseason magic after slashing .262/.352/.452 on his first 600 at-bats for the Cubs this season. If he does, Chicago will be even more thrilled that his injury was less severe than initially anticipated.

item.title: [tsn.ca] Marlins stymie Cubs’ push for NL wild card with victory
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.description: CHICAGO (AP) — Griffin Conine drove in Esteury Ruiz with a tiebreaking single in Miami's six-run 12th inning, and the Marlins stymied Chicago's push for an NL wild card with an 8-2 victory over the Cubs on Tuesday night. item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO (AP) — Griffin Conine drove in Esteury Ruiz with a tiebreaking single in Miami's six-run 12th inning, and the Marlins stymied Chicago's push for an NL wild card with an 8-2 victory over the Cubs on Tuesday night.
Conine put Miami ahead to stay with his well-placed blooper to left field. Jakob Marsee added a run-scoring single, and Joe Mack capped the outburst with a two-run single.
Kyle Stowers hit a solo homer for the Marlins (77-80), who had lost three in a row. Josh Ekness (3-4) pitched a scoreless inning for the win.
The Cubs (87-70) could have clinched a playoff berth with a win or an Arizona loss, but the Diamondbacks won 7-2 at Colorado.
Chicago, San Diego and Philadelphia are tied atop the wild-card standings for all three NL spots. The Phillies posted a 6-4 victory over Milwaukee on Tuesday night, and the Padres lost 7-0 to the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Cubs had a chance to win the game in the 10th, loading the bases with two down. But Miami second baseman Javier Sanoja robbed Pedro Ramírez of a game-ending single with a terrific sliding stop.
Caleb Thielbar (3-4) was charged with the loss.
Chicago played without third baseman Alex Bregman, who is recovering from multiple facial fractures after he was struck in the face by a foul ball. The three-time All-Star could return to the lineup before the end of the regular season this weekend.
Miami jumped in front when Stowers doubled and scored on Agustín Ramírez's single in the fourth. Stowers added his 20th homer in the sixth.
Chicago rallied in the bottom half, putting runners on the corners with no outs. Michael Busch then hit a hard grounder to first, but Mack mishandled Deyvison De Los Santos' throw to the plate and Pete Crow-Armstrong scampered home with the Cubs' first run. One batter later, Ian Happ hit a tying single off Calvin Faucher.
Up next
Ryan Gusto (1-5, 4.14 ERA) starts for Miami on Wednesday night, and fellow right-hander Kevin Gausman (9-12, 4.55) pitches for Chicago.
___

Jay Cohen, The Associated Press

item.dc:creator: Scott Martin
item.description: BOSTON — Nathaniel Lowe had a tiebreaking sacrifice fly off reliever Erik Miller in the ninth inning, and the Cleveland Guardians maintained their slim in the AL Central with a 3-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night. Angel Martínez had three hits for the Guardians, who entered the day with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the division. Chicago owns the tiebreaker by winning the season series. Cleveland stranded 15 baserunners. The loss was Boston’s eighth in 12 games, spoili
item.content:encoded:
BOSTON — Nathaniel Lowe had a tiebreaking sacrifice fly off reliever Erik Miller in the ninth inning, and the Cleveland Guardians maintained their slim in the AL Central with a 3-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night.
Angel Martínez had three hits for the Guardians, who entered the day with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the division. Chicago owns the tiebreaker by winning the season series. Cleveland stranded 15 baserunners.
The loss was Boston’s eighth in 12 games, spoiling Chad Tracy’s first game as manager after the club named him its 49th in team history.
Adley Rutschman added three hits for Boston, which clinched one of the AL’s wild-card spots on Sunday.
Boston pinch hitter Mickey Gasper hit Hunter Gaddis’ first pitch, tying it at 2-2 leading off the eighth.
Gaddis (5-3) got the win and Cade Smith recorded the final three outs for his 40th save.
Miller (4-2) hit a batter and gave up two hits in an inning.
A strong candidate for the AL Rookie of the Year, Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick gave up a run over five innings. He lowered his ERA to 2.55 and is on pace to become the fourth rookie starting pitcher in MLB history with an ERA under 2.60 and averaging 9.0 or more strikeouts per nine innings.
In his tune-up for a likely playoff start next week, Boston lefty Payton Tolle struggled with his control over 5 2/3 innings, giving up two runs on eight hits.
Up next
Guardians LHP Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67 ERA) is set to face Red Sox RHP Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.82) on Wednesday in the middle game of the three-game series.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 07:35 GMT+10

(Photo credit: David Butler II)
Nathaniel Lowe hit a sacrifice fly to right field that drove in Chase DeLauter in the ninth inning and the visiting Cleveland Guardians held on to beat the Boston Red Sox 3-2 Tuesday in the first game of a three-game series.
Boston's Erik Miller (4-2) walked one and allowed two hits in the ninth.
Hunter Gaddis (5-3) got the win despite allowing a game-tying home run to Mickey Gasper in the eighth. Cade Smith pitched a scoreless ninth to record his 40th save. The victory extended Cleveland's winning streak to six games as it maintained its one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox in the AL Central.
Parker Messick held Boston to one run on five hits in five innings. He struck out five and walked one. Messick has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his last 14 starts.
Payton Tolle started for the Red Sox (84-73) and gave up two runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings. He walked two and struck out five.
Adley Rutschman had three hits for the Red Sox, who had eight hits in the game.
Cleveland's Angel Martinez went 3-for-4 and scored a run. The Guardians (82-75) received two hits from DeLauter, who reached in the ninth when Miller hit him with a pitch.
The Guardians went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 15.
The Guardians took a 2-0 lead in the second. Martinez doubled and made it 1-0 when he scored on David Fry's single. Fry doubled the lead by scoring when Brayan Rocchio grounded into a 4-6-3 double play.
Boston trimmed its deficit to 2-1 in the second. Rutschman led off with a double, moved to third on Caleb Durbin's groundout to second and scored on Andrew Monasterio's groundout to shortstop.
Gasper's home run, his 10th of the year, tied the game leading off the eighth.
Boston stranded the tying run on second in the ninth as Smith retired Nick Sogard on a grounder to second.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Postseason secured, but Red Sox trending in wrong direction and Guardians take advantage to open series - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Tim Healey
item.description: In this purgatorial period for the Red Sox, after they clinched a playoff berth over the weekend and before they open the postseason next week, what matters? The result Tuesday, a 3-2 loss to the Guardians at Fenway Park, was not of major significance. Of greater note was the how — and what those trends may portend heading into the most important time of year: another ugly outing for reliever Erik Miller, and another night of minimal hitting for the lineup. The Red Sox (84-73) have dropped three
item.content:encoded:
In this purgatorial period for the Red Sox, after they clinched a playoff berth over the weekend and before they open the postseason next week, what matters?
The result Tuesday, a 3-2 loss to the Guardians at Fenway Park, was not of major significance.
Of greater note was the how — and what those trends may portend heading into the most important time of year: another ugly outing for reliever Erik Miller, and another night of minimal hitting for the lineup.
The Red Sox (84-73) have dropped three games in a row and eight of their past 12.
“We’ve still got five games to play, and you [have to] keep guys out there and engaged and ready to roll,” manager Chad Tracy said. “I told the guys before, we earned the right to be in position to be able to line things up. That being said, we still want to go out and win the games. We had a chance to tonight.”
Miller inherited a tied game in the ninth inning and struggled again, allowing a game-deciding run and throwing 22 pitches (10 strikes). He hit his first batter, Chase DeLauter, with a pitch. DeLauter eventually scored on Nathaniel Lowe’s sacrifice fly. Altogether, Miller yielded two hits and a walk.
In September, the Sox’ theoretical top lefthanded setup man has one clean inning in seven attempts, a 8.53 ERA, and a 2.37 WHIP.
Miller said his patience with himself — and a mechanical issue he is trying to fix — is “definitely running thin at this point.”
“I’d be lying if I say otherwise,” he said. “I would like to have been through this by now, be over it. But … there’s no way I can feel better and work through it without throwing [in] a game. So that’s just how it’s going to have to be: keep throwing, get through it.”
Tracy, noting that Miller will pitch in a couple more games before the regular season ends Sunday, added: “I thought today was even another step in the right direction.”
Offensively, the Red Sox had few highlights. Mickey Gasper launched a pinch-hit tying home run off setup man Hunter Gaddis to lead off the eighth, but the Sox totaled nine runners stranded on base and went 0 for 9 with men in scoring position.
In the positives column: Adley Rutschman finished 3 for 4, with two doubles (and a line out to deep center) coming against lefthanders.
Entering the game, Rutschman was 2 for 26 with no extra-base hits against lefties as a member of the Red Sox.
“Being a switch hitter has a lot that goes into it, and you go through phases where you’re hitting good [from] one side and not the other and it flip flops sometimes and then goes back,” Rutschman said. “I want to be in a good spot, especially with the playoffs coming up.”
In a matchup between perhaps the top two rookie pitchers this year, Payton Tolle (5⅔ innings, two runs) was almost equal to fellow lefthander Parker Messick (five innings, one run) of the Guardians.
Tolle slogged through a 22-pitch second frame, during which he allowed three hits and two walks but managed to hold the AL Central-leading Guardians (82-75) to the two runs.
When Tracy pulled him in the sixth, Tolle walked off the Fenway mound — for potentially the last time this year — to a standing ovation from the fans behind the home dugout. He waved back to them.
“I think he’s won them over pretty significantly,” Tracy said.
Tolle finished his rookie season with a 3.03 ERA and 171 strikeouts in 148⅔ innings (26 starts).
Up next: a start in the AL Wild Card Series.
“It’s the postseason. This is what we play for,” Tolle said. “But it is what it is. We go on, and we have a job to do.”
Tim Healey can be reached at timothy.healey@globe.com. Follow him @timbhealey.

item.dc:creator: Ian Browne
item.description: BOSTON -- When Payton Tolle walked off the mound with two outs in the top of the sixth inning on Tuesday night, it was the perfect opportunity for the Fenway faithful to recognize the power lefty for an outstanding rookie season. Next time Tolle pitches, the noise is likely to be even louder, and not nearly as favorable. item.content:encoded:
BOSTON -- When Payton Tolle walked off the mound with two outs in the top of the sixth inning on Tuesday night, it was the perfect opportunity for the Fenway faithful to recognize the power lefty for an outstanding rookie season.
Next time Tolle pitches, the noise is likely to be even louder, and not nearly as favorable.
The Red Sox will have no hesitation sending out the confident, charismatic 23-year-old into enemy territory.
While this was far from the best (5 2/3 innings, 8 hits, 2 ER, 2 BBs, 5 K’s) of Tolle’s 26 regular-season starts, it was more than enough to keep the Red Sox in the game.
Assuming Tolle doesn’t pitch again in the regular season, his final stat line includes this: A 3.03 ERA, 171 strikeouts, 40 walks, 1.10 WHIP and a .222 opponents batting average.
Playing short-handed without Willson Contreras (bruised knuckle, right hand), Ceddanne Rafaela (right quadriceps strain, 10-day IL) and Trevor Story (rest), the Red Sox continued their recent trend of not scoring much.
There were two bright spots.
Mickey Gasper came up as a pinch-hitter and hammered a game-tying solo shot to right in the bottom of the eighth.
Adley Rutschman, who had been slumping of late, belted two doubles as part of a three-hit night.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Erik Miller gives up lead in ninth as Red Sox lose third straight
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: For all intents and purposes, none of these last games down the stretch mean anything to the Red Sox. They have already punched their ticket to the playoffs and nothing that happens from here on out will change that. But while readying themselves for the games that matter, the Red Sox would still prefer to go into the postseason with some momentum, and Tuesday’s performance was at times pretty hard to watch. Playing without three projected postseason starters, the Red Sox suffered a listless 3-2
item.content:encoded:
For all intents and purposes, none of these last games down the stretch mean anything to the Red Sox. They have already punched their ticket to the playoffs and nothing that happens from here on out will change that.
But while readying themselves for the games that matter, the Red Sox would still prefer to go into the postseason with some momentum, and Tuesday’s performance was at times pretty hard to watch.
Playing without three projected postseason starters, the Red Sox suffered a listless 3-2 loss in their series opener against the Cleveland Guardians. Despite a game-tying pinch hit home run by Mickey Gasper in the bottom of the eighth, the Red Sox gave the lead right back in the ninth, capping off a night riddled with poor decisions and uncharacteristic mistakes.
Reliever Erik Miller saw his struggles continue by allowing two hits, a walk, a hit batsman and the go-ahead sacrifice fly by Angel Martinez in the top of the ninth, and outside of Gasper and Adley Rutschman going 3 for 4 with two doubles and a run scored, there wasn’t much to write home about as the Red Sox suffered their third straight defeat.
Making his final start before the playoffs, Payton Tolle wasn’t as sharp as he would’ve hoped, but once again he gave the Red Sox a chance to win.
After posting a scoreless first, Tolle allowed two runs and five baserunners over the course of a challenging second inning. He started by giving up a leadoff double, had a soft grounder from David Fry deflect off his leg and into the outfield for an RBI single, and allowed another single and a walk to load the bases with nobody out.
Tolle was able to minimize the damage from there, allowing a second run to score on a double play ball by Brayan Rocchio before escaping the inning. He continued facing traffic for the rest of his outing but grinded his way into the sixth and departed to a standing ovation from the Fenway Park faithful.
Tolle finished with two runs allowed on eight hits, two walks and a hit batsman over 5 2/3 innings with five strikeouts. He fell one out short of recording another quality start, leaving him with 13 in 26 outings, and he ends his rookie year with a 3.03 ERA and 171 strikeouts in 148 2/3 innings.
The Red Sox got a run back in the bottom of the second after Adley Rutschman led off with a double and came around to score on an RBI groundout by Andruw Monasterio, but otherwise the bats struggled against Guardians rookie Parker Messick. The left-hander, who came into the game with a 2.57 ERA and projects as a possible AL Cy Young Award finalist, limited the Red Sox to one run on five hits over five innings.
One thing Boston was able to do was drive up the rookie’s pitch count, particularly in the fourth when Monasterio was able to work a 12-pitch walk. That helped force the lefty from the game after five, giving the Red Sox a chance to try their luck against Cleveland’s bullpen.
The Red Sox let a golden opportunity go to waste in the bottom of the sixth, leaving men at second and third, but Alec Gamboa kept it a one-run game in the top of the seventh despite the Guardians taking advantage of some sloppy baseball to get runners at second and third themselves with one out.
Cleveland’s Fry, who had already grounded into a fielder’s choice where the runner was thrown out at the plate earlier in the third inning, did so a second time for the second out of the seventh, and Gamboa struck out former No. 1 overall pick Travis Bazzana to end the inning.
Then, in the bottom of the eighth, Gasper struck for his 10th home run of the season, hitting the first pitch he saw from Guardians reliever Hunter Gaddis 390 feet to the right field stands.
The good vibes didn’t last long.
Miller, who had proven an impactful bullpen addition since his arrival at the trade deadline, saw his recent control issues continue with his latest ugly outing. The left-hander hit the first batter he faced, gave up the lead on a sacrifice fly by Martinez and eventually loaded the bases before getting a fly out to keep things from spiraling further.
Miller has now allowed six runs and six walks over his past 3 1/3 innings, a trend the Red Sox can’t afford to continue if he’s to remain a high-leverage option in the playoffs.

It seems they just about know exactly what seed they’ll have and who they’ll play as well. Yankees Will Likely
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are in the middle of a series with the Tampa Bay Rays, but they’ve already clinched a postseason spot, which is set to begin next week.
It seems they just about know exactly what seed they’ll have and who they’ll play as well.
One Tampa Bay win over New York would clinch the AL East for the Rays, which would then slot the Yankees as the top Wild Card team and, as of right now, have them hosting a best-of-three series against the Boston Red Sox next week.
Yankees Will Likely Be Without Judge
Prior to Tuesday’s doubleheader, Yankees manager Aaron Boone revealed that he does not expect Judge to return for the Wild Card series next week due to his calf injury.
He received an injection in his calf this week, and the diagnosis was a moderate calf strain.
“We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said.
Aaron Judge is likely out for the AL Wild Card Series vs. Boston. “We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Aaron Boone said.
Judge had a PPP injection in his right calf during the off-day.
— Bryan Hoch ⚾️ (@BryanHoch) September 22, 2026
This now makes it all the more important for the Yankees’ depleted offense to have their starting rotation hold down the fort, which it has done all season long, headlined by Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodon, Max Fried, and Will Warren.
Pedro Martinez Makes Suggestion for Yankees
One of the biggest questions facing the Yankees is how they plan to structure a shortened rotation come playoff time, and Hall of Fame pitcher and MLB on TBS analyst Pedro Martinez believes he knows exactly how they should use their core pitchers.
“For the Yankees’ pitching rotation, I’d go with Schlittler first, Rodon second, and Cole third,” Martinez posted on X.
For the Yankees’ pitching rotation, I’d go with Schlittler first, Rodón second, and Cole third. #mlbontbs
— Pedro Martinez (@45PedroMartinez) September 22, 2026
You’re not going to pitch all five starters. That’s just not realistic. With the potential for more off days, you’re going to want your best arms available.
While Schlittler is an obvious no-brainer. Boone will have to decide whether he wants to go with a three-man group or extend it to four and have both Rodon and Fried start, rather than moving one of them to the bullpen alongside Warren, which seems like the most likely outcome for now.

item.title: [Boston.com] Red Sox get good news as Garrett Crochet nears return for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Conor Ryan
item.description: Reinforcements might be on the way for the Red Sox ahead of a seemingly inevitable postseason rematch with the Yankees later this month. For the first time in close to four months, Red Sox ace Garrett Crochet faced a live hitter. He threw 16 pitches to Ceddanne Rafaela at Fenway Park in another encouraging step forward for the southpaw. Crochet, sidelined with several injuries, has not pitched in a game for Boston since April 25. While the 2025 American League Cy Young runner-up won’t be able to
item.content:encoded:
Reinforcements might be on the way for the Red Sox ahead of a seemingly inevitable postseason rematch with the Yankees later this month.
For the first time in close to four months, Red Sox ace Garrett Crochet faced a live hitter. He threw 16 pitches to Ceddanne Rafaela at Fenway Park in another encouraging step forward for the southpaw.
Crochet, sidelined with several injuries, has not pitched in a game for Boston since April 25.
While the 2025 American League Cy Young runner-up won’t be able to build back enough strength to rejoin Boston’s rotation for the playoffs, a clean bill of health for Crochet could make him a viable option as a power arm out of the bullpen.
“I would say the way that live [session] just went, that I could go get outs,” Crochet said after his appearance on the mound, per MLB.com’s Ian Browne. “It depends obviously what role they want me in. It’s not really for me to say. I know myself, and I know my body, and the biggest thing was that I felt good out there. Felt like I was able to ramp up intensity to a place that I haven’t gone yet.”
As the Red Sox wait to see how Crochet responds on Wednesday after testing that shoulder on the mound, Crochet’s potential return will make for an interesting call for Chad Tracy and his staff.
Crochet should offer some value to an already strong Boston bullpen if he’s cleared, given both his swing-and-miss stuff and his familiarity as a reliever after making 72 appearances out of the bullpen with the White Sox from 2020-23.
The next step for Crochet will be another live BP at some point this weekend — or potentially drawing into one of Boston’s final regular-season games against the Cubs for an inning or two.
“It’s whatever Craig thinks is right,” Crochet told Browne. “This team’s had a great year. I think that for me to take a spot on the roster, someone would have to lose one. I would feel bad doing that because this team’s pitched their ass off the whole season. Ultimately, that’s something that’s coming up to the front office, and whenever they gauge that I’m ready, then I’ll accept that. In the meantime, I’m just gonna keep working my butt off.”

item.title: [mlbkor.com] [오피셜] 보스턴 레드삭스, 채드 트레이시 감독과 3년 계약 연장…크레이그 브레슬로우 단장 옵션도 실행

item.content:encoded:
보스턴 레드삭스는 22일(미국 현지시간) 단 한 번의 과감한 조치로 프런트오피스와 감독실 모두에 탄탄한 기반 안정을 구축했습니다.
보스턴 레드삭스 구단 역사상 손꼽히는 시즌 중반 대반전을 이끌어낸 채드 트레이시는 임시 감독 꼬리표를 떼어냈습니다. 이에 따라 지난 20일에 포스트시즌 진출을 확정 지은 트레이시는 2030년 팀 옵션이 포함된 2029시즌까지의 3년 계약에 합의하며 구단 역사상 제49대 감독으로 공식 취임했습니다.
한편, 2023년 가을 보스턴의 야구 운영 부사장(CBO)으로 부임한 크레이그 브레슬로우는 2029년과 2030년 계약 옵션을 행사하기로 했습니다.
샘 케네디 레드삭스 사장 겸 최고경영자(CEO)는 "오늘은 보스턴 레드삭스 구단에 매우 훌륭한 날입니다"라며, "오늘 전해진 소식보다 더 기쁠 수는 없습니다. 올 시즌 다사다난한 롤러코스터 같은 시간을 보냈는데, 이러한 발표를 하게 되어 정말 기쁩니다"라고 소감을 밝혔습니다.
이번 인사는 시즌 초반 32승 46패라는 부진한 출발을 보이며 험난했던 처음 3개월을 보낸 레드삭스가 어떻게 팀을 다시 안정궤도에 올렸는지를 보여주는 또 하나의 사례였습니다.
상황이 그토록 심각해지기 전, 브레슬로우는 10승 17패로 시즌을 시작한 직후 오랜 기간 팀을 이끌었던 알렉스 코라 감독과 코치 5명을 경질하며 과감하게 결단을 내렸습니다.
케네디 사장은 "두 사람이 가장 공통으로 갖고 있는 점은, 적어도 최근 들어 레드삭스가 두 사람 모두에게 매우 어려운 임무를 맡겼다는 사실입니다"라며, "브레슬로우, 당신은 2023년에 레드삭스의 야구 운영 부문을 지속적인 성공의 길로 이끌고, 월드시리즈 우승을 위해 경쟁할 수 있는 위치로 되돌려 놓기 위해 영입되었습니다. 아직 해야 할 일이 많이 남아 있지만, 당신의 리더십 아래 구단이 나아가는 궤적에 대해 이보다 더 만족스러울 수 없습니다. 그리고 채드, 당신은 지난 4월 믿을 수 없을 정도로 어려운 상황에 투입되어 구단이 가장 필요로 할 때 안정감과 리더십을 제공해 주었습니다"라고 치하했습니다.
2006년부터 2014년까지 마이너리그에서 뼈를 깎는 노력을 했으나 선수로서 메이저리그를 밟지 못했던 41세의 트레이시에게는 특히나 감격스러운 하루였습니다. 그 후 그는 2015년부터 코치나 감독으로서 메이저리그에 진출하겠다는 새로운 도전에 나섰습니다.
끈기는 결실을 맺었습니다.
트레이시는 "그렇습니다. 선수와 코치로 보낸 시간을 정확히 합치면 22년이나 됩니다"라며, "정말 긴 시간이었고, 그 모든 순간을 사랑했습니다. 저는 선수로서 이 목표를 이루기 위해 온 힘을 쏟았고, 고등학교 시절부터 확고한 의지를 품었습니다. '나는 야구를 할 것이고 메이저리그 선수가 될 것이다'라고 다짐하며 그것을 실현하기 위해 할 수 있는 모든 노력을 다했습니다. 하지만 여러 장애물들이 가로막아 뜻을 이루지 못했습니다"라고 회상했습니다.
이어 그는 "그리고 나서 저는 야구라는 스포츠를 사랑하고 선수들과 지식을 나누는 것을 좋아하며, 클럽하우스의 일원이 되는 것과 야구 선수들 곁에 있는 것이 좋기 때문에 맨 밑바닥부터 다시 시작해 코치로서 모든 것을 해내겠다고 결심했습니다. 그 여정을 따라 가다 보면, 결국 이 지점에 도달하는 것이 얼마나 멋진 일인지 실감하게 됩니다"라고 덧붙였습니다.
트레이시에게 진정한 의미의 감격스러운 순간은 발표를 축하하는 기자회견이 열리기 전, 트리플A 우스터에서 4년 넘는 기간 동안 자신이 마이너리그에서 직접 지도했던 선수들을 비롯한 선수단과 기쁨을 나눌 때 찾아왔습니다.
트레이시는 "목이 살짝 메였습니다"라며, "그 순간에 서서 그동안의 여정을 되돌아보고, 지난 5년 동안 제 곁을 지켜주었던 선수들의 얼굴들을 둘러보았기 때문입니다. 방 안에 있는 선수들을 둘러보고, 제가 아주 깊은 유대감을 쌓아온 선수들과 함께 그 발표를 나눌 수 있었다는 것은 정말 멋진 순간이었습니다"라고 털어놓았습니다.
또한 그는 "선수들에게 오늘은 양복 재킷을 벗어던지고 유니폼으로 갈아입은 뒤 다시 업무에 복귀하여 선수들 자신과 우리가 10월에 무엇을 해낼 것인지에만 집중하겠다고 말했습니다. 하지만 우리 그룹과 함께한 이번 순간은 정말 특별했습니다"라고 전했습니다.
레드삭스는 6월 25일부터 시작된 32승 5패의 질주를 통해 모든 예상을 뒤엎은 팀이었습니다.
이토록 많은 승리를 거두기 전, 브레슬로의 감독 및 코칭스태프 교체 단행이 당장의 순위에 큰 변화를 주지 못하자 그는 거센 비판과 검증의 대상이 되었습니다. 하지만 구단주 그룹이 비공개로 지속적인 지지를 보내는 동안, 브레슬로는 외부의 소음에 귀를 닫았습니다.
그는 "솔직한 심정을 말씀드리자면, 저와 나머지 프런트오피스는 팀을 어떻게 다시 정상궤도에 올릴 것인지, 어떻게 더 많은 승리를 거둘 것인지, 그리고 선수들이 자신들의 역량을 온전히 발휘할 수 있도록 어떻게 도울 것인지에 너무 몰두해 있었습니다. 덕분에 저 자신에게 무슨 일이 일어날지 걱정할 겨를조차 없었습니다. 야구 운영 부서로서 우리는 오직 '어떻게 이 상황을 뒤집을 것인가?'에만 집착했습니다. 그것이 최우선 과제였고, 우리의 모든 시간을 쏟아부은 대상이었습니다"라고 설명했습니다.
트레이시와 브레슬로가 마주할 다음 과제는 오는 9월 29일 시작되는 아메리칸리그 와일드카드 시리즈를 위해 레드삭스를 철저히 준비시키는 것입니다.
케네디 사장은 "우리가 앞으로 나아가고 가을 야구를 향해 전진함에 따라, 이 구단은 이제 탄탄한 기반 위에 서게 되었습니다"라며, "우리 야구 운영 부서는 이제 연속성과 안정성을 확보했습니다. 우리는 다가올 미래와, 야구계에서 가장 열정적인 우리 팬들에게 그들이 마땅히 받아야 할 선물인 '챔피언십을 위해 싸울 기회'를 안겨줄 수 있는 우리의 능력에 대해 큰 기대와 낙관을 품고 있습니다"라고 강조했습니다.

item.title: [bostonherald.com] How Red Sox reached ‘natural conclusion’ to keep Chad Tracy as manager
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: There were no guarantees on the night of April 25, when Chad Tracy was abruptly pulled from what ultimately became his 499th and final win as Triple-A Worcester manager, and handed the keys to Boston’s big-league kingdom on an interim basis. Nor the next morning when Tracy, 41, walked into the Camden Yards visitors’ clubhouse in Baltimore to manage his first big-league game, to stunned and upset Red Sox players publicly questioning the future of the organization after the previous night’s firing
item.content:encoded:
There were no guarantees on the night of April 25, when Chad Tracy was abruptly pulled from what ultimately became his 499th and final win as Triple-A Worcester manager, and handed the keys to Boston’s big-league kingdom on an interim basis.
Nor the next morning when Tracy, 41, walked into the Camden Yards visitors’ clubhouse in Baltimore to manage his first big-league game, to stunned and upset Red Sox players publicly questioning the future of the organization after the previous night’s firing of longtime manager Alex Cora and six coaches.
The future became clearer on Tuesday morning. Hours before opening the final homestand of 2026, and fresh off clinching a playoff spot for the second consecutive year, the Red Sox officially announced Tracy’s new three-year contract to become their 49th manager, and the exercising of their 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.
“When it became time to make the very difficult change in leadership with our major league team, there was kind of really only one name that was considered,” Breslow said as he, Tracy and team president and CEO Sam Kennedy sat in the Fenway Park interview room Tuesday afternoon to discuss the day’s news.
The Red Sox were 10-17, tied for the American League’s worst record, when Tracy arrived. And they got worse before they got better. They lost several stars to injuries in late April and early May, and fell to their worst home record to begin a season since 1932 in early June.
“I mean, it was abysmal,” Kennedy said. “April, May and June were brutal to live through.”
As the losses mounted, so did public perception of Tracy as a stalking horse, and Breslow as a man on borrowed time. But within the organization, Red Sox leadership and players felt a significant shift when Tracy took the reins.
“It became pretty clear early on that Chad was the right person at the right time to lead this group,” Breslow, 46, said. “(We) recognized that this was a fit we wanted to preserve. … I think there was probably some realization a few weeks ago, maybe even further, that there’s a natural conclusion here that we’re working toward.”
The question of Tracy’s future with the organization was present from the start, both internally and externally, but he remained unruffled.
“Yeah, I mean, it didn’t bother me much anyways,” Tracy said. “I worried about the players. I worried about getting us on track, helping get us on track. … That was what my focus was on, and I figured this stuff, if it goes well enough, it’ll come together on its own.”
Tracy took a similar approach to last offseason’s WooSox managerial contract negotiations. Many might try to make the leap to a major league coaching job after managing a Triple-A team to winning seasons in each of their four years at the helm, and spending over two decades playing and working in the minor leagues. But Tracy took the “Que Sera Sera” approach; whatever will be, will be.
“I think those opportunities happen on their own,” Tracy said. “You don’t operate in those jobs thinking about, how do I get to my next one? You just do your job. … I’m here to help people. I’m here to help the players. And if I do that properly, then whether it’s here or somewhere else, those things always take care of themselves.”
Tracy’s unbotheredness by limbo and chaos, and his ability to navigate turbulent waters and help his players do the same were key factors in the removal of the interim tag.
Asked what he learned about Tracy after moving him up to the majors, Breslow said, “The answer to that is maybe what makes Chad most remarkable, which is, he was exactly the same. He was exactly as he was as the manager in Worcester, he was exactly the same after a shutout win as he was a heart-wrenching defeat, and I think that stability, that consistency, is how our players have responded so well.
“So what I’ve learned is he is just an unbelievably intense but even-keeled leader, someone who builds sincere and authentic relationships with everyone that he interacts with and comes across, someone that I think can can be trusted to be honest and questioned when it’s appropriate to do so, and someone who is willing to always put the players in the organization first.”
Members of the Red Sox echoed Breslow’s sentiments.
“I’m happy for him, because he’s handled this amazingly,” veteran shortstop Trevor Story told the Herald. “Odds were kind of stacked against him, and kind of our team in general, too. So happy for him, and he deserves it. He stewarded the ship in an incredible way, so pumped for him that he can kick that interim tag and be here for a while.”
“He’s a real calming influence,” Story continued. “If you talk to him or get to know him at all, he’s very level-headed, really knowledgeable baseball guy, and just being around him is a good feeling. So that goes a long way, I think, to being a manager, and I think yeah, he’s shown that he can handle this whole situation of Boston and everything going on.”
“He’s done an incredible job, just bringing this clubhouse together, and just taking it one day at a time, and I am incredibly happy for him,” catcher and first baseman Mickey Gasper told the Herald. “There’s nobody that’s earned something more that I’ve been around in the game of baseball than Trace, getting this job. He’s done a tremendous job, and I couldn’t think of anybody else better for the role.”
“I’ve learned so much from him,” added Gasper, who played for Tracy on the ‘24 WooSox and split this season between Worcester and Boston. “How to be a baseball man around your teammates, how to bring a fresh slate every day to the ballpark.
“The wins and losses wear on you that day. Playing for Trace the last couple years, even in the minor leagues we’ve had some tough losses together, and he always comes back the next day. Today is a new day. This is the task at hand, and just being able to turn the page after tough spots, tough losses, just adversity in general. And I think just watching him go about his business that’s what I’ve learned the most. He leads by example.”
Those particular attributes also made Tracy an ideal partner for Breslow. The latter must make the difficult decisions, the former has proved adept at ensuring the ripple effects don’t become tsunamis. The Red Sox feel this pairing will provide the stability that has been in scarce supply over the last decade.
“It’s huge,” Kennedy said of locking in this tandem for the next three years. “It’s a sacred relationship, between the head of baseball operations and the manager. Being on the same page, having that trust, that confidence in each other (is) something that I’ve learned going back to my days at the New York Yankees and the San Diego Padres. And here, seeing successful versions of it, and seeing unsuccessful versions of it.
“Lord knows we’ve made mistakes in our time. And just ensuring that you have that relationship right is critical. So yeah, it’s great to have that stability now. And look, we haven’t achieved anything, we know that. But I think we’re set up for success going forward.”
Story was glad to say he felt differently than that morning in Baltimore, when he was one of several longtime Red Sox who wondered “what the true direction of the franchise is.”
“When AC and all the guys got let go, we didn’t know the direction,” Story said. “And now, I feel like we do.”

item.title: [heavy.com] 4-Year Atlanta Braves Player Dealt Unfortunate News With New MLB Team
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: Atlanta Braves fans should remember outfielder Eli White quite well. The 32-year-old has played for the Braves this season and has spent parts of the last four seasons with the organization. Atlanta decided to move on from Eli White this August in a trade with the Boston Red Sox that landed reliever Tyler Uberstine in the Braves system. Well, on Tuesday, White was dealt some unfortunate news regarding his status for the rest of the season. More MLB on Heavy: Recent Atlanta Braves Player Quickly
item.content:encoded:
Atlanta Braves fans should remember outfielder Eli White quite well.
The 32-year-old has played for the Braves this season and has spent parts of the last four seasons with the organization.
Atlanta decided to move on from Eli White this August in a trade with the Boston Red Sox that landed reliever Tyler Uberstine in the Braves system.
Well, on Tuesday, White was dealt some unfortunate news regarding his status for the rest of the season.
More MLB on Heavy: Recent Atlanta Braves Player Quickly Released by New MLB Team
Eli White Undergoes Season-Ending Surgery
Eli White had recently been put on the IL with the Boston Red Sox, which already put the remainder of his 2026 campaign in jeopardy, but the final verdict came on Tuesday, September 22, when the Red Sox announced that White underwent Lisfranc repair surgery for his injured foot.
MLBTR.com’s Darragh McDonald wrote (about Eli White):
“The Sox added him at the deadline in the hopes that he could be a valuable complementary player for the stretch run and postseason as a late-game substitute for pinch-running or defensive purposes. Unfortunately, White got into just 27 games before hitting the IL. He told reporters last week, including Rob Bradford of WEEI, that he had a tear in a ligament in his foot and might require surgery.”
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Sean Murphy Decision Before Reds Game
Taking a Quick Look at Eli White’s Time with the Braves
As noted, Eli White spent a considerable amount of time with the Braves.
In fact, over his seven-year MLB career, the most games he’s played with a single team is 215 with the Braves (spread across four seasons).
In those 215 games, Eli White batted .233 with 16 home runs, 56 RBI, and an OPS+ of 86.
In 2026, White posted a batting average of .233 over 133 at-bats with the Braves before being moved to the Red Sox.
He’s a lifetime .216 hitter with 26 career home runs and holds an OPS+ of 73.
Speaking very quickly to the Red Sox side of this news, Boston will likely have to rely on names like Nate Eaton and Jahmai Jones to pick up platoon slack since Elit White will not be available for the MLB playoffs, which the Red Sox will be taking part in.

item.title: [MLB.com] Bregman (facial fractures) won't need IL, could return this weekend
item.dc:creator: Jordan Bastian
item.description: CHICAGO -- If Alex Bregman is not spotted in the Cubs’ locker room before a game, chances are he is down the tunnel in the batting cage. item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO -- If Alex Bregman is not spotted in the Cubs’ locker room before a game, chances are he is down the tunnel in the batting cage. That was no different on Tuesday afternoon, even with his left cheek and eye still bruised and swollen from the foul ball that struck him in the on-deck circle on Sunday in Cincinnati.
“He’s completely himself,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “He can’t sit still. He’s all over the room. Those are really good signs.”
All the worst-case scenarios that immediately came to mind for anyone who witnessed Sunday’s freak accident have, by all accounts, been avoided. Bregman has had multiple appointments with a variety of specialists and has received positive news on all fronts. His vision is fine. There are multiple fractures in his cheek area, but no surgery is required.
Counsell noted prior to Tuesday’s game against the Marlins that Bregman would not be placed on the injured list and a return before the end of the regular season has not been ruled out. In the coming days, Bregman will continue to ramp up his activity to gauge whether any symptoms arise, and the Cubs’ medical and training staff will assess and proceed from there.
“I think Alex is going to be fine, I really do,” Counsell said. “He’s planning on playing. He knew he had to get some good news from the doctors. He got that good news. So he’s going to do everything in his power. And as long as symptoms don’t increase, or happen as he increases activity, I think you’re going to see him play.”
After this three-game series at home against the Marlins, the Cubs are scheduled to play three games against the Red Sox in Boston, where Bregman played last season. The North Siders headed into Tuesday atop the National League Wild Card standings.
In the fourth inning of Sunday’s 9-1 win over the Reds, Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Cincinnati’s Luis Mey. The baseball hit the dirt and then struck Bregman in the face as he prepared to hit. The third baseman immediately dropped his bat, grabbed his face and headed down the dugout steps with members of Chicago’s staff.
Bregman was examined at a local hospital and cleared of any concussion symptoms. He posted photos on his Instagram account that showed severe swelling around his eye, but declared, “I’ll be back.” The Cubs had a staffer remain in Cincinnati to drive back to Chicago with Bregman, as opposed to having him fly back with the team.
“He doesn’t look great, that’s for sure,” Cubs president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer joked. “But no one loves to play more than him. I can say that with no equivocation. I’ve never had a player that loves baseball as much as he does. He just wants to play all the time. Right away, when we first heard from him afterwards, [he said] he was going to find a way to do it.
“There were scenarios where there was no way it was going to happen -- if he needed surgery or things like that. But he didn’t. Now he has the chance to get out there. And there’s nothing he wants to do more. It’s impressive.”
During the pregame hours on Tuesday, Bregman got a workout in and also donned a helmet and headed into the batting cage to track pitches on the high-velocity Trajekt machine. Around the clubhouse and in the cage, Bregman was very much acting like his usual self, which brought a smile to Nico Hoerner’s face.
“His reaction to everything has been uplifting,” Hoerner said. “Just in being relentlessly aggressive and positive and speaking about all the things he’s excited to do and turn it into. Just his own mentality kind of leads the group in that way in how to handle it. It was a super jarring thing and terrible timing, obviously.”
Through 153 games this season, the 32-year-old Bregman has hit .262 with 26 homers, 32 doubles, 89 RBIs and an .804 OPS. Since the All-Star break, however, only teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong (4.5) has been worth more wins above replacement (per FanGraphs) in the Majors than Bregman (3.4). The third baseman has hit .296 with 17 homers, 17 doubles, 48 RBIs and a .978 OPS in 59 games in the second half.
While Bregman is out, the Cubs have both Pedro Ramírez and Matt Shaw as options for third base. Ramírez -- recently the primary starter at second base, while Hoerner manned short with Dansby Swanson on the IL -- was in the lineup on Tuesday night. Shaw was Chicago’s main third baseman last year before Bregman came aboard via his five-year, $175 million deal.
“No one’s asking anyone to replace Breggy and what he’s done this year,” Hoerner said. “But in the meantime, we’re very well-equipped to handle it.”

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox Injury Update: Aggressive Willson Contreras, Ceddanne Rafaela, Curtis Mead, pitching options
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: Alongside the news that beloved interim skipper Chad Tracy will drop his interim tag, the Boston Red Sox got a slew of positive injury updates. Boston is just six games from the postseason and it needs all the reinforcements it can get. item.content:encoded:
Alongside the news that beloved interim skipper Chad Tracy will drop his interim tag, the Boston Red Sox got a slew of positive injury updates. Boston is just six games from the postseason and it needs all the reinforcements it can get.
One of the best, if not the best update is that Willson Contreras is swinging a bat following a scary hit by pitch against the Texas Rangers. Contreras on September 17 took a pitch on the side of his hand, immediately fell to the ground in pain and left the game without delay.
Contreras doesn't easily leave games after being plunked, which has happened 24 times this season. His immediate departure led fans to believe he could've been severely injured. Thankfully, that was not the case, as his imaging came back clean. He believed he fractured his hand because it was numb for a few minutes after the hit, but Contreras avoided the worst.
The Red Sox have not announced an estimated return date for Contreras, but any progress is a good sign. He's been Boston's best hitter all season and leads the team in home runs — the Sox can't afford to go to the postseason without him, especially with the New York Yankees' fearsome rotation ahead in the Wild Card series.
Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela near returns to Red Sox after both take batting practice on September 22
Ceddanne Rafaela also took batting practice on September 22. He hit off Garrett Crochet, who threw 16 pitches before Contreras' turn in the batter's box. The outfielder on September 19 told Alex Speier of The Boston Globe that he hopes to be active for the final homestand of the season, which has already started.
Like Contreras, Rafaela has been one of Boston's most consistent hitters all year. The Soxs offense has faltered without the two in the lineup. If his timeline holds, Rafaela should be back before the postseason so the Red Sox can take full advantage of his clutch timing in huge moments.
Rumors swirl about Curtis Mead's recovery following Garrett Crochet's BP session
There were also rumors that Curtis Mead was expected to hit off Crochet following Rafaela's practice, but there has been no confirmation that he actually swung a bat. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline to bring a righty power bat to their lineup, but he was plunked in his second Red Sox at-bat and the pitch fractured his wrist.
The most recent update on Mead from mid-September was that he was still feeling soreness in his wrist when he tried to swing. The soreness would need to subside for his hitting progression to start, and given the time of the season, many people assumed his year had reached its end. Given that he may not have hit against Crochet, it might still be.
Red Sox send Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo to Fort Myers to stay loose in case of postseason use
Alongside Crochet, the Red Sox have starters-turned-relievers Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo nearing the end of their respective recoveries. Both pitchers made rehab assignments with the Triple-A Worcester Red Sox before their season ended and they've been sent to Fort Myers to stay loose just in case Boston needs them in the playoffs, according to Chris Cotillo of MassLive.
The Red Sox will have no shortage of pitching depth entering the playoffs, but whether they use any of their rehabbing pitchers is still yet to be seen. Well-rested arms would be helpful, but the team could be concerned about upsetting the chemistry of the preexisting bullpen, which has been one of the best in the sport all year.

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] Boston Red Sox Announce Wilyer Abreu Decision Before Cleveland Guardians Series
item.dc:creator: Scott Roche
item.description: After an off day on Monday, the Boston Red Sox will return to Fenway Park to begin the next-to-last series of the regular season before the playoffs next week. Boston clinched their spot in the postseason after the Atlanta Braves completed a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros on Sunday afternoon. item.content:encoded:
After an off day on Monday, the Boston Red Sox will return to Fenway Park to begin the next-to-last series of the regular season before the playoffs next week. Boston clinched their spot in the postseason after the Atlanta Braves completed a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros on Sunday afternoon.
The Red Sox are all but locked into the second American League wild-card spot. They are on a collision course with the New York Yankees next week in the Bronx for a best-of-three series. Before then, however, Boston has three games with the Cleveland Guardians. They will then host the Chicago Cubs this weekend, weather permitting.
As for the Guardians series, Wilyer Abreu is back in the lineup for manager Chad Tracy and batting in a familiar spot.
Boston Red Sox Announce Wilyer Abreu Spot in Lineup Against Guardians on Tuesday Night
Tracy will send left-hander Payton Tolle to the mound to open the series and as far as his lineup goes, Abreu us back and batting cleanup. Here is Boston's lineup for the series opener against Cleveland's Parker Messick,
Nick Sogard 1B
Jahmai Jones DH
Wilyer Abreu RF
Caleb Durbin 3B
Isiah Kiner-Falefa SS
Nate Eaton CF
Abreu will be batting fourth, with first baseman Willson Contreras still out of the lineup after getting hit by a pitch last Thursday night against the Texas Rangers. He missed the series against the Tampa Bay Rays. As for Abreu, he did not play in Sunday's series finale, a 5-1 loss.
Boston Red Sox Playing Out the String Ahead of Playoffs
Tuesday, it was announced that Tracy was having the interim tag removed, and Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow is having his option in 2029 and 2030 picked up by the club. It's not surprising that it was announced before the playoffs.
Boston is scheduled to send their three projected starters on the mound next week against the Yankees: Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suárez against the Guardians. However, Cleveland is in a heated race with the Chicago White Sox for the American League Central Division title. They enter the series with a one-game lead over the White Sox, who are playing the Kansas City Royals this week.
Boston has slumped in September. However, they can use the six games before next week as a tune-up. As for this weekend, the weather is projected to be a mess. Tim Healy of the Boston Globe reported that MLB has no plans to move the series out of Boston. There are going to be very few windows to play baseball this weekend.
The Cubs are in a battle for home-field advantage in the National League wild-card round. Those games will have big meaning for them and the NL. They enter play this week tied with the San Diego Padres for home-field advantage next week. The Philadelphia Phillies are a game behind. There is a lot riding on this weekend.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Boston Red Sox Announce Wilyer Abreu Decision Before Cleveland Guardians Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have been without Aroldis Chapman for the last five games as he battles a lat injury.
Chapman last pitched on Sept. 13, but the team has noted that they do not think his lat injury is something that will be a long-term issue. He has been an elite closer, once again, for the Red Sox, earning his second straight All-Star nod. The 28-year-old is getting close to making his return, it seems.
"I think we're a day or two away from him being ready to roll," manager Chad Tracy said on Tuesday, per MassLive's Christopher Smith. "We'll see how everything feels today."
Chapman won't be available for Tuesday's game, but the Red Sox's top priority is making sure he's ready for October baseball. In all likelihood, the Red Sox will be playing the New York Yankees in a best-of-three Wild Card Series in the Bronx when the postseason starts on Sept. 29.
Chapman spent seven seasons with the Yankees in his career, so he is very familiar with Yankee Stadium. In his career, opponents hit .168 against him there. He has 88 career saves at Yankee Stadium and a 3.10 ERA. In four innings against the Yankees this season, Chapman has given up three hits and has four strikeouts.
The Red Sox will need Chapman at his best if they want to make a deep run in the postseason.
More MLB: Pitcher Yankees Traded At Deadline Designated For Assignment By New Team

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox might've cemented Craig Breslow’s rise off the hot seat too soon
item.dc:creator: Brian Burrows
item.description: The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years. With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head
item.content:encoded:
The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years.
With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head of baseball operations who got his team to the playoffs in years two and three of their time running the club getting years added to their contract, would make sense, but in Breslow's case it isn't as straightforward.
It was only three months ago when most of Red Sox Nation was calling for Breslow's head. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24, dead last in the division, and it already seemed like the season was over. It took a miraculous turnaround to get the team to the playoffs. Not to say that Breslow had nothing to do with that; he had added a lot of players to the roster who were key contributors, but that has a lot more to do with the players and coaches than the front office.
Breslow's tenure has also been marred by controversy, specifically the Rafael Devers drama. It was his handling of the situation, along with former manager Alex Cora, that ultimately led to the fracture of the relationship with the team's then-face of the franchise. While the fanbase was split on whose side they took, player or team, his actions after the fact didn't make it any better.
Red Sox's Craig Breslow had the hottest seat of any GM only three months ago
It was the signing of Alex Bregman that caused the Devers drama in the first place. While Breslow was praised for the signing, Bregman opted out at the end of the year and was then not re-signed. The Red Sox went from two elite third basemen to none in the span of a season. It wasn't a good look for the Red Sox CBO.
Now, Breslow's pivot from all of the drama and mess surrounding Devers and Bregman looks incredibly good in hindsight. The additions of Ranger Suarez, Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and others have been extremely impactful to the Red Sox's success this season. While some of those moves were celebrated at the time they happened, others like the Durbin-Kyle Harrison swap (that also netted the Red Sox Andruw Monasterio and Anthony Seigler) were heavily scrutinized.
Breslow also made good moves at the trade deadline, adding Erik Miller and Eli White, who have looked good for the Sox. He also made the splash trade for Adley Rutschman, which hasn't worked as well on the field, but certainly instilled confidence in the team, knowing the front office believed in them.
Red Sox could've softened the impact by extending one of Craig Breslow's options at first
All of this is to say that Breslow's time as CBO hasn't been as smooth sailing as the records would suggest. He has had some high highs but also some low lows. Why did ownership feel the need to exercise both options right now? The first option wasn't needed until the 2029 season, two years out. The second was for 2030, three years out.
Doing the first one now would've been fine — picking up the 2029 option gives Breslow another three comfortable seasons on his contract. That would make him more comfortable making moves for the future and give him the job security to know he will likely be in place to see them play out. Selecting the 2030 option on the same day was unnecessary, though.
There have been too many hiccups in the three years under Breslow to say he has warranted another four seasons. The start of 2026 could easily repeat itself in 2027. Should ownership feel the need to relieve him of his duties early, then this makes it that much harder. Breslow hasn't won a World Series in Boston; in fact, he hasn't even made it out of the Wild Card round. Exercising the option for 2030 feels very premature.
Breslow has not done a bad job in Boston. At the end of the day, it's results that matter, and Breslow's teams have made the playoffs two out of three times. He shouldn't be fearing for his job, but his contract also wasn't ending for another two seasons. It feels early to be handing him the keys so far down the road after the drama of his first two years as CBO.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox’s rotation against Guardians could preview Wild Card Game 1 starter fans desperately want
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The postseason begins on September 29, giving teams one day of rest between the end of the regular season and the start of the race. Playoff teams must plan their rotations early have the right pitchers rested and ready for the opening series and the Boston Red Sox have seemingly made their call. The Red Sox's rotation for their upcoming matchup with the Cleveland Guardians, their second-to-last series of the year, is Payton Tolle in game one, Sonny Gray in game two and Ranger Suarez in game thr
item.content:encoded:
The postseason begins on September 29, giving teams one day of rest between the end of the regular season and the start of the race. Playoff teams must plan their rotations early have the right pitchers rested and ready for the opening series and the Boston Red Sox have seemingly made their call.
The Red Sox's rotation for their upcoming matchup with the Cleveland Guardians, their second-to-last series of the year, is Payton Tolle in game one, Sonny Gray in game two and Ranger Suarez in game three. That leaves Patrick Sandoval, Jake Bennett and Brayan Bello (or a bullpen game) for the final series against the Chicago Cubs, not necessarily in that order.
Tolle has earned the series-opening start against the New York Yankees. He's posted a 2.36 ERA and 0.88 WHIP with 56 strikeouts over his last seven starts. He's stayed hot despite having 143 innings on his arm this year, and he's gotten even better as the year has gone on.
Tolle has had previous success against the Yankees, including two stellar outings this year. He faced the Yankees in his first big league appearance this year and allowed just one run on three hits with 11 strikeouts and a walk over six innings. Tolle next faced New York on June 26 (one of the games in the four-game sweep that started Boston's historic summer winning streak) and he pitched seven, one-hit innings with seven strikeouts.
Red Sox-Guardians series likely previews Boston's Wild Card rotation with Payton Tolle starting Game 1
Starting Tolle first could set up a battle between two young lefties and Cy Young Award contenders (though it isn't much of a contest) if the Yankees plan to open the series with their ace Cam Schlittler. This might not be the case, though, as New York seems to be setting Gerrit Cole up for the Game 1 start. The Red Sox don't fare as well against right-handed pitching as they do against lefties, with a .712 team OPS against them, and taking Boston off its game will be a high priority for its rival.
Whether the Red Sox win or lose Game 1, Game 2 means everything. With a series loss or a sweep on the line, Boston's ace Gray should take the mound. The 36-year-old Gray has surprised fans everywhere by posting one of the best seasons of his career with the Red Sox and his consistency is unmatched.
Gray has clocked a 2.82 ERA, 1.16 WHIP, 146 strikeouts and 45 walks over 163 innings. Like the Red Sox, the Yankees also don't perform especially well against righty pitching, with a .713 OPS as a club. With a sweep on the line or to stay alive, the veteran Gray is the guy to trust.
In a win-or-go-home Game 3, Suarez deserves Boston's trust. He's gotten back on his feet over the last few weeks following a shaky spell (5.70 ERA in August) after a groin injury. Postseason starts are Suarez's bread and butter — he boasts a 1.48 ERA and 1.06 WHIP over 42.2 frames across seven playoff series — and he's the best choice to keep the Red Sox alive when they're on the brink of elimination.
Boston's rotation has been the biggest strength of the team all season. With these three pitchers, in any order, the Red Sox have good chances to get past the Yankees to advance to the Division Series. But setting the energy with Tolle and having the two veterans follow, as Boston has set things up, makes a lot of sense.

Contreras was not placed on the injured list and is trying to make a return before the end of the regular season. According to manager Chad Tracy, Contreras is "doing much better" and took some swings on Wednesday. "He was able to swing pretty aggressively in the cage again today," Tracy told MassLive's Christopher Smith. Contreras was an All-Star this year and is a huge reason why the
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have been without Willson Contreras since Thursday, when he was hit in the hand by a pitch.
Contreras was not placed on the injured list and is trying to make a return before the end of the regular season. According to manager Chad Tracy, Contreras is "doing much better" and took some swings on Wednesday.
"He was able to swing pretty aggressively in the cage again today," Tracy told MassLive's Christopher Smith.
Contreras was an All-Star this year and is a huge reason why the Red Sox turned their season around. At 34 years old, he is having a career year, hitting .276 with a .905 OPS. If the season ended today, he would tie his career-high batting average and set a new career-high in OPS. He also has a career-high 27 home runs and 81 RBIs.
The Red Sox will need him back in the lineup if they want to make a deep run, but there is no real reason to rush him back in the regular season. The Red Sox are pretty much locked into the No. 5 seed, and the only real benefit of bringing Contreras back for the regular season is to get him a few at-bats before the postseason.
The Red Sox will likely play the New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series. This season, Contreras has just a .673 OPS against the Yankees in 13 games. He will hope to get better results in the postseason, but that won't be easy if his hand is not 100%.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Red Sox ace encouraged after facing live hitters: ‘I could go get outs’
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Garrett Crochet reached an important milestone in his road to recovery on Tuesday, facing live hitters on the mound at Fenway Park for the first time since his ill-fated comeback attempt in late May. Throwing live batting practice against Ceddanne Rafaela, the Red Sox ace threw 16 pitches, one more than originally planned because he spiked a changeup into the dirt on what was supposed to be his final pitch. The left-hander said he was able to ramp up his intensity to a level he hadn’t reached ye
item.content:encoded:
Garrett Crochet reached an important milestone in his road to recovery on Tuesday, facing live hitters on the mound at Fenway Park for the first time since his ill-fated comeback attempt in late May.
Throwing live batting practice against Ceddanne Rafaela, the Red Sox ace threw 16 pitches, one more than originally planned because he spiked a changeup into the dirt on what was supposed to be his final pitch. The left-hander said he was able to ramp up his intensity to a level he hadn’t reached yet, that his fastball was in the 94-96 mph range, and that following the session he got good feedback from Rafaela.
With that crucial box checked, could Crochet’s next time on the mound come in a game setting? Crochet said it’s too soon to say, but he’s cautiously optimistic about his ability to do so.
“You don’t know until you know I suppose. I would say the way that live just went that I could go get outs,” Crochet said. “It depends, obviously, what role they want me in, like I said it’s not really for me to say, I know myself and I know my body, and the biggest thing is that I felt good out there.”
Crochet has missed the majority of the season due to left shoulder inflammation, which landed him on the injured list in late April after only six starts. What was originally believed to be a short-term injury wound up sidelining Crochet for five months and counting, but after Tuesday’s session there remains a possibility Crochet could factor into the postseason equation for the Red Sox out of the bullpen.
That will be up to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy, Crochet was sure to emphasize.
“This team has had a great year, I think for me to take a spot on the roster then someone would have to lose one, and I would feel bad doing that because this team has pitched their (butts) off the whole season,” Crochet said. “Ultimately that’s going to be something that’s up to the front office and whenever they gauge that I’m ready then I’ll accept that, and in the meantime I’m just going to keep working my butt off.”
Tracy said he was encouraged by Crochet’s outing, noting that his velocity is climbing and the spin on his pitches looked sharp. The next step will be seeing how his body recovers in the upcoming days and mapping out a plan for the weekend.
“What that looks like now, I don’t know,” Tracy said. “I just know that whatever it is it’s going to be done with Garrett’s best interest in mind.”
Typically the next stage in a throwing progression after throwing live batting practice would be to start a rehab assignment, but given that the minor league season ended this past weekend, that isn’t an option for Crochet. Time also isn’t on the left-hander’s side, so if Crochet is going to pitch in a game before the playoffs, he would have to be activated at some point over the final homestand.
Tracy said those are all factors the club is considering, and while he believes Crochet would be up for the challenge of jumping right into a playoff series, they have to be realistic about where he’s at when it comes time to decide who will be on the playoff roster.
“Knowing the player, if he was healthy and we felt he could he’d probably be like ‘I’m not going to be afraid of that,'” Tracy said. “That being said, we have to consider it and just be very mindful of what are we potentially exposing him to and what can he give us, really? Understanding you don’t want to leave yourself short, so for me it’s been step by step, the next step would be sometime this weekend, let’s see what that entails, and we’ll go from there.”
Rafaela, Contreras getting close
Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) and Willson Contreras (bruised right hand) remain sidelined with their respective injuries, but Tracy said both are getting close to a return.
“(Rafaela) is doing much better, we’re getting close there, and Willson’s also doing much better, he was able to swing pretty aggressively in the cage again today,” Tracy said, adding that Rafaela was scheduled to run and Contreras was set to take batting practice on the field. “(We’ll) let them get through their whole day, see where they’re at and assess, but I think we’re getting pretty close with both of them.”
Staying ready
With the minor league season finished the Red Sox have sent a contingent of players who may potentially factor into the club’s plans the rest of the way to Fort Myers so they can stay ready in the event they’re needed.
Tracy did not have the full list of players available when asked Tuesday, but some of those headed to Fort Myers include pitchers Tanner Houck, Johan Oviedo, Jedixson Paez, Tyler Samaniego and Wyatt Olds, infielders Romy Gonzalez, Franklin Arias and Tsung-Che Cheng, and outfielder Braiden Ward.
Veteran catcher Tomas Nido has also come up from Worcester to serve as an extra catcher on the taxi squad for the Red Sox.
Extra innings
The Red Sox announced Eli White underwent successful Lisfranc repair surgery on his right foot Tuesday. The procedure was performed by Dr. Martin O’Malley at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York City. … Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) is feeling much better but is still a day or two away from a return to the mound. … Curtis Mead (fractured left wrist) has resumed swinging a regular bat and is taking overhand batting practice, but while the Red Sox haven’t ruled out a possible return, Tracy acknowledged that time isn’t on his side.

item.title: [Over the Monster] Payton Tolle makes his final start before the postseason
item.dc:creator: Matthew Gross
item.description: Chad Tracy told us not to look very much into the order of the rotation this week, but it’s hard not to note that Payton Tolle is starting tonight exactly one week before the Wild Card series begins, and Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez are set to go tomorrow and Thursday. That feels like a Game 1, Game 2, and Game 3 setup for New York, but again, we’ll still have to wait a few more days for official word. Regardless of how the Sox choose to stack the deck, this will be Tolle’s final tune up before
item.content:encoded:
Chad Tracy told us not to look very much into the order of the rotation this week, but it’s hard not to note that Payton Tolle is starting tonight exactly one week before the Wild Card series begins, and Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez are set to go tomorrow and Thursday. That feels like a Game 1, Game 2, and Game 3 setup for New York, but again, we’ll still have to wait a few more days for official word.
Regardless of how the Sox choose to stack the deck, this will be Tolle’s final tune up before the showdown against the Yankees, so how he looks here will be even more important than the result of this game for the Red Sox.
On the contrary, this game means everything to Cleveland. Despite entering the night three games behind the Red Sox, they’re currently leading the AL Central by a game over the Chicago White Sox, and if the season ended today, they’d actually get a bye and wouldn’t even have to play in the Wild Card round.
To help them maintain control of that bye, they have their ace Parker Messick on the mound, who enters the evening with a 2.57 ERA and 186 strike outs on the season.
Switching gears to the Red Sox lineup, the biggest note is that Roman Anthony is again in left field and Jarren Duran starts the night on the bench. This is becoming the theme against left handed starts, which is obviously noteworthy for next week because Carlos Rodon and Max Fried are both left handed.
⚾️ First Pitch: 6:45pm — Fenway Park. Boston, MA

item.title: [si.com] Samuel Basallo's Second Half Raises More Red Flags For Orioles Hitting Staff And Medical Staff
item.dc:creator: Jason La Canfora; Unknown
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles, under failed head of baseball operations Mike Elias, are incapable of cultivating their greatest resources into consistently productive players. Since running off one of the most respected and accomplished training staffs so Elias could bring in his own people, their Injured List stints have soared and the same recurring injuries have cropped up and their most important young everyday players have regressed, markedly and quickly, and, in some cases, perhaps permanently. item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Orioles, under failed head of baseball operations Mike Elias, are incapable of cultivating their greatest resources into consistently productive players.
Since running off one of the most respected and accomplished training staffs so Elias could bring in his own people, their Injured List stints have soared and the same recurring injuries have cropped up and their most important young everyday players have regressed, markedly and quickly, and, in some cases, perhaps permanently. So watching 22-year-old catcher Samuel Basallo struggle mightily and not look like himself and appear to be compensating for a lingering shoulder injury deep into a lost season is a major concern for him (especially against the backdrop of what has become of Gunnar Henderson and Jackson Holliday, among others).
Wasn’t that long ago that Basallo was the most prodigious power hitting catcher under the age of 22 in MLB history, as we documented at the time. He also left a game against Toronto briefly back in May wincing and leaving with trainers, only to pop back up in the on deck circle late in the game, only to experience more issues that clownish rookie manager Craig Albernaz tried to minimize,only to end up on the IL in July, after all, with what was deemed “right shoulder inflammation” and struggle mightily ever since.
Carrying three catchers for most of the second half of the season, again, in a lost season, there seemed to be a mounting case for shutting down a young man who ended up catching infinitely more innings for this team than alleged star Adley Rutschman and endured his fair share of adversity in a rookie season at a very young age for someone manning this position. That seemed smart ever before he took a foul tip tot he head Monday that had him getting checked for a concussion.
It seems even more obvious, now.
This kid barely caught 200 games in the minors, and I am thoroughly convinced the shoulder situation has been fairly significant for way longer than they got around to putting him on the IL. Regardless, the second half has been a mess.
Hitting The Wall
Basallo has not seemed comfortable at all since being reactivated and his power stroke is lacking and he’s been getting under the ball a lot and failing to line things up. His strikeout rate has gone from 26% to 30%.
Split G GS PA HR RBI BA OBP SLG OPS
1st Half 83 70 301 16 46 .248 .309 .464 .772
2nd Half 29 24 98 2 8 .140 .235 .221 .456
In May, as Basallo came into his own, he did what he always did in the minors – destroy fastballs. He hit .314 of fastballs that month and slugged .543. Since then, he is 15-for-100 against fastballs with just five extra base hits (all homers). That’s a massive red flag and I tend to think health and wear and tear have much to do with it. And probably some mounting frustration with one of MLB’s worst hitting staffs that has undermined many a fledgling career already.
Any chances of trying to end this season at anything close to the power and ferocity with which he was swinging the bat in midsummer is long gone. How much first base he ends up playing in the future – or even picking up some right field – remains to be seen. And hopefully he will not need any sort of procedures or clean ups this offseason.
