item.content:encoded:
Sox slugger Mickey Gasper's motivation stems from his roots in Merrimack
Merrimack's Mickey Gasper has become a fan favorite at Fenway Park, with his baseball journey taking him from high school to the Nashua Silver Knights through the minor leagues and finally to the Boston Red Sox.
Gasper grew up in Merrimack, about an hour away from Fenway.
"For me, playing with a little chip on my shoulder helps me," he told News 9.
Gasper's story is familiar to Granite Staters now, but many still ask how he can go from playing T-ball to consistently hitting homers for the Red Sox.
"A lot of work," he said.
>> Download the free WMUR app to get updates on the go <<
That work ethic was taught by his parents, Livia and Mick, who moved from New Jersey to Merrimack in 2001 when Mickey was about 5 years old.
"He is tenacious, and the resilience started growing at a young age," Livia Gasper said.
"He was competitive in T-ball," his father said. "One day, he made a great play. The coach of the other team said, 'We don't play outs.' And Mickey is like (making an appalled expression)."
"If there's anything that somebody from the Northeast does, it's that you do play with a chip on your shoulder," Mickey Gasper said. "A lot of people have doubted my process just in the last two years."
"He had bunk beds in his room, and I found it taped up on the flat, and it says, 'I'm not good enough,'" his father said.
Mickey Gasper worked to become good enough to play for the Merrimack High School Tomahawks.
"A lot of elite high school players rely on talent. He never did," said Nick Jaskolka, his high school coach. "That's a rare makeup for a high-end player."
That makeup has been put to the test. Mickey Gasper is currently having a breakout season at 30 years old in his second stint with the Red Sox.
Two years ago, he made his major league debut with Boston after more than five years in the minors. His family was in the stands for the first few games, making the trip from New Jersey, where they moved from New Hampshire in 2019.
But Gasper went 0-for-18 and was sent back down to the minors.
"We actually have not been back to Boston," his mother said.
"I'm staying away from Boston," his father said. "I feel like I was the kiss of death."
What has happened in Boston this summer is nothing short of remarkable. Recalled from AAA on Aug. 17, Mickey Gasper hit his first home run in a Red Sox uniform two years after his debut.
It was the first of three straight games with a homer -- six in 12 games -- for one of the best months in the history of baseball. His stats were up there with the likes of Ted Williams and Barry Bonds.
"It's cool," Mickey Gasper said. "It's something you can't live on. It's a month's stretch."
On the bottom of the bat he used to get all those hits is a picture of him and his father.
"It's very humbling," his father said. "It's been a lifelong love for baseball."
Despite that amazing run, he was sent back down on Saturday, Aug. 29. He didn't have to report to Worcester until the following Tuesday, so he visited his parents.
"First thing I said was, I'm going to go back to Freehold for the day just to be able to spend time with them," he said.
"We definitely felt the heaviness," his mother said. "We were actually supposed to go to the game on Sunday. I made a big old vat of sauce and meatballs."
"Short pasta. Against my request," Mickey Gasper said. "I like spaghetti. I'm a spaghetti guy."
This AAA stint was shorter than the pasta his mom made. During that dinner, Mickey Gasper's phone was ringing. It was the Red Sox on the other end, saying he was going back up. In his first at-bat, he hit another home run.
"He makes good meatballs," his father said.
"We go together from what feels like the lowest of lows to the highest of highs, and on that day, it was in a span of 12 hours," his mother said. "We were in tears."
"I thank my family for everything. Just being around them is…," Mickey Gasper said before trailing off.
Mickey Gasper's efforts helped the Red Sox clinch a playoff spot. Like him, the team turned things around this year. The Sox were 14 games below .500 in late June, and if the season ended today, they would play a best-of-three Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium, where his parents have been this year.
Mick and Livia Gasper could bring the pasta and meatballs to him next time.

item.title: [MLB.com] Chad Tracy Named Red Sox Manager
item.dc:creator: Spokane Indians
item.description: The Red Sox dropped the interim tag and made it official. Chad Tracy was named Boston's 49th manager in franchise history today, capping off a historic turnaround that saw the former Spokane Indians catcher lead the team from 14 games under .500 to a postseason berth. "Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization. What this team has accomplished over
item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox dropped the interim tag and made it official. Chad Tracy was named Boston's 49th manager in franchise history today, capping off a historic turnaround that saw the former Spokane Indians catcher lead the team from 14 games under .500 to a postseason berth.
"Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization. What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic," said Red Sox CEO Sam Kennedy. "Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others.
Tracy, 41, took over as Boston's interim manager in late-April after the team fired Alex Cora following an 10-17 start to the season. The Red Sox have gone 74-55 (.574) since Tracy took the helm, including a 15-game winning streak (tying the franchise record set in 1946) and a 27-3 (.900) stretch from July 3rd through August 7th—the best 30-game span in franchise history.
Boston joined the 1914 Miracle Braves, 1974 Pirates and 2005 Astros as the only teams to reach the postseason after falling as many as 14 games under .500, and the team's 31-44 record is the worst 75-game start by a team to make the playoffs in MLB history (h/t Sarah Langs).
"I think there was pretty much an understanding when I first got here that we've a lot of work to do, let's focus on that. Let's worry about the rest of the stuff later as it goes along," said Tracy during a press conference on Tuesday. "I am very happy, though, that it is done and in the course of three days we've clinched a playoff spot and now all the focus can be on what we can try to do in October."
Originally a third-round pick of the Texas Rangers out of Pepperdine in 2006, Tracy was named a Northwest League All-Star that summer after slashing .262/.339/.456 and hitting 11 home runs in 66 games with the Indians. He would reach as high as Triple-A during his playing career before shifting to the dugout as a manager starting in 2015.
Tracy spent three seasons as a minor league manager in the Los Angeles Angels organization and served as the team's minor league field coordinator from 2018-2021. He joined the Red Sox in 2022 and has spent the last five years as manager of the Triple-A Worcester Red Sox, compiling a 324-296 record (.523) while helping to develop the organization's top prospects like Peyton Tolle and Roman Anthony.
ABOUT THE SPOKANE INDIANS
The Spokane Indians are the High-A affiliate of the Colorado Rockies located in Spokane Valley, Wash. The Indians have played at Avista Stadium, home to the MultiCare Kids Bench Seat, since 1958 and have been a proud member of the Spokane community since 1903. Parking at all Spokane Indians games is FREE. The Spokane Indians Office and Team Store are open 9:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Monday to Thursday and 9:00 a.m. - 1:00 p.m. on Fridays.

item.content:encoded:
Once again, Garrett Crochet donned a full Red Sox uniform, made the walk from the bullpen to the mound, and pitched at Fenway Park on Tuesday afternoon. This time, he faced a live hitter -- in the form of Ceddanne Rafaela -- as he took another step toward returning to the mound for Boston.
And for the first time in what's been a long recovery period, the 27-year-old said he feels ready to contribute.
"I would say, the way that that live [batting practice] just went, that I could go get outs," Crochet told reporters inside the Red Sox clubhouse.
That being said, Crochet shared that he has some hesitance to joining the roster, though it has nothing to do with his own health.
"This team's had a great year. I think that for me to take a spot on the roster, then someone would have to lose one. And I would feel bad doing that, because this team has pitched their ass off the whole season," Crochet said. "Ultimately, that's something that's gonna be up to the front office. And whenever they gauge that I'm ready, then I'll accept that. In the meantime, I'm just gonna keep working my butt off."
More Red Sox Coverage
Crochet's work on Tuesday involved 16 pitches, and he estimated he was sitting at 94-96 mph on his fastball velocity. The left-hander said how well he recovers on Wednesday will be a significant determinant on his ability to pitch in games. Yet when asked if he'll pitch in a regular-season game this weekend or save his return for the postseason, he is leaving that decision to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy.
"I think that I'm just gonna do whatever they tell me to do, to be honest," he said. "I think that [live BPs] and games, obviously it's a big step up and the pressure of the moment, I suppose, and the intensity. But I don't think that there's a set amount of [live BPs] that need to be thrown before a game."
Tracy, who officially dropped the interim tag earlier in the day, said that whatever decision is made on Crochet, it will be "done with Garrett's best interests in mind."
"Looking at what is he able to accomplish this week, and what does the playoffs require?" Tracy explained. "And then deciding can he fit that role or not based on what he's done."
Ceddanne Rafaela
Rafaela, who hasn't played since Sept. 2 due to a hamstring injury, partook in the live BP with Crochet as he nears a return to the lineup.
"Much better," Tracy said on Rafaela. "Getting close there."
Rafaela has produced the best offensive season of his career, as he's batted .282 with a .760 OPS in 135 games, while continuing to provide Gold Glove-level defense in center field.
Willson Contreras
Tracy also shared a positive injury update on Willson Contreras, who continues to improve after taking a pitch off his right hand last Thursday.
Tracy said that Contreras is "doing much better" and is "swinging aggressively" as he works his way back to full strength.
Aroldis Chapman
Closer Aroldis Chapman hasn't pitched since Sept. 13 due to some lat tightness, but Tracy had yet another positive injury update.
"He's getting very close," Tracy said. "I think we're a day or two away from him being ready to roll."
Group staying ready in Fort Myers
The Red Sox are keeping a team of reinforcements ready in Fort Myers for the playoff run, in case anybody is needed as an injury replacement along the way. That list of players includes:
- SP Tanner Houck
- SP Johan Oviedo
- SS/2B Franklin Arias
- OF Braiden Ward
- RP Wyatt Olds
- SS/2B Tsung-Che Cheng
- RP Tyler Samaniego
- 1B/2B Romy Gonzalez
- RP Jedixson Paez
Curtis Mead
Perhaps the lone negative injury update from Tracy was on second baseman Curtis Mead, who broke his wrist in his first game with the Red Sox on July 27.
"Haven't ruled it out yet. It's gonna be tough," Tracy said when asked if Mead might be able to return for the first round of the playoffs.
Tracy said that Mead is taking some overhand batting practice, but there may not be enough time for Mead to progress to being game-ready.
"I said we would probably be a little aggressive to see how the hand responds," Tracy said. "Have not ruled it out. It's just we're getting up against it a bit."

While there's still work to do for Boston, looking to secure a top-two wild card spot in the American League over the next few days, the team can also officially start planning for the playoffs. For the most part, the Red Sox know who their key contributors will be in the AL Wild Card round. But on Tuesday, fans got positive updates on two injured stars, both of whom appear to be nearing potential returns. Here's the latest on bo
item.content:encoded:
Could the Red Sox get some reinforcements ahead of the postseason?
While there's still work to do for Boston, looking to secure a top-two wild card spot in the American League over the next few days, the team can also officially start planning for the playoffs.
For the most part, the Red Sox know who their key contributors will be in the AL Wild Card round. But on Tuesday, fans got positive updates on two injured stars, both of whom appear to be nearing potential returns.
Here's the latest on both Garrett Crochet and Curtis Mead as they work toward getting back to full health for the Red Sox.
Red Sox Get Encouraging Signs From Two Injured Stars Ahead of Postseason
Boston's pitching staff has been terrific in 2026 despite the absence of Crochet, who has been out since April with a lat strain and other shoulder inflammation. But ahead of the postseason, it appears Crochet is ramping up at a perfect time.
Crochet throwing live BP with Ceddanne at Fenway today 👀 pic.twitter.com/Iwv2R14iVk
— NESN (@NESN) September 22, 2026
On Tuesday, Crochet was seen completing a live BP session against Ceddanne Rafaela, throwing 16 pitches that included a velocity in the 94-96 mph range, according to Tyler Milliken.
Garrett Crochet ended up throwing a total of 16 pitches in his first live BP.
Velocity was in the 94-96 range. Few ticks up from the last time he threw a regular bullpen. Currently feeling good and thinks he can get outs.
Some great video from @alexspeier. pic.twitter.com/ZMsMmUXzvU
Notably, per Chris Cotillo, Crochet also told reporters that he thinks he could "get outs" with the way his live session went.
On Saturday, new full-time manager Chad Tracy also provided the latest on Crochet and whether he could return, potentially as a reliever for the postseason.
“I think it just depends on how he feels coming out of it, how much volume we give him,” Tracy said, per MLB.com. “So it’s hard to say. I know it’s not a great answer, but it’s just really how it is. How does he feel after each step? So when he does that, how does he feel? And then determine from there. Do we give him more hitters or do we want to put him in a game? It’s hard to say until you know how he feels.
Meanwhile, infielder Curtis Mead, who was injured in his Red Sox debut in July, also appeared to take a step forward on Tuesday. According to Cotillo, Mead, at one point during Crochet's session, appeared to be getting ready to step into the batter's box as well. Over the weekend, Mead began hitting off a tee and playing catch, per MLB.com.
There's no guarantee that Crochet or Mead will be ready in time for a likely best-of-three playoff series, but either could provide Boston with a huge boost. At their best, Crochet is one of baseball's best left-handed pitchers, while Mead hit 17 home runs before joining the Red Sox this season.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] The Garrett Crochet Bullpen Detail Red Sox Fans Should Be Watching Closely
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown

Crochet has been tossing bullpens for a few weeks at this point and hasn't suffered any setbacks. On Saturday, he tossed a bullpen at Polar Park and sat between 91and 92 miles per hour with his fastball and Triple-A WooSox pitching coach Dan DeLucia said he looked "great" and was "probably a tick above" expectations. item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday, Boston Red Sox star Garrett Crochet took his biggest step towards a late-season return yet.
Crochet has been tossing bullpens for a few weeks at this point and hasn't suffered any setbacks. On Saturday, he tossed a bullpen at Polar Park and sat between 91and 92 miles per hour with his fastball and Triple-A WooSox pitching coach Dan DeLucia said he looked "great" and was "probably a tick above" expectations. On Tuesday, he continued his progression and faced live hitters for the first time since May, which is a huge step in the path back to the majors.
Crochet faced off against Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela and topped out at 96 miles per hour in his 16-pitch outing. The fact that he hit 96 miles per hour in the outing was the biggest bright spot, to say the least.
After the outing, Crochet spoke to the media and said that if he can pitch like he did in the live bullpen, he can get outs for the team right now. He also acknowledged that he would feel bad to take the spot of someone on the roster in the playoffs.
Garrett Crochet Just Took His Biggest Step Yet Towards Return
"I would say the way that that live just went, that I could go get outs [in a game]," Crochet said, as transcribed by The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey.
" ... For me to take a spot on the roster, then someone would have to lose one, and I would feel bad doing that because this team's pitched their ass off the whole season," Crochet said.
Over the weekend, there were some in Red Sox Nation concerned when reports surfaced that Crochet was sitting at 91-92 MPH in his last bullpen. There really shouldn't have been concern there, though. Crochet wasn't facing live hitters and you're not going to see max velocity in an outing like that. So, seeing him not only facing live hitters, but getting to 96 MPH is a massive bright spot and is a clear sign he's trending in the right direction.
If Crochet does return this season, it's going to be in a relief role. Over the last few weeks, we've seen various positive updates, including him building up to the point of a 30-pitch up-and-down, and now facing live hitters just three days after his last bullpen. The Red Sox will begin their playoff run in exactly one week on Sep. 29, likely against the New York Yankees.
If Crochet bounces back well from his live bullpen, it will be very interesting to see what Boston does next. If Boston has Crochet throw on a three-day schedule again, that would make his next appearance be on Friday, or right around then. Then, Boston will begin the playoffs just a few days later on Tuesday, Sep. 29. If he bounces back well on Wednesday without any setback after the live bullpen, it's going to make a return in time for the playoffs very possible.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have been without ace Garrett Crochet since late April when he began dealing with a shoulder injury.
Fans have eagerly awaited the return of the 2025 AL Cy Young Award runner-up, and his comments after a live BP session on Tuesday indicated that his return may be very soon.
Crochet threw a 16-pitch live BP session on Tuesday, his first time facing live hitters since May. Despite the limited number of pitches, Crochet left the session feeling fairly confident about his ability to get major league hitters out.
“I felt like, with the way that went, I could go get outs," Crochet said, via Red Sox beat writer Chris Cotillo.
Boston would almost certainly like to see Crochet build up a little past 16 pitches, but his confidence and mindset are an encouraging sign.
Garrett Crochet says what happens next is up to Craig Breslow and Chad Tracy after a 16-pitch live BP against Ceddanne Rafaela in which he hit 96 mph.
“I felt like, with the way that went, I could go get outs.”
It is clear that Crochet won't be returning as a starter, so what exactly could his role in a postseason series look like?
The option that makes the most sense would appear to be Crochet returning as a high-leverage reliever in late-game situations. Boston has Aroldis Chapman as its closer, meaning Crochet could be an option for the seventh or eighth inning.
Whatever the case may be and whatever the role is, a returning Crochet for what will likely be an AL East showdown between the Red Sox and New York Yankees will give Boston an even better chance to get revenge from last year's Wild Card Series loss to the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
With just a few games remaining in the regular season, the chances of a Red Sox vs. Yankees matchup in the AL Wild Card round appear high.
If the Rays can officially clinch the AL East, and the Red Sox can pull away from the White Sox for the AL's No. 5 seed, Boston will be traveling to face New York in a best-of-three matchup.
So when Aaron Boone announced the latest on Aaron Judge's injury status on Tuesday, it carried massive implications for the Red Sox as they begin looking toward the postseason.
Here's the latest on Judge and what it could mean for the Red Sox.
How Yankees' Aaron Judge Injury Update Affects Red Sox
On Tuesday, Boone told reporters that Judge, who was recently played on the 10-day IL with a calf strain just days after his return from a significant injury, is dealing with a "moderate grade" strain.
However, more significantly, Boone said the Yankees aren't preparing for Judge to be ready for the start of the postseason after he had a PPP injection on Monday.
"We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said, per Bryan Hoch.
While Judge's status for a likely wild-card matchup won't become official until early next week, when the Yankees would have to finalize their roster for a series, it's looking unlikely that he will be healthy in time.
For the Red Sox, no Judge would change the dynamic of attacking the Yankees' lineup. While Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger remain power threats themselves, the presence of the three-time AL MVP boosts New York's offense to an elite status. Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle — likely to pitch for Boston in a best-of-three series — wouldn't have to worry about the threat of Judge's bat breaking a game open in one swing.
Red Sox vs. Yankees is not yet official, and neither is Judge's status for the postseason. But as of Tuesday, all indications are that New York will have to host Boston without its superstar outfielder.

item.title: [nbcsports.com] Eli White undergoes successful foot surgery
item.dc:creator: Matthew Pouliot; Eli White
item.description:
Eli White had a successful Lisfranc repair surgery Tuesday, the Red Sox announced.
White, 32, tore a ligament in his foot while getting stuck in Fenway’s center field fencing a couple of weeks ago. He hit .246/.289/.398 in 204 plate appearances for the Braves and Red Sox this season. The Red Sox could keep him as a bench guy for $1.5 million or so next year or set him free this winter.

item.title: [heavy.com] Red Sox Manager Reveals Big Update on Garrett Crochet Amid Return
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: The Boston Red Sox were able to clinch a postseason spot, giving them a chance to go after a World Series title this year. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox were able to clinch a postseason spot, giving them a chance to go after a World Series title this year.
But the Red Sox may be getting back a crucial reinforcement to their pitching staff very soon. Ace left-hander Garrett Crochet has been out since April due to left shoulder inflammation, but he has been progressing well.
Crochet has been trying to return for the playoffs as a reliever for this team, and he may be in line to do so. The left-hander recently threw to hitters, looking great from this long injury recovery.
Will Garrett Crochet Return For Red Sox in Playoffs?
Assuming that Crochet continues to not feel any issues after this latest live batting practice outing, he could make his return soon. Red Sox manager Chad Tracy revealed the latest behind Crochet, giving an update on the injured ace.
“I think it just depends on how he feels coming out of it, how much volume we give him,” said Tracy. “So it’s hard to say. I know it’s not a great answer, but it’s just really how it is. How does he feel after each step? So when he does that, how does he feel? And then determine from there. Do we give him more hitters or do we want to put him in a game? It’s hard to say until you know how he feels.”
Tracy will see how the ace feels before making any other decision regarding his injury, giving him time to heal. But the Red Sox have been patiently waiting for Crochet to get back on the mound following his injury back in April.
Boston would love nothing more than to get Crochet back for the playoffs, and he could be a true weapon out of the bullpen. While the team doesn’t have time to ramp him back up as a starter, having an ace coming in as a reliever could offer the Red Sox some sort of advantage.
Garrett Crochet Opens Up on Injury
Following a 16-pitch live batting practice outing against Ceddanne Rafaela, Crochet revealed the next steps in the injury process. The left-hander said that whatever happens is up to the organization, but that he feels good about where he is.
“I felt like, with the way that went, I could go get outs,” Crochet said.
Garrett Crochet says what happens next is up to Craig Breslow and Chad Tracy after a 16-pitch live BP against Ceddanne Rafaela in which he hit 96 mph.
“I felt like, with the way that went, I could go get outs.”
— Chris Cotillo (@ChrisCotillo) September 22, 2026
If Crochet can return in time, the Red Sox would want him to take part in the final homestand. This would give him a chance to ramp things up before the playoffs and avoid his first outing in a crucial postseason moment.
But the veteran left-hander will have to hit some target points for the team before that can happen. Crochet only appeared in six games for Boston this season, posting a 6.30 ERA during this time.

item.title: [whec.com] Tuesday's MLB clinching scenarios: Rays can lock up AL East, while Cubs and Padres seek wild cards
item.dc:creator: DAVID BRANDT The Associated Press outputDateTimeDetails; 1

item.content:encoded:
Tuesday’s MLB clinching scenarios: Rays can lock up AL East, while Cubs and Padres seek wild cards
Major League Baseball’s postseason is rapidly approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game’s biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they’ll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is rolling even though four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani’s health is a concern.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves have also clinched spots in the postseason. Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, a three-time AL MVP, is dealing with a right calf strain that will likely keep him out through at least the Wild Card Series.
While the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here’s some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
Here’s who can clinch a playoff spot Tuesday
The Rays can clinch the AL East and No. 1 seed in the American League with a win in either game of their doubleheader against the Yankees.
Over in the National League, the Cubs can earn their spot in the postseason by beating the Marlins or if the D-backs lose to the Rockies. The Padres can also clinch if they beat the Dodgers and the D-backs lose to the Rockies.
The Brewers can earn a bye through the Wild Card Series and home-field advantage in the NLDS by beating the Phillies or if the Braves lose to the Reds.
AL race is murky while NL is more defined
There’s quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Cleveland Guardians (81-75) have a narrow advantage over the Chicago White Sox (80-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-78) are just ahead of the Houston Astros (77-79) in the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) and Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but will almost certainly make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), who are four games back.
MVP races, stats to watch
MLB’s major awards probably won’t have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago’s Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston’s Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero has also had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has an outside shot at a Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .313 but his 40 homers are one behind Caminero and his 99 RBIs are nine back of Baltimore’s Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati’s Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit’s Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
What is the MLB playoff format?
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB’s postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 29. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
What is the MLB postseason schedule?
Wild Card Series: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
Who are the favorites to win the World Series?
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.

item.title: [heavy.com] Curtis Mead Injury Update is Surprise News From Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The Boston Red Sox thought they had made a solid early splash well ahead of the MLB trade deadline when they acquired Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals for lefty pitcher Connelly Early. Instead, Mead was injured in his first game playing for the Red Sox, and he hasn’t appeared in a game since. With the playoffs beginning next week, Mead has mostly run out of time to return, but there are starting to be hints that he could soon be back on the field. Curtis Mead Injury Update On Tuesday, f
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox thought they had made a solid early splash well ahead of the MLB trade deadline when they acquired Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals for lefty pitcher Connelly Early.
Instead, Mead was injured in his first game playing for the Red Sox, and he hasn’t appeared in a game since.
With the playoffs beginning next week, Mead has mostly run out of time to return, but there are starting to be hints that he could soon be back on the field.
Curtis Mead Injury Update
On Tuesday, for example, Mead was digging in to take an at bat against Garrett Crochet, the lefty ace who is also on his way back from injury.
Live at bats are a big step in a comeback, so this is quite encouraging:
Rafaela is in the box now and it looks like Curtis Mead is next, which is interesting.
— Chris Cotillo (@ChrisCotillo) September 22, 2026
It had actually been reported over the weekend that Mead had begun doing some work off a tee, which is an early step.
He’s coming back from a fractured left wrist, so it’ll be all about getting his hands and hitting mechanics to feel right.
Curtis Mead Stats
Mead was awesome for Washington this season before being traded.
He had played 87 games, and he had an .852 OPS in that time. He had doubled 17 times, hit a triple and left the yard with 17 home runs. Mead had 48 RBI and 49 runs for the Nats, and also had stolen six bases in eight attempts.
It was by far his most production in the major leagues. In 90 games in the 2025 season split between the Rays and White Sox, Mead had just three homers. In the two seasons prior to that, Mead had appeared in 52 games for the Rays and hit a total of two home runs.
This season, though, the shine he once had as a pretty promising prospect showed itself for Mead.
The Nationals didn’t have to trade Mead. He’s under club control through 2030.
Washington simply didn’t want to pass up the opportunity to get an arm like Early.
The Red Sox, on the flip side, wanted more right-handed hitting production out of the infield, where Mead can play multiple positions.
Mead will have future seasons to prove it to be a good trade for Boston, but it remains to be seen whether he’ll return in time this year to start making that case.
At least Mead seems to be taking steps in the right direction. Still just 25, the native of Australia would be eligible to impact the pennant race if the Red Sox want to activate him. Maybe if he looks good taking some live at bats, Mead will make a quality case for himself.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Announce Craig Breslow Decision Before Postseason

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox tied controversial chief baseball officer Craig Breslow's future to the Boston franchise through 2030 on Tuesday, extending his grip on baseball operations after a season that at one point looks like it would have cost him the job.
The move, announced alongside a three-year contract making interim skipper Chad Tracy the club's 49th manager, arrives five months after a coaching purge and a fan revolt threatened to end Breslow's tenure early.
Born in New Haven and raised in nearby Trumbull, Connecticut, Breslow grew up attending Congregation B'nai Israel in Bridgeport, where he had his bar mitzvah in 1993. His older sister's childhood cancer diagnosis, when Breslow was 12, pointed him toward medicine long before baseball made that detour permanent.
Red Sox Turbulence Under Breslow
Breslow retired as a player following a stint with the Cleveland franchise, then called the Indians, in 2017. He stated a new baseball career in the front office in 2019, when Theo Epstein brought him to the Chicago Cubs as director of strategic initiatives. He rose to assistant general manager and senior vice president of pitching before the Red Sox hired him as chief baseball officer in October 2023, replacing Chaim Bloom.
His tenure produced long-term extensions for core players such as Brayan Bello, Garrett Crochet and Roman Anthony — and no shortage of turbulence. The 2025 trade of Rafael Devers to the San Francisco Giants reportedly fractured his standing in the clubhouse, and ESPN's Jeff Passan reported Breslow's circle of trust had narrowed, with one loyalist warning that "turncoats" were plotting against him internally.
Criticism intensified in April 2026, when Breslow fired manager Alex Cora and six coaches following a 10-17 start. A plane towed a banner over Fenway Park demanding his firing, and Boston Globe columnist Dan Shaughnessy branded his player evaluations "horrendous."
Team president Sam Kennedy insisted that June that dismissing Breslow was "not even on the table", even as national voices called it nearly impossible to picture Breslow surviving the year.
The the turnaround happened. From a 32-46 low point, the club reeled off a 15-game win streak from July 3 to July 22 went 38-16 in July and August clinching their second straight postseason berth on Sunday.
"When you reach a certain level of conviction, you have to act," Breslow said of the gambles that defined his season, according to The Boston Globe's Alex Speier.
Kennedy cited that same conviction Tuesday in explaining the new deal.
"Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others," Kennedy said in a statement posted by the team — a verdict on Breslow's most scrutinized season yet.
Breslow's Path to Boston Red Sox Top Job
He captained Trumbull High School's baseball and soccer teams before enrolling at Yale, where he led the Ivy League with a 2.56 ERA as a senior and graduated in 2002 with a molecular biophysics and biochemistry degree. He deferred admission to NYU's medical school to chase a professional pitching carer, a gamble that later earned him The Wall Street Journal's "Smartest Man in Baseball" label and a No. 1 spot on The Sporting News' smartest athletes list.
The Milwaukee Brewers drafted him in the 26th round in 2002, and he debuted with the San Diego Padres in 2005. Breslow pitched 12 big league seasons for seven organizations, posting a 3.45 ERA over 576 appearances, with his sharpest stretch coming during with the Red Sox during Boston's 2013 title run, when he posted a 1.81 ERA and didn't allow an earned run in nine of 10 postseason outings. That championship made Breslow one of only four former Red Sox players to later run the club's baseball department.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Red Sox Announce Craig Breslow Decision Before Postseason appeared first on HEAVY.

item.dc:creator: Luis Mote Nava
item.description: A falta de una semana para que termine la temporada regular en la MLB, el panorama de playoffs comienza a definirse y con ello te presentamos aquellos peloteros mexicanos que ya aseguraron su clasificación a playoffs y quienes todavía están en la pelea por entrar a la postemporada. Mexicanos que ya aseguraron su pase a postemporada La presencia de peloteros mexicanos en las últimas ediciones de los playoffs ha sido constante y este año no será la excepción pues hasta ahorita se tiene confirmada
item.content:encoded:
A falta de una semana para que termine la temporada regular en la MLB, el panorama de playoffs comienza a definirse y con ello te presentamos aquellos peloteros mexicanos que ya aseguraron su clasificación a playoffs y quienes todavía están en la pelea por entrar a la postemporada.
Mexicanos que ya aseguraron su pase a postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos en las últimas ediciones de los playoffs ha sido constante y este año no será la excepción pues hasta ahorita se tiene confirmada la participación de cuatro peloteros mexicanos y dos con estatus todavía pendiente, ya que uno está en sucursales y el otro se encuentra en lista de lesionados.
PUBLICIDAD
A continuación, te presentamos la lista de jugadores nacionales que estarán en los playoffs:
Jonathan Aranda (Tampa Bay Rays)
Ha firmado su campaña más sólida y consagratoria en MLB. Con 149 juegos jugados, el infielder presume un promedio de bateo de .277, conectando 156 imparables, 22 cuadrangulares y remolcando 92 carreras, convirtiéndose en una pieza medular en el lineup de los Rays.
Jarren Durán (Boston Red Sox):
Se ha consolidado como un auténtico motor en los senderos y el jardín central. A lo largo de la temporada suma 20 jonrones, 69 carreras impulsadas y 19 bases robadas en 145 encuentros, destacando además por su velocidad con 5 triples.
PUBLICIDAD
Joey Ortiz (Milwaukee Brewers):
Ha sido una de las grandes revelaciones del año tras su llegada a Milwaukee, aportando una defensa de élite en el cuadro y un bateo sumamente oportuno que ayudó a los Brewers a amarrar temprano su boleto a octubre.
Patrick Sandoval (Boston Red Sox):
El lanzador que representó a México en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol regresó esta temporada tras un periodo largo fuera de las canchas y ha tenido altibajos con los Boston Red Sox con una efectividad de 5.15 y un récord de 1-7.
Manuel Rodríguez (Tampa Bay Rays):
El lanzador yucateco venía sumando valiosos relevos con efectividad de 3.86 y 8 ponches en el bullpen de Tampa Bay en los cuatro juegos que disputó.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, Manuel Rodríguez se encuentra actualmente en la lista de lesionados (IL) de 15 días debido a una distensión en la espalda baja (low back strain), por lo que el cuerpo técnico espera su evolución para ver si podrá estar listo en las primeras rondas de los playoffs.
Alek Thomas (Oklahoma City Comets):
Después de haber sido cambiado desde los Arizona Diamondbacks a inicios de año, el jardinero Alek Thomas se encuentra actualmente en las sucursales de Los Angeles Dodgers
Aunque tuvo una breve participación de 7 juegos con el primer equipo de los Dodgers bateando para .211, la tremenda profundidad del roster angelino ha hecho que se mantenga buscando ritmo en el sistema de ligas menores, a la espera de un llamado que lo devuelva al roster de postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
Peloteros mexicanos todavía buscan entrar a la postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos aumentará conforme avance la semana, con varios representantes en equipos que continúan en competencia por buscar entrar a los playoffs.
Toronto Blue Jays cuenta con Alejandro Kirk, Tibo Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Luis Urías. Por su parte, Randy Arozarena y Andrés Muñoz forman parte de los Seattle Mariners.
Isaac Paredes representa a los Houston Astros, mientras Javier Assad se encuentra con los Chicago Cubs. Alejandro Osuna integra el roster de los Texas Rangers.
Taijuan Walker juega con los Philadelphia Phillies y Jeremiah Estrada pertenece a los San Diego Padres.
Cada uno luchará hasta el último segundo por entrar a la postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox just buried a Craig Breslow show of faith in Chad Tracy news drop
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: After a rollercoaster of a season which included a brutal start, sudden managerial firings, historic win streaks and a playoff clinch, the Boston Red Sox have extended the man who brought it all together. Boston has removed Chad Tracy's "interim" tag and made him their manager, first reported by Christopher Smith of MassLive. Tracy and the Red Sox have agreed to a three-year contract with a club option in 2030, per Smith. His salary has not yet been reported. Tracy was Boston's Triple-A manager
item.content:encoded:
After a rollercoaster of a season which included a brutal start, sudden managerial firings, historic win streaks and a playoff clinch, the Boston Red Sox have extended the man who brought it all together. Boston has removed Chad Tracy's "interim" tag and made him their manager, first reported by Christopher Smith of MassLive.
Tracy and the Red Sox have agreed to a three-year contract with a club option in 2030, per Smith. His salary has not yet been reported.
Tracy was Boston's Triple-A manager on April 25, the day Alex Cora and six other members of his coaching staff were fired. The Red Sox then flew him out to Baltimore to take over in a whirlwind and a leap of faith, and it worked. He'll be the 49th manager in Red Sox franchise history (subscription required).
The Red Sox had a 10-17 record on the day of Tracy's promotion and he managed the club to two games below .500 by July 12, the start of the All-Star break. Boston's historic 15-game winning streak had already begun by then — it rallied to sweep the New York Yankees in four games two weeks before, lost a series to the Washington Nationals, and it was all winning from there.
Red Sox name Chad Tracy manager through 2029, exercised club options to keep Craig Breslow CBO through 2030
Tracy had long been revered as the manager of the WooSox and it didn't take long for Red Sox fans to become equally endeared to him. His direct, but friendly communication style offered a stark contrast to other leaders in the organization. He had preexisting relationships with many of the organization's young players from their time in Triple-A and from rehab assignments, and it showed. After the Red Sox's historic July and August spell, Tracy's promotion seemed almost inevitable, and rightfully so.
Within the Tracy contract announcement, the Red Sox also included another contract update. The Red Sox have exercised the 2029-30 club options on Craig Breslow's contract, essentially extending him for another two years.
This is quite a sign of trust from Boston. Breslow's tenure started with some massive moves like the Garrett Crochet trade, and the Red Sox made the playoffs for the first time in three seasons with him at the helm. But his communication style has been criticized, it's led to massive trades of players who were supposed to be fixtiures of the organization for years to come, and front office leaks have marred his public image.
But Breslow has loosened up a bit since the beginning of the season. He's been pictured around the players more often and has been cracking jokes on his radio appearances.
There's also no denying that he had a great 2025-26 offseason. Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Ranger Suarez and Caleb Durbin, all acquired by Breslow over the offseason, are all major parts of the Red Sox's success.
Cora had been Boston's manager for eight seasons and many Red Sox fans couldn't stand Breslow at the beginning of June. Things can change quickly in baseball.

item.content:encoded:
El gran repunte de los Red Sox durante la segunda mitad de la temporada ya tiene recompensa. Boston retiró este martes el interinato de Chad Tracy y lo nombró oficialmente como el mánager número 49 en la historia de la franquicia.
Tracy, de 41 años, firmó un contrato por tres temporadas que lo mantendrá en el cargo hasta 2029, además de incluir una opción del club para 2030.
El anuncio llegó apenas dos días después de que Boston asegurara un lugar de comodín para los playoffs.
Tracy asumió el puesto en abril, luego de que los Red Sox despidieran a Alex Cora tras un inicio de 10-17.
Desde entonces, el equipo cambió por completo el rumbo y consiguió una marca de 74-55 bajo las órdenes de Tracy.
Durante ese periodo, Boston hiló 15 victorias consecutivas, una racha que igualó el récord de la franquicia establecido en 1946.
Además, entre el 3 de julio y el 7 de agosto, los Red Sox tuvieron marca de 27-3, un porcentaje de .900 que representó el mejor tramo de 30 juegos en la historia del equipo.
El cambio fue todavía más notable si se toma en cuenta que el 24 de junio Boston tenía récord de 32-46 y estaba a 15 juegos y medio del liderato del Este de la Liga Americana.
También ratifican a Craig Breslow
La organización también confirmó la continuidad de Craig Breslow, director de operaciones de béisbol, al ejercer sus opciones para las temporadas 2029 y 2030.
Breslow, de 46 años, llegó al puesto en octubre de 2023. Antes fue jugador de los Red Sox y formó parte del equipo campeón de la Serie Mundial de 2013.
Es apenas el cuarto exjugador de Boston que encabeza las operaciones de béisbol de la franquicia.
Durante sus tres temporadas al frente, los Red Sox acumularon una marca de 254-226, con porcentaje de .529, la tercera mejor de la Liga Americana.
Antes de llegar a las Grandes Ligas, Tracy dirigió durante cuatro temporadas completas a los Worcester WooSox, la sucursal Triple-A de los Red Sox, desde 2022.
En cada una de esas campañas consiguió un récord ganador.
Su experiencia como mánager también incluye siete años dentro del sistema de ligas menores de los Angelinos de Los Ángeles.
Como jugador, Tracy fue seleccionado en la tercera ronda del draft de 2006 por los Rangers de Texas, procedente de la Universidad de Pepperdine.
Jugó ocho temporadas profesionales, entre 2006 y 2013, dentro de las organizaciones de los Rangers, los Rockies de Colorado y los Reales de Kansas City.
El presidente y director ejecutivo de los Red Sox, Sam Kennedy, destacó el trabajo realizado por Breslow y Tracy durante el proceso de reconstrucción del equipo.
Sobre Breslow, señaló que durante los últimos tres años aportó claridad, disciplina y convicción para construir la operación de béisbol.
Respecto a Tracy, Kennedy destacó que asumió una situación complicada con poco tiempo de preparación y rápidamente ganó la confianza dentro del equipo.

item.title: [Telediario] Red Sox nombra a Chad Tracy mánager permanente y renueva a Breslow

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox ratifica a Chad Tracy como mánager y asegura a Craig Breslow
La directiva del equipo bostoniano retiró el interinato de Chad Tracy firmándolo hasta 2029 tras amarrar su boleto de comodín a los playoffs.
Los Boston Red Sox disputarán la Postemporada de las Grandes Ligas tras firmar un regreso espectacular en la segunda mitad de la campaña regular, y la directiva no tardó en recompensar a los dos grandes arquitectos del resurgimiento en las Mayores.
Este martes, la franquicia anunció de manera oficial la remoción del interinato del timonel Chad Tracy para nombrarlo el mánager número 49 en la historia de la organización, otorgándole un contrato por tres temporadas que lo vincula hasta el final de la campaña 2029 con una opción del club para 2030.
A la par, el equipo anunció la extensión del contrato del presidente de operaciones de beisbol, Craig Breslow, al ejercer sus opciones institucionales para 2029 y 2030.
¿Cómo logró Chad Tracy la ratificación como mánager de Red Sox?
La consolidación de Tracy, de 41 años de edad, llega apenas dos días después de que Boston asegurara uno de los boletos de comodín a la fiesta grande de la Liga Americana.
El estratega tomó las riendas del vestidor en el mes de abril de manera intempestiva tras el cese de Alex Cora, quien dejó el cargo luego de un convulso arranque de temporada con marca de 10-17.
Desde su nombramiento, Tracy guió a los Patirrojos a un récord de 74-55, incluyendo una racha de 15 victorias consecutivas que igualó la marca histórica de la franquicia impuesta en 1946.
Asimismo, la novena bostoniana registró una marca de 27-3 entre el 3 de julio y el 7 de agosto, firmando el mejor lapso de 30 encuentros en toda la historia de la organización para levantar un barco que el 24 de junio marchaba a 15.5 juegos de distancia en la División Este.
El respaldo de la directiva y la trayectoria de Craig Breslow
A través de un comunicado institucional, el presidente y CEO de los Red Sox, Sam Kennedy, resaltó la labor realizada por el cuerpo técnico y la plana mayor para revertir el panorama deportivo.
"En los últimos tres años, hemos visto a Craig aportar claridad, disciplina y convicción al trabajo de construir nuestras operaciones de beisbol. Se le pidió a Chad asumir una situación difícil con muy poco margen de aviso, pero la confianza que inspiró de inmediato a nivel de Grandes Ligas se la ganó tras años de trabajo en nuestra organización. Lo que este equipo ha logrado durante los últimos meses ha sido histórico", señaló el directivo.
Breslow, de 46 años y campeón de la Serie Mundial de 2013 con Boston como lanzador, asumió el cargo ejecutivo en octubre de 2023.
Durante sus tres campañas al frente del proyecto deportivo, los Red Sox registran una marca global de 254-226 (.529), ostentando el tercer mejor récord de toda la Liga Americana.

item.content:encoded:
El tercera base de los Cachorros de Chicago, Alex Bregman, sufrió múltiples fracturas faciales tras ser golpeado por un foul ball el domingo pasado, pero no requerirá cirugía y mantiene la esperanza de regresar a tiempo para los playoffs de las Grandes Ligas.
El incidente ocurrió en el cuarto inning del triunfo 9-1 de Chicago sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati. Michael Busch, bateador zurdo de los Cubs, cortó el swing ante un pitcheo de Luis Mey y la pelota rebotó en el terreno e impactó a Bregman, que se encontraba en el círculo de espera. El pelotero cubrió su rostro, salió del campo con sangrado y fue trasladado a un hospital para radiografías y tomografía.
TAMBIÉN TE PUEDE INTERESAR: ¡Renovado! Keyonte George se queda con Utah Jazz
Bregman presentó fracturas en el lado izquierdo del rostro, principalmente en el pómulo debajo del ojo. El ojo izquierdo quedó muy hinchado. El manager Craig Counsell describió el golpe como “un accidente terrible” y destacó que primero importaba el bienestar del jugador.
Bregman publicó en Instagram una foto de su rostro inflamado con el mensaje: “Thanks for all the messages yall. I’ll be back.” Al día siguiente, ya de regreso en Chicago, compartió otra imagen con la leyenda “Back in Chicago”.
Impacto para los Cubs rumbo a octubre
Bregman, de 32 años, firmó un contrato de cinco años y 175 millones de dólares con Chicago para 2026. Esta temporada registra .262 de average, 26 jonrones, 89 impulsadas y 5.2 WAR. En la segunda mitad ha estado especialmente caliente, con línea de .296/.378/.600.
Los Cubs están en la pelea por el primer wild card de la Liga Nacional, empatados o cerca de Padres y Filis con seis juegos por disputar. Se espera que Bregman vaya a la lista de lesionados de 10 días y se pierda el tramo final de la temporada regular en las series ante Marlins y Red Sox. Los playoffs comienzan el 29 de septiembre.
En su ausencia, Matt Shaw y el novato Pedro Ramírez podrían cubrir la tercera base. La visión del jugador se considera en buen estado, según fuentes cercanas al equipo. El propio Bregman, conocido por su intensidad, ha dejado claro que quiere volver lo antes posible. El club prioriza su recuperación y evaluará día a día si puede estar listo para la postemporada.

item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Gran preocupación por Aaron Judge: “Existe una fuerte posibilidad de que no vuelva a jugar esta temporada”
- MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”
En este momento, los Chicago Cubs necesitan que todos aporten al máximo para el tramo final de la temporada regular. El título de la división está fuera de alcance, pero el primer puesto en la carrera por el comodín de la Liga Nacional sigue en juego. Lamentablemente, el equipo perdió a uno de sus mejores jugadores para esta recta final el pasado fin de semana.
Alex Bregman sufrió una lesión terrible, y ocurrió de la manera más desafortunada posible. Mientras esperaba su turno en el círculo de espera (*on-deck circle*), Bregman recibió un golpe en la cara por una bola de foul bateada por un compañero de equipo. Sufrió múltiples fracturas faciales, y la imagen que se vio tras el incidente fue impactante.
La lesión de Bregman ha llevado a muchos aficionados a plantearse un par de cosas. En primer lugar, a muchos les sorprende que este tipo de incidentes no ocurran con más frecuencia. El margen de error es mínimo cuando los bateadores que esperan su turno se colocan tan cerca de la caja de bateo. Hemos visto situaciones similares antes, pero resulta algo sorprendente que no sean más habituales.
Trevor Plouffe pide a la MLB que proteja a los bateadores que esperan su turno en el futuro
Sin embargo, aunque no suceda tan a menudo como cabría suponer, incluso exjugadores de la MLB como Trevor Plouffe creen que ha llegado el momento de que el béisbol implemente cambios para evitar este tipo de lesiones en el futuro. Plouffe expresó su opinión el lunes en el podcast "Talkin’ Baseball".
"Hace falta que ocurra algo así. Por ejemplo, si esto hubiera pasado en los playoffs y, de repente, Alex Bregman ya no pudiera jugar, eso sacudiría a la gente y provocaría una reacción. Quizás esto ya sea lo suficientemente grave. ¿Qué tal si ponemos una red protectora o algo parecido?"
Simplemente no hay razón para que un jugador esté tan cerca cuando no está bateando activamente. Es cierto que estar tan cerca permite al bateador que espera su turno conocer mejor al lanzador que está en el montículo, pero eso también pueden hacerlo desde el dugout o contando con mayor protección a su alrededor.

item.content:encoded:
Los Boston Red Sox tomaron una decisión importante de cara a su futuro y anunciaron que Chad Tracy deja de ser manager interino para convertirse oficialmente en el entrenador del equipo. El acuerdo tendrá vigencia hasta la temporada 2029.
La organización también ejerció las opciones contractuales de Craig Breslow para las campañas 2029 y 2030, por lo que ambos continuarán al frente del proyecto de Boston durante los próximos años.
Chad Tracy recibe la confianza de Boston
Tracy asumió el puesto el pasado 26 de abril, cuando reemplazó a Alex Cora después de que los Red Sox comenzaran la campaña con marca de 10-17. Desde entonces, el equipo protagonizó una importante recuperación.
Bajo su dirección, Boston consiguió asegurar un lugar en los playoffs de la Liga Americana y llegó a registrar una impresionante marca de 27-3 entre el 3 de julio y el 7 de agosto, el mejor periodo de 30 partidos en la historia de la franquicia.
El trabajo de Tracy permitió que los Red Sox pasaran de un complicado inicio de temporada a conseguir su boleto a la postemporada. El equipo anunció que será el manager número 49 en la historia de la organización.
Craig Breslow también continuará en Boston
La continuidad no será exclusiva de Tracy, pues los Red Sox también decidieron mantener a Craig Breslow como Chief Baseball Officer. La organización ejerció sus opciones contractuales correspondientes a 2029 y 2030.
Breslow asumió ese cargo en octubre de 2023 y durante su gestión Boston ha construido un proyecto que ahora tendrá continuidad con Tracy en el dugout. Los términos económicos de ambos acuerdos no fueron revelados.
Con estas decisiones, los Red Sox aseguran la continuidad de dos de las figuras que han encabezado la transformación del equipo durante 2026. Tracy y Breslow ahora tendrán la responsabilidad de preparar a Boston para las próximas temporadas.

Los Red Sox eliminan la etiqueta de interino a su dirigente Chad Tracy
Lo nombran como el 49no mánager de la franquicia tras una remontada histórica.
PUBLICIDAD
Los Red Sox de Boston han eliminado la etiqueta de interino y han nombrado a Chad Tracy como el 49no mánager en la historia del equipo.
El equipo anunció el nombramiento definitivo este martes, firmando a Tracy un contrato de tres años que se extenderá hasta la temporada 2029, con una opción del club para 2030. Los Red Sox también anunciaron que han ejercido las opciones para 2029 y 2030 sobre el director de operaciones de béisbol, Craig Breslow.
El ascenso de Tracy, de 41 años, se produce después de que los Red Sox aseguraran el domingo un puesto de comodín (wild card) para los playoffs. Tracy asumió el cargo en abril, tras el despido del anterior mánager, Alex Cora, después de un inicio de temporada con un balance de 10 victorias y 17 derrotas.
Desde entonces, Tracy ha guiado a los Red Sox a un registro de 74-55, incluyendo una racha de 15 victorias consecutivas que igualó el récord de la franquicia. Se trata de una remontada notable para un equipo que, el 24 de junio, presentaba un récord de 32-46 y se encontraba a 15 juegos y medio de distancia en la lucha por el liderato de la División Este de la Liga Americana.

The Boston Red Sox officially named Chad Tracy as the 49th manager in franchise history. The team announced Tuesday it will be removing the interim tag off Tracy, who helped turn the season around and lead the Red Sox to the postseason after the
In addition, the Red Sox announced that they have exercised the 2029 and 2030 contract options on Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow.
Tracy received the interim manager title in April. Cora was to the season.
After Cora's firing, the Red Sox posted a 74-55 record, good for second best in the American League and fifth best in MLB during that span. That includes the best 30-game stretch in Red Sox history. Boston went 27-3 from July 3 through Aug. 7, spurred by a 15-game winning streak.
Boston clinched a playoff spot on Sunday and will likely play the New York Yankees in the Wild Card round.
Prior to taking over in Boston, Tracy had been manager of the Triple-A Worcester Red Sox since 2021.
Breslow was hired in October 2023 and has spent three seasons in his current position. Now, his contract has been extended through 2030.
"What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic," Red Sox President and CEO Sam Kennedy said in a statement. "Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others. Craig and Chad have demonstrated all of those qualities, and they have earned our confidence in leading us forward."

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Red Sox Hit Jackpot by Locking Up Chad Tracy, Craig Breslow Now
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: There will not be institutional turnover this upcoming offseason for the Boston Red Sox. In April, the Red Sox fired former manager Alex Cora, along with a handful of coaches. At the time, Boston's season was sputtering out of control and the Red Sox turned the reins over to Chad Tracy as the club's interim manager and the rest is history. item.content:encoded:
There will not be institutional turnover this upcoming offseason for the Boston Red Sox.
In April, the Red Sox fired former manager Alex Cora, along with a handful of coaches. At the time, Boston's season was sputtering out of control and the Red Sox turned the reins over to Chad Tracy as the club's interim manager and the rest is history. The first few months weren't great and it seemed like everyone's seat was getting hotter and hotter. But Boston stayed the course and turned its season around. The Red Sox met the moment and already have put themselves in the record books as the team with the worst 75-game start (31-44) by a team to make the playoffs in MLB history.
Now, the interim tag is coming off Tracy and the Red Sox don't need to think about it or have the decision hang over the club throughout the rest of the season. Boston announced on Tuesday that it has signed Tracy to a three-year deal with a 2030 club option. That's not all, though. Boston also announced that chief baseball officer Craig Breslow has had his 2029 and 2030 club options exercised as well.
"The Red Sox today announced that they have exercised the club’s 2029 and 2030 contract options on Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow and named Chad Tracy the team’s 49th manager in club history, agreeing to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season with a club option in 2030," the Red Sox announced.
The Red Sox Got It Right
Boston got it right.
With Tracy leading the charge, the Red Sox have gone 74-55. Boston tied its franchise record for the longest winning streak in team history at 15 back in July. That's not all, though. Boston also went on the best 35-game stretch in franchise history throughout the summer when it went 30-5, which was the 26th time in the World Series Era (1903-present) that a team was able to reach this feat in general.
Tracy came into the picture and picked up a team that was dealing with injuries all over the place and led the way with a steady hand. The team loves him. The fans love him. And now, he's not going anywhere. The timing couldn't be better as well with the postseason a week away from kicking off. The decision has been made and it doesn't have to linger or hang over the team any longer. The full focus can be on the task at hand: winning games and making a run.
The same can be said about Breslow, and this is also the right call. As Boston struggled early in the summer, his job security certainly was talked about. Boston has shown in recent memory that it isn't afraid to move on from a decision-maker at the top of the baseball operations department. The Red Sox were struggling and it seemed like Breslow would fall victim to that in the offseason.
Then, the Red Sox transformed their season and now is in a much different place. Boston is getting healthier and went out and added pieces, including Adley Rutschman. We're starting to see how good this roster that Breslow built can be. Now, he has more job security. Again, this is the right call. It took a while for the baseball world to truly see it, but Breslow built a winner that has a real shot at winning the World Series this season.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox today announced that they have exercised the club’s 2029 and 2030 contract options on Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow and named Chad Tracy the team’s 49th manager in club history, agreeing to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season with a club option in 2030.
“Craig and Chad are two exceptionally talented leaders who have earned these opportunities in very different ways,” said Red Sox President & CEO Sam Kennedy. “Over the last three years, we have watched Craig bring clarity, discipline, and conviction to the work of building our baseball operation. Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization. What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic. Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others. Craig and Chad have demonstrated all of those qualities, and they have earned our confidence in leading us forward.”
Breslow, 46, was hired as Chief Baseball Officer on October 25, 2023. A 2013 World Series champion with Boston, Breslow is only the fourth former Red Sox player to lead the club’s baseball operations efforts, the first since Haywood Sullivan served as General Manager from 1978-83. During his three seasons in his current role, the Red Sox have gone 254-226 (.529), the third-best record in the American League and ninth best in the Majors.
Prior to his 2023 hiring, Breslow spent the previous five seasons in the Chicago Cubs organization, most recently as Assistant General Manager/Senior Vice President, Pitching in 2023. His front office career began in 2019 with the Cubs as Director of Strategic Initiatives, evaluating and implementing data-based processes throughout all facets of Baseball Operations while also supporting the pitching infrastructure in the farm system. In 2020 he was named Director of Pitching/Special Assistant to the President and General Manager, then spent the 2021-22 seasons as Assistant General Manager/Vice President, Pitching.
Tracy, 41, made his Major League debut as Interim Manager on April 26. After entering that day tied for the American League’s second-worst record (10-17, .370), the Red Sox’ 74-55 (.574) record since is the second best in the AL and fifth best in the Majors.
Under Tracy, Boston posted the best 30-game span in franchise history, going 27-3 (.900) from July 3 through August 7. That stretch included a club-record-tying 15-game winning streak from July 3 through July 22-G1, a streak matched only by the 1946 Red Sox. Boston’s 21-4 (.840) record during July marked the club’s best winning percentage ever in a calendar month (minimum 20 games) and the third-best record of any Major League club during July.
A native of Illinois, Tracy earned his 499th career minor league managerial win on April 25, one day before being named Boston’s interim manager. He had served as Triple-A Worcester’s manager since 2022, leading the WooSox to a winning record in each of his four full seasons as manager (2022-25). Tracy spent the previous seven seasons (2015-21) in the Los Angeles Angels system, including three as a minor league manager with Low-A Burlington (2015) and High-A Inland Empire (2016-17). He served as the Angels’ minor league field coordinator from 2018-21.
Selected by the Texas Rangers in the third round of the 2006 First-Year Player Draft out of Pepperdine University, Tracy played eight professional seasons (2006-13) in the Rangers, Colorado Rockies, and Kansas City Royals organizations. While at Pepperdine (2004-06), he earned West Coast Conference Player of the Year and First-Team All-Conference honors in 2005.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have scored 2.82 runs per game across their last 11 outings. The lineup is collectively batting .210 and posting a .621 OPS in that span. Wilyer Abreu, Adley Rutschman, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Nick Sogard have all gone cold at the wrong time.
With the Wild Card Series beginning September 29, the Red Sox need their bats to wake up before October arrives.
The cavalry is coming. And the timing could not be better.
The Latest on Rafaela
Ceddanne Rafaela is expected to return to the lineup on Tuesday when the Red Sox open a three-game series against the Guardians at Fenway Park.
The All-Star center fielder has been sidelined for 16 games since straining his right quadriceps.
Chad Tracy indicated over the weekend that Rafaela should come off the injured list for the homestand. The rotation is set up with Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez, a sequence that mirrors how the staff could be deployed in the Wild Card Series.
Getting Rafaela back before those games begin gives him a chance to find his timing and reintegrate into the lineup before the stakes get higher.
What Rafaela Brings Back
Rafaela's absence has been felt. On the season, he has produced 16 home runs, 70 RBIs, and a .282/.760 line. His combination of contact, power, and speed makes him one of the most complete players on the roster.
The defensive impact is equally significant. Rafaela's range in center field changes the way the pitching staff operates. Fly balls that fall for hits with other outfielders become outs when he is patrolling the middle of the outfield. His presence there tightens the entire defense.
The Red Sox have been using Jarren Duran and Nate Eaton to fill the void in center. Both have been serviceable, but neither provides the combination of offense and defense that Rafaela delivers on a daily basis.
The Red Sox Offense Needs a Spark
The numbers paint a clear picture of how badly the Red Sox have struggled at the plate.
Mickey Gasper is 4-for-25 over the recent stretch. Kiner-Falefa has managed just one hit in his last 20 at-bats. Sogard is 8-for-40. The lineup has lacked the consistent production that fueled the summer surge.
There have been bright spots. Roman Anthony broke out of a prolonged slump with a 5-for-13 weekend against the Rays that included two doubles and a homer. Trevor Story has been one of the hottest hitters on the roster since returning from the injured list, carrying a .338 average with an .869 OPS across 19 games.
Willson Contreras is also working his way back from a bruised right hand and could return this week. If both Contreras and Rafaela rejoin the lineup for the Guardians series, it would be the healthiest the Red Sox' batting order has looked in weeks.
Final Word for the Red Sox
The Red Sox have six games left before the playoffs begin.
Rafaela's return gives the lineup a jolt it needs. What he provides on both sides of the ball is invaluable for Boston.
Fenway awaits.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Ranger Suarez’s antics cement his perfect playoff mentality after Red Sox clinch
item.dc:creator: Brian Burrows
item.description: Ranger Suarez is back to having fun after clinching the playoffs. Despite losing on Sunday, the Boston Red Sox clinched their spot in the postseason due to other teams' losses. item.content:encoded:
Ranger Suarez is back to having fun after clinching the playoffs. Despite losing on Sunday, the Boston Red Sox clinched their spot in the postseason due to other teams' losses. The Sox took a team picture on the field at Tropicana Field before heading into the clubhouse for the usual champagne showers and beer.
In the team photo, Suarez clearly sticks out. Standing right in the middle, the lefty starter had bright red shorts pulled up well above his waist, and his celebratory shirt tucked in. He was also the only player in the picture with his goggles already covering his eyes. Suarez was known as a fun celebration guy with the Philadelphia Phillies, and it was something the fans there loved about him; Red Sox Nation was just waiting to see in Boston.
While Suarez is all fun and games with good spirits during a celebration, he does a complete 180 once the playoffs start. He's been one of the best playoff pitchers ever. His 1.48 ERA is the sixth-lowest of all time among pitchers with at least 40 innings pitched in the playoffs.
The 31-year-old has pitched in each of the last four postseasons. In 2023, he allowed just two earned runs in 14 2/3 innings. In 2024, he allowed four earned runs in 18 2/3 innings. In 2024, he allowed no runs in 4 1/3 innings. In 2025, he allowed one earned run in five innings. In the regular season, the lefty has a career 8.4 K/9; in the playoffs, it's 9.3
Ranger Suarez's playoff pedigree should excite fans after last season's playoff rotation
His playoff excellence was part of the reason the Red Sox signed him. While Suarez has been a very solid regular-season pitcher, it was his success in the playoffs that really made him stand out in last season's free-agent pool. After Garrett Crochet, the Red Sox ended up relying on Brayan Bello and Connelly Early. The Sox knew they needed another playoff-tested arm for the postseason and made the splash signing of the lefty to do so.
The Red Sox now head into the 2026 playoffs with a projected Wild Card round rotation that will consist of Suarez, Sonny Gray, and Payton Tolle. While the exact order is yet to be determined, those three arms will instill much more confidence than the three who started the games last year.
Suarez likes to have his fun. He did so in Philly and is doing so again here in Boston. That doesn't mean that opponents should take him lightly. Come playoff time, Suarez turns it on and shuts down the other teams.

item.title: [nesn.com] Chad Tracy Delivers Powerful Message After Red Sox Clinch Playoff Spot | NESN
item.dc:creator: Rodney Knuppel
item.description: The Boston Red Sox did not clinch their postseason berth with a dramatic walk-off hit or a dominant performance from their pitching staff. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox did not clinch their postseason berth with a dramatic walk-off hit or a dominant performance from their pitching staff. They clinched after losing 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays and receiving help from Mike Yastrzemski and the Atlanta Braves.
Interim manager Chad Tracy did not care how the ticket was punched.
“When you work as hard as we have worked, I don’t think you care much how it gets done,” Tracy told reporters. “You just want to see your ticket get punched.”
That message perfectly captured Boston’s remarkable season. The Red Sox were 32-46 and appeared destined to spend the summer discussing trades, organizational changes and another disappointing finish. Instead, they became the first team in MLB history to finish above .500 and reach the playoffs after losing at least 46 of its first 78 games.
“They didn’t take no for an answer,” Tracy said.
Where It Started
Tracy inherited a 10-17 team when the Red Sox moved on from Alex Cora in April. There was no immediate transformation, and Boston’s season continued to drift for several weeks.
Eventually, everything changed. Boston swept four games from the New York Yankees at Fenway Park in late June and began one of the most impressive turnarounds in franchise history. Young players developed into meaningful contributors, the clubhouse remained together and the Red Sox kept finding ways to survive injuries.
The result is a second consecutive postseason appearance and another likely Wild Card Series against the Yankees. That matchup did not work out for Boston last October. The Red Sox won the opener behind Garrett Crochet but dropped the next two games in New York.
This year’s roster has traveled a much different road.
The Red Sox have played meaningful baseball for months because almost every loss threatened to undo the progress they had made. Players such as Roman Anthony, Payton Tolle and Connelly Early have grown up in that environment, while veterans including Trevor Story and Willson Contreras helped keep the clubhouse steady.
Getting Things Set Up
Now Boston has an opportunity to set its rotation, protect tired relievers and enter the postseason with more than a week to prepare. The final regular-season games still matter, especially with the Cleveland Guardians visiting Fenway Park. Boston can use the series to evaluate potential postseason matchups and determine which pitchers are best equipped for important October innings.
The celebration also strengthens Tracy’s case to remain manager beyond this season. Boston did not merely improve after he took control. The Red Sox completed a turnaround that had never been accomplished in major league history.
Tracy did not want credit Sunday. His message remained focused on the players who refused to allow a terrible start to define them. That approach may be one of the biggest reasons the Red Sox are still playing.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Decisions, decisions: Five questions for Red Sox to answer before playoffs
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: The Red Sox are officially headed back to the postseason, and by clinching a spot with more than a week to spare, the club now has the luxury of making all of its playoff preparations without stressing about the final six-game homestand.
